AI Search.description: Adds an AI search bar to the Jellyfin web client. Ask in natural language and get titles from your own library, personalized to your watch history. Also adds meaning-based matches inside Jellyfin's own native search, alongside title matches. Works with any OpenAI-compatible model, with a local or remote retrieval source.
AI Search.overview: AI natural-language search & recommendations from your own library.

versions.changelog:
For Jellyfin 12. Fixes for the three open issues.

- Newer OpenAI models work now. They refuse `max_tokens` and only accept the default temperature, so the plugin switches to `max_completion_tokens` and drops the temperature on its own, then remembers it for that model. You can also pick the field in the settings ("Reply length limit field"). Fixes #4.
- You can exclude libraries from AI Search. Ticked libraries are left out of the index, the AI search popup and the AI matches in Jellyfin's search, but still show up in Jellyfin's normal title search. Fixes #3.
- Building the index with a model that gives no embeddings (a reranker, or llama.cpp with `--pooling rank`) now stops with a clear message saying so, instead of a JSON error. If only a few titles fail, the build skips them and tells you how many. Fixes #2.

For Jellyfin 12. Searching is much faster, and you can now see where each result comes from.

What's new:
- Jellyfin's own search no longer waits for AI Search. Title results show up right away.
- AI matches get their own "AI Search" row under Jellyfin's results, with a short reason under each title.
- If a chat model is set up, it writes a one-line reason for each AI match a few seconds later.
- The plugin speaks French or English. By default it follows each user's Jellyfin language, or you can pick one in the settings.
- The search model is loaded as soon as you open the search page, so the first search isn't slow anymore.
- Repeated searches are almost instant, and the AI popup no longer loads your whole library before searching.

Fixes:
- The search page no longer jumps up or down while results and reasons load.
- Opening the AI search button no longer scrolls the page back to the top.
- The search history list in the popup is back to its normal layout.
- Remote search works again for searches made with an API key.
- Search log files no longer start with a byte-order mark.

TV and mobile apps still get AI matches mixed into Jellyfin's results, waiting at most 2 seconds for them. Jellyfin 10.11 servers stay on 1.1.1.0.

For Jellyfin 12. Jellyfin's own search now also finds titles by meaning, shown in the usual Movies, Shows and Episodes rows after the title matches. New options: turn it on or off, only use it for searches that look like a sentence, limit how many matches it adds, hide the AI search button completely (native search only), and keep a log of every search for a few days so an admin or API key can collect them.
Fixes the search button missing on new Docker installs.

One unified setup: a chat endpoint plus a local or remote retrieval source (replaces the old Direct/Platform modes). New: search without a language model, returning retrieval matches ranked by relevance with no per-result reasons. Embedding model is now a dropdown, and endpoints are configured per capability.
Show more now returns new titles instead of repeating the first results. Recommendations no longer come back empty on reasoning models.
Fixed a bug when choosing TV or Movies in platform mode.

versions.changelog: v1.8.3.36: Library jobs wait out a busy AI service (HTTP 429/503, following Retry-After) instead of failing the whole video on one rejected frame. The AI service now explains why an Intel/AMD GPU is not used (render group ID mismatch; see /doctor and /status) and runs OpenVINO on its CPU device instead of silently falling back; that part is in the AI service and needs the 1.8.3.36 Docker image. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.35: The player button no longer needs write access to Jellyfin's web folder. The plugin adds its script to index.html as Jellyfin serves the page, so Windows installs (NetworkService), the Debian package, snaps and read-only containers get the button in every browser tab. Behind a Jellyfin base URL, the Lanczos, Anime4K and WebGPU real-time engines load again. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.34: Real-time upscaling starts again in the web client. Since v1.8.3.31 it refused every video with "Video color metadata unavailable", because Jellyfin 10.9 and later no longer put the playing item in the page address; the player now reads the item from the video's stream or the web client's playback request and checks the version that plays. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.33: Redesigned in-player menu and settings page. SDR videos (DVD/SD rips, untagged 10-bit) are no longer refused as HDR in real time or in library jobs; HDR batch output keeps the model's detail; Server AI hides stale frames during outages and falls back to Lanczos when the server cannot keep up. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.32: Native Jellyfin 12 build on .NET 10, aligned plugin/test dependencies, updated CI and ABI-aware release validation. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.31: Remove the image-action rate limit from playback frames/chunks; forward busy/error responses and Retry-After; serialize player captures with abortable requests and backoff; guard driver upscaling and object masking; enforce measured Auto-mode performance; reject invalid model categories and unsupported HDR; fail library jobs on AI errors without local resize/original-frame substitution; enforce nonempty passing TRX and publish-only runtime packaging. Target-server acceptance was explicitly waived by the owner; GPU, live-player and HDR target-hardware behavior remain unverified.

v1.8.3.30: notifications stack instead of piling up - issue #77, 'if you hit a toggle in quick succession, the notifications at the lower right side of the screen will simply pile on top of each other'. They did, literally: every notification was its own position:fixed element anchored to the same corner, so two of them resolved to the identical coordinates and the second covered the first. Measured in a browser against the real CSS - three toasts all reported top 1185 / bottom 1226; after the fix 1185, 1136, 1087 with no overlap. They are flow children of one fixed host now and the host does the stacking, column-reverse so the newest sits nearest the corner. Two things beyond the literal report, both aimed at what 'quick succession' actually produces: a repeated toggle emits the SAME text over and over, so an identical message already on screen has its timer restarted instead of being cloned (firing 'Settings saved!' five times leaves one), and the stack is capped at four so holding a control down cannot fill the viewport. THE PLUGIN HAD THREE COPIES of this code, each with the same defect - the config page (reported), the player overlay and the quick menu - and all three are fixed, because patching only the reported surface is how the same bug gets filed twice. sidebar-upscaler.js was already correct (it defers to Jellyfin's own toast module) and a test now keeps it that way. Verified by measurement, not by reading: a browser harness built from the real CSS and the real showToast confirmed stacking, de-duplication and the cap, and re-applying the old position:fixed rule reproduced the exact overlap from the screenshot. Eleven regression tests; five reintroduced defects are each caught. 375 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.29: the error message now says what went wrong. Testing v1.8.3.28 live showed the last piece of the same problem - a failed Load Detection Model printed one generic sentence regardless of cause, because the handler read err.responseText (an XHR field) while Jellyfin 10.11's client is fetch-based. Checked against the running server rather than assumed: the rejection is [object Response], err.text IS a function, err.responseText does not exist, status 404 - so JSON.parse(undefined) threw on every failure and the fallback was the only thing anyone saw, while the body carried exactly what was needed ('... is not on disk. Import or upload a detection model first'). That reaches the status line now. The same run confirmed the v1.8.3.28 modelName parameter end to end: the service named the id that was passed, not the saved one. The old fallback also advised saving the settings first, which stopped being true in v1.8.3.28 when the button began saving them itself. 364 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.28: the two object-masking UI bugs reported in discussion #11, where the feature itself is confirmed working - Ultralytics YOLO exports load (YOLO26n fastest in the reporter's testing), boxes land where they should, 5-10 fps at low quality on a Ryzen 5 7600 through docker7-cpu. 'THE STATUS WOULD OFTEN STICK ON A PREVIOUS MODEL NAME' - because it was telling the truth: the button POSTed nothing and the endpoint read only the SAVED config, so a newly typed id loaded the PREVIOUS model and the status correctly named that one. A comment in the UI described this exact trap and guarded only against an empty field; documenting a bug is not fixing it. The endpoint takes a modelName parameter now, the button sends what is on screen, and the saved value stays as the fallback for scripts. 'IT SEEMED TO IGNORE THE CONFIDENCE VALUES I PUT IN' - it did. step=0.05 makes a type=number input report value === '' for entries the browser rejects, and floating point puts ordinary values off that grid: (0.6-0.05)/0.05 evaluates to 10.999999999999998, so 0.6 was rejected. The save path skipped empty strings, which normally means 'left blank' but here meant 'the browser disliked it', so the number vanished without a word. Now step=any, parsed and clamped, and the stored value written back into the field. Both share a root cause: an action button sits next to fields that were not persisted until the global Save, so Load Detection Model now saves the card first - which also stops values reverting when you navigate away and back. Four regression tests, each verified to fail when its fix is reverted. 364 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.27: three defects a live server showed that no unit test could. EVERY TRANSLATED STRING HAS BEEN FALLING BACK TO ITS KEY on every install since the i18n work landed - strings.en.json is declared as an EmbeddedResource, MSBuild lists it as one, and it was not in the DLL, because MSBuild reads the '.en.' in the file name as a CULTURE TAG and compiles it into a satellite assembly the release ZIP does not ship. Jellyfin logged 'Failed to get resource' on every config-page load. The test guarding it asserted that the .csproj MENTIONED the file, which it always did; it now reads the built assembly's manifest resource names, and removing the fix fails it. /hardware-info REPORTED THREE THINGS IT NEVER CHECKED: GpuAvailable returned the HardwareAcceleration config toggle (default on), so a CPU-only server was told it had a GPU while /gpu-verify on the same box reported no devices at all; FFmpegAvailable was the literal true and OnnxRuntime the literal 'Available'. All three are observations now, null means 'not asked yet' rather than 'no', and what the user requested is a separate field. THE FRAME PROXIES THREW AWAY THE DIAGNOSIS: after a container restart the service answers {'detail': 'No model loaded'} and both proxies replaced it with 'Frame upscaling failed'; confirmed that was all it was by loading fsrcnn-x2 and getting 200 at 4.7 fps / 214 ms per frame at 480x270 on a CPU-only box. Also two documentation errors found the same way: GET /Upscaler/health is listed and does not exist (only health/detailed), and benchmark-frame is a GET, not a POST. 360 C# + 166 Python tests green.

versions.changelog: v2.4.2 'Genre and studio badges that count what you watched' - FIXED (#154, thanks @mattsigal for his first PR, with once-per-item counting by @camarigor): TV episodes now credit studio badges with their series' studios (It's Not TV, Auntie Beeb and Netflix and Watch only ever saw movies); TMDb composite genres count for each part ('Action & Adventure' for Action Hero, 'Sci-Fi & Fantasy' for Sci-Fi Scholar and Fantasy Forever) and 'Sci-Fi' counts as 'Science Fiction'; studios match as a whole word plus aliases ('Walt Disney Pictures' counts for Disney, 'HBO Max' for HBO); every item counts once per badge however many of its names match. WHEN YOU UPDATE: watches already in your history start counting, so progress jumps and badges can unlock on the spot (on our server: 11 genre badges across 23 profiles, no progress went down); custom genre and studio badges match the same way (a custom 'War' badge now counts 'War & Politics'); episode plays from before this update stored no studio, so TV credit on studio badges starts now. FIXED (#147, @Roboatlas21, by @camarigor): the Friends chat's message box no longer sits behind a phone's navigation bar. CHANGED (#146, @Roboatlas21, by @camarigor): a plugin card image that survives the catalogue's crop. Deps: codeql-action 4.38.2, ClusterFuzzLite base image. 440/440 tests on both frameworks; smoke-tested on Jellyfin 10.11.10 and 12.1.0. Sigstore-signed + SLSA attested. Drop-in from v2.4.x - no migration.

v2.4.1 'What 2.4.0 got wrong, and a cap you can raise' - FIXED (#140, @Roboatlas21): the Jellyfin 12 package reported a version Jellyfin could not act on. Both assemblies were stamped x.y.z.0, so the dashboard showed 2.4.0.0 for an install the manifest called 2.4.0.1 - the plugin image 404'd and UNINSTALL FAILED OUTRIGHT. Each package now stamps the version it ships as. Stuck on 2.4.0.1? Updating through the catalogue is enough; the restart that loads the new build removes the old folder. FIXED (#141, @Roboatlas21): the page worked in a private window and nowhere else. A browser that cached Jellyfin's page before the plugin was installed revalidates it, Jellyfin answers 304 from the file on disk, and a 304 has no body to inject into - so the browser kept using a copy with no plugin in it. Worst where the web directory is read-only, since the on-disk patch cannot take either. The middleware now forces a full page while the patch has not taken. No need to clear browsing data; a normal reload is enough. CHANGED (#129, @Tschiyo): the targeted badge cap is a setting, 1 to 1000, default still 50, with the targets past it named on the page; the per-play check no longer grows with the target count (ancestor-set lookup, cached collection/playlist members). FIXED (#133, @clarjon1): the Revamp style reached the rest of Jellyfin - invisible checkboxes, text inputs losing border and height, selection colour changing everywhere, on Jellyfin's own controls and every other plugin's settings page. Twelve rules are now anchored to this plugin's own surfaces. FIXED (#131, @Borededdy): a Custom Tab rendered nothing under a theme that ships its own copy of Jellyfin's home page (Abyss); the plugin now builds the missing panel itself. NEW (#136, @Verdancy-Rin): a top-center toast placement plus an admin default for users who have not picked one; also fixed - the default UI style (#43) was never stored, and every main config save switched the page integrations back off. NEW (#138, @Digital-Yeti): optional, off by default - keep accounts hidden from Jellyfin's login screen out of other users' leaderboards, activity feed, friend search, compare picker and profile endpoints. FIXED: this plugin had been returning 500 for the whole server's /api-docs/openapi.json since 2.1.0 - its MediaType enum collided with Jellyfin's own type name and took the entire OpenAPI document down, breaking Swagger UI and every spec-driven client, silently. Renamed to BadgeMediaType; numbers and property names unchanged, nothing to migrate. 421/421 tests on both frameworks; verified live on Jellyfin 10.11.10 and 12.1.0. Sigstore-signed + SLSA attested. Drop-in from v2.4.0 - no schema change, no migration.

v2.3.1 'Music that counts, and leaderboards that show you' - a fast follow to 2.3.0. FIXED (#93/#94): music tracks no longer inherit genres and tags from their album or artist, so a custom 'disco tracks' badge stops counting dance and pop plays by a disco-tagged artist. FIXED (#95/#96): the watch-history scan now replays played music, so the artist discography badges from 2.3.0 can be rebuilt from a scan instead of only ever building from live playback - which also fixes music-heavy profiles that came back from a scan looking empty. Track count is reported in the scan summary. FIXED: deleted Jellyfin accounts no longer appear on leaderboards as raw GUIDs or inflate the admin user count; leaderboards and server stats filter to accounts that still exist, and the admin Stats/Leaderboard tabs refresh on open. NEW: a 'Prune deleted accounts' admin button reclaims the on-disk profiles of removed accounts. NEW: both the admin and user-facing leaderboards always show your own rank - highlighted in the top ten, or appended with your true rank below it (all six category boards on the standalone page). CHANGED: the 'Blades' shareable card skin is now 'Aurora', localized across all 8 languages (slug unchanged, existing selections preserved). Thanks to @Daemon-Network for real-music-library testing and @camarigor for the music fixes. 202/202 tests, live smoke-tested. Sigstore-signed + SLSA attested. Drop-in from v2.3.0 / v2.2.x / v2.1.x.

v2.3.0 'Friends & Foundations' - a social layer on top of reliability fixes that matter to published builds. NEW (#76): hover a friend in the drawer for a profile card (rank tier, completion, score, best streak, equipped showcase) and click to pin a larger one; backed by a public-summary endpoint gated by the same leaderboard opt-out, so it exposes nothing extra. NEW: three server-rendered shareable card skins - Console (default), Metro, and Aurora Spine - each drawn in the card owner's rank colour and chosen per user. FIXED (#80/#79): library completion now recomputes during the watch-history scan, so its five badges finally unlock through normal use instead of sitting at zero on every install. NEW (#81/#24): artist discography completion - played over total tracks per artist - as both a badge and a parameterised custom-badge metric. NEW (#77/#84/#85): Tracearr history crediting for deleted media and true rewatch counts via the public v2 API, with a standalone sync button made idempotent by a ledger. NEW: per-user toast position (four corners or top-centre); admin-set default achievements UI style with optional lock (#43). RELIABILITY: watch-time carry survives session breaks, restarts, and media-file replacement/quality upgrades (#87/#89/#91/#92); rebuilt counters floored with dated snapshots; per-user backfill lock. FIXED (#59/#60): profile data loss where opening the friends panel could create an empty twin profile that later folded over the live one. FIXED (#46): the injected UI now mounts under gzip, so the sidebar, widget, item ribbon and toasts load in every browser (also behind #37/#36). Full 8-language coverage. 200/200 tests, live smoke-tested. Thanks to @camarigor for the profiles, Tracearr, completion wiring, carry work, and the data-loss/gzip fixes. Sigstore-signed + SLSA build-provenance attested. Drop-in from v2.2.x / v2.1.x / v2.0.x.

v2.2.0 'Your Screen, Your Rules' - modular navigation and unlock notifications. NEW (#37): optional Custom Tabs and Plugin Pages hosts reuse the stock Achievements surface; both are admin opt-in, fail safely when the host is unavailable, and never remove the built-in page. NEW (#37): every user can independently show or hide the Custom Tabs entry, Plugin Pages entry, and header trophy from Achievement settings or Jellyfin's native user settings without disabling tracking. NEW (#38): simultaneous unlocks can use one grouped count/score summary or individual queued animations. NEW (#38): toast delivery can target all signed-in devices or only the Jellyfin device that earned the unlock, with origin matching enforced server-side. ADDED: real single unlock toasts are mouse- and keyboard-navigable to the exact highlighted badge; grouped summaries open Recently unlocked. Synthetic admin previews remain inert and no-write. ADDED: Test 10 unlocks admin preview, build-specific client asset cache keys, and full localization of every new option across all 8 UI languages. Drop-in from v2.1.x / v2.0.x; safe defaults, no manual migration. 67/67 tests plus live headed Playwright smoke. Sigstore-signed + SLSA attested.

v2.1.3 'Open Library' (patch) - resolves the outstanding reports from #24 and #36 plus a full builder-localization pass. FIXED (#24): genre-filtered music badges now actually filter by genre - plays and listening time are tracked per genre (case-insensitive), so a 'play 50 disco tracks' badge no longer ticks up when you listen to metal; three new builder metrics (music plays / music hours / items watched of a genre) reveal a genre field. FIXED (#24): custom badges fully delete - the visual builder, badge list and delete now share one store (previously split, so builder-made badges could not be removed) and deleting a badge purges its earned + equipped copies from every user profile; a one-time ID-preserving migration folds legacy badges into the unified store on first startup. FIXED (#24): badge category labels no longer show raw category.* keys, and every built-in category is translated. FIXED (#36): header UI survives another header-injecting plugin - when a second plugin (e.g. Ratings) stripped the badge scripts from index.html, the guard used to think it was still patched and never re-injected; it now keys on the actual script tag so a stripped page is always repaired. ADDED: full localization of the badge/quest builders, power-up + cosmetic pickers and status messages across all 8 languages. NOTE: ebook reading progress still isn't tracked - Jellyfin exposes no page count or reading time, so Book badges credit on mark-as-played completion. Drop-in from v2.1.x / v2.0.x. 52/52 tests. Release 2.0.0.12
AniLiberty STRM Native Media Segments & Docker Playback Hardening

This release improves Jellyfin-native skip controls, managed-library refresh behavior, authentication visibility, and Docker playback safety. It also expands automated coverage and adds formatting/analyzer checks to both stable and nightly release pipelines.

### Licensing and Branding
- The repository is now licensed for non-commercial use under the **PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0**.
- Added explicit commercial licensing, trademark, and required-notice documents.
- Commercial use requires separate permission from the project owner; the AniLiberty STRM name and branding are not granted for unrestricted reuse.

### Docker Direct Play Guard
- Fixed automatic playback proxy URL selection inside Docker and other containers.
- The plugin no longer writes container-only bridge addresses such as `172.17.x.x` into generated `.strm` files.
- Proxy base URL priority is now: explicit **Jellyfin Playback Proxy Base URL**, `JELLYFIN_PublishedServerUrl`, then native-host auto-detection outside containers.
- When no client-reachable HTTP(S) base URL exists in a container, generation safely falls back to direct AniLiberty HLS URLs and records a clear task warning.
- Invalid manual or published proxy URLs are ignored instead of producing broken playback links.

### Native Skip Intro / Outro
- Replaced generated EDL and chapter XML skip files with a Jellyfin `IMediaSegmentProvider` implementation.
- Opening and ending timings are stored in `.aniliberty-strm-plugin/media-segments.json` and exposed as native Jellyfin media segments.
- Added background warm-up and path-to-episode reconciliation so existing library items receive updated skip timings without rewriting user-authored metadata.

### Managed Mirror and Metadata Refresh
- Expanded managed manifest tracking for STRM, NFO, artwork, popularity metadata, and media-segment state.
- Generated metadata is refreshed when the upstream AniLiberty signal changes while unmarked user-authored files remain protected.
- Cleanup remains bounded to plugin-managed files, with `Keep`, `DryRun`, and opt-in `Delete` behavior.
- Improved specials, franchise-season, fractional-ordinal, hydration, and image-handling paths.

### Popularity and Authentication Visibility
- Added an optional AniLiberty popularity badge to Jellyfin Web item pages.
- Added a public, read-only metadata endpoint backed only by plugin-generated popularity sidecars.
- Added Jellyfin activity notifications when a stored AniLiberty token starts returning HTTP 401/403, with cooldown protection against notification spam.
- Improved login/password, OTP, favorites, and watch-timecode API handling and validation.

### Playback and Sync Reliability
- Kept HLS playlist and segment delivery streaming through Jellyfin without buffering complete media objects in memory.
- Improved STRM URL normalization, playlist route handling, redirect validation, and playback diagnostics.
- Improved per-session watch-progress coordination, cancellation, path resolution, and forward-only progress updates.

### Quality Gates and Verification
- Added `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` to stable and nightly workflows, covering formatting and built-in Roslyn analyzer diagnostics without an extra linter dependency.
- Expanded automated coverage across controllers, API clients, scheduled tasks, managed cleanup, native media segments, popularity injection, authentication notifications, and Docker proxy URL selection.
- Full release-gated result: **207/207 non-integration tests passed**, clean Debug and Release builds, and zero compiler warnings. Three opt-in live AniLiberty API checks remain outside the release gate.
- Reproduced the Docker failure on Jellyfin 10.11.11: an internal bridge URL caused `DirectPlayError` and ffmpeg fallback; a client-reachable proxy URL played the same H.264/AAC stream through Direct Play with no transcoding.

### Upgrade Notes
- Restart Jellyfin after installing the update.
- Run **Generate AniLiberty STRM library** again so existing `.strm` files and managed state receive the new routing and metadata behavior.
- Docker users who want Jellyfin-proxied playback should set **Jellyfin Playback Proxy Base URL** or `JELLYFIN_PublishedServerUrl` to an address reachable by playback devices and the Jellyfin container.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build.
- No full-segment server-side cache or mid-segment resume; brief client-side HLS buffering remains the current protection against connection jitter.
- No change to AniLiberty API endpoint hosts or the legacy GitHub Pages repository URL.
- No season-gap fix: the reported missing-season case was not established as a plugin defect in this work.

Release 2.0.0.11
AniLiberty STRM Support Trace & Docker Preflight

This update adds a safer diagnostics flow for Docker and headless Jellyfin setups: compact logs stay readable, while the Support Trace rail captures the full failure context needed for issue triage.

### Diagnostic Command Center
- Added a **Huge trace** switch for explicit support sessions.
- `Show logs` now remains the compact operational view for normal task results.
- `Show support trace` exposes the high-volume diagnostic stream only after Huge trace is enabled and the task is rerun.
- `Copy support bundle` packages sanitized configuration, compact logs, and captured support trace without exposing AniLiberty tokens.

### Full Exception Visibility
- Support trace now records full exception details, including stack traces and inner exceptions.
- Compact logs keep short, readable error summaries so normal UI logging does not turn into a wall of text.
- Verified with a read-only Docker output path: the trace captures the filesystem failure, plugin preflight stack, task failure stack, and remediation hint.

### Docker Output Flight Check
- Scheduled generation now validates that the configured output root is writable before fetching AniLiberty catalog data.
- Permission and path failures now stop early with a clear message about Docker volume mapping, host directory ownership, and PUID/PGID permissions.
- Favorites and full-catalog generation both run this preflight before network/catalog work begins.

### Noise Suppression
- Detailed catalog page progress, per-title generation chatter, and stale-file dry-run lists are routed into support trace instead of compact logs.
- Compact logging defaults remain tuned for routine operation.
- Debug logging in compact logs is now described separately from support trace so the UI makes the diagnostic path clearer.

### Verification
- Built and tested with the non-integration suite.
- Smoke-tested in Docker on Jellyfin 10.11 with manifest installation.
- Confirmed support trace captures full write-permission failures while compact logs remain short.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build.
- No change to AniLiberty API endpoint hosts.
- No change to the legacy repository URL used for the plugin manifest.

Release 2.0.0.10
AniLiberty STRM Docker Playback Rail Fix

This update tightens the Docker playback path for AniLiberty STRM Plugin and documents the supported container workflow: repository manifest install, container-visible output path, scheduled reconstruction, Jellyfin library scan, and proxied HLS playback.

### Docker Playback Proxy Rail
- Fixed a Docker/headless Jellyfin case where `ReverseVirtualPath` could resolve the playback proxy route as `file:///AniLibertyPlayback/hls`.
- Generated `.strm` files now keep the Playback Proxy Rail on HTTP/HTTPS instead of writing unusable `file://` proxy URLs.
- Added proxy endpoint tests that preserve valid absolute HTTP routes and normalize non-HTTP absolute routes back into Jellyfin route paths.

### Docker First Launch Flight Check
- Added a README path contract for Docker: plugin output path and Jellyfin media library path must use the same container-visible path.
- Documented a working volume pattern such as `/srv/aniliberty-strm:/media/aniliberty-strm`.
- Added a first-run sequence for full-catalog generation, favorites generation, scheduled tasks, and empty-output diagnostics.

### Tested Environment

- Smoke-tested on Windows 10 Pro with Docker Desktop 4.51.0, Docker Engine 28.5.2, and Docker Compose 2.40.3.
- Confirmed Jellyfin scans generated output as a TV library, recognizes generated series and episodes, returns item-level playback info, rewrites HLS playlists through the proxy, and streams HLS segments through the plugin route.

### Not Included

- No change to AniLiberty API endpoint hosts.
- No change to the legacy repository URL used for the plugin manifest.

Release 2.0.0.9
AniLiberty STRM Hardening System Release

This update hardens AniLiberty STRM Plugin as a full Jellyfin reconstruction system: stable Jellyfin ABI targeting, explicit AniLiberty identity, safer generated-library governance, streaming playback proxying, and a stronger operational surface for administrators.

### Jellyfin Compatibility & Quality Gates
- Pinned all `Jellyfin.*` NuGet references to `10.11.0` to stop builds from silently drifting to newer Jellyfin packages.
- Added committed `packages.lock.json` files and locked restore in CI.
- Added CI checks that verify every resolved `Jellyfin.*` package remains on `10.11.0` while `targetAbi` stays `10.11.0.0`.
- Release automation now keeps `build.yaml`, package version, assembly version, file version, and informational version in sync.

### AniLiberty Identity & API Courtesy
- Rebranded the public plugin identity to **AniLiberty STRM Plugin** while keeping the legacy `AniLibriaStrmPlugin` repository URL for install compatibility and branch history.
- Added a shared `PluginIdentity` with display name, product token, repository URL, version discovery, and canonical User-Agent.
- All AniLiberty API, media proxy, static media, and HLS clients now identify as:
  `AniLibertyStrmPlugin/<version> (Jellyfin; +https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin)`.

### Mirror Governance Layer
- Added `.aniliberty-strm-plugin/manifest.json` inside each output root to track files managed by the plugin.
- The manifest records generated STRM, ANIID, EDL, chapter XML, NFO, artwork/thumbs, release/episode IDs, hashes, sources, and timestamps.
- First manifest run initializes the baseline and never prunes existing files.
- Generated NFO/artwork refreshes only when the file is known as plugin-managed through the manifest or generated marker.
- Existing unmarked `.nfo` files and artwork are preserved as user-owned content.

### Safe Cleanup Modes
- Added `StaleCleanupMode`: `Off`, `DryRun`, and `Delete`.
- Default is `DryRun`, which reports stale managed files without deleting anything.
- `Delete` removes only manifest-managed stale files and then removes empty directories created by that cleanup path.
- Untracked user files are left alone.

### Playback Proxy Rail
- Non-playlist HLS segments and keys now stream directly to `Response.Body`.
- The proxy no longer reads segment/key payloads into memory with `ReadAsByteArrayAsync`.
- Upstream host allow-listing and redirect validation remain in place.
- Playlist rewriting continues to route segments and keys through the Jellyfin proxy endpoint.

### Identity & Access Command Center
- OTP codes are no longer persisted in plugin configuration after the OTP flow.
- Login/password and OTP sign-in clear stored OTP state.
- The token box is masked by default, with explicit reveal/copy actions.
- Auth logs no longer include the login e-mail address.

### Operational Reliability
- Scheduled tasks now rethrow failures after logging so Jellyfin can mark task execution accurately.
- Cancellation flows are preserved instead of being swallowed as generic failures.
- AniLiberty progress pull no longer overwrites newer local Jellyfin playback positions with older remote timecodes.
- Clearing UI logs now persists the cleared state.

### Presentation & Documentation
- README now presents the plugin as a coherent product system: Signal Acquisition Layer, Context-Aware Reconstruction Core, Playback Proxy Rail, Mirror Governance Layer, Operational Command Center, and Distribution Quality Gates.
- Added three README visual assets showing the reconstruction core, system capability layers, and operational command center.

### Test Coverage
- Added tests for Jellyfin package pins and lock-file resolution.
- Added User-Agent and named/static HTTP client coverage.
- Added managed mirror tests for baseline creation, generated metadata refresh, unmarked NFO preservation, dry-run cleanup, delete cleanup, and empty-directory cleanup.
- Added proxy tests for streaming segments, playlist rewriting, unsupported upstream rejection, redirect validation, and upstream failure status.
- Added auth/config tests for OTP payload boundaries, safe defaults, and AniLiberty identity.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build in this release.
- No migration of AniLiberty API endpoint hosts.
- No destructive cleanup unless `StaleCleanupMode` is explicitly changed to `Delete`.

versions.changelog: Rifinitura completa del motore di ricerca e abbinamento, del backend e dell'interfaccia: guardia sull'anno nei sequel per stagione, conservazione dell'ID stagione e separazione della trama serie/stagione nei refresh, pulizia degli ID figli obsoleti e cache immediata quando si corregge un abbinamento, refresh post-traduzione AI anche per le serie, cache delle sottopagine personaggi/relazioni vuote, allineamento tra analisi singola e completa della libreria, protezione lato server della chiave AI al cambio di destinazione e miglioramenti di accessibilità e reattività nella pagina del plugin. README rinnovato. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Corretto il doppio caricamento dopo un aggiornamento (issue #2): lo ZIP contiene un meta.json con il nome del plugin, così Jellyfin tiene tutte le versioni sotto lo stesso nome e rimuove la vecchia, e all'avvio il plugin segna come superate le proprie copie più vecchie. Licenza AGPLv3 con termini aggiuntivi (attribuzione, versioni modificate riconoscibili, marchi e mascotte); attribuzione e link al codice sorgente nella pagina del plugin. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AniList come fonte senza chiave insieme a TMDB: cast giapponese con i personaggi, studio di animazione, date, stato, voto, trailer, copertina e banner, solo nei campi vuoti. L'anno di una stagione senza date arriva dalla catena dei sequel di AniList, se gli episodi coincidono. Gli ID AniList che non corrispondono per tipo o anno vengono ignorati. Nuovo passo AniList nel setup. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Comunità per tutti: dopo una correzione il plugin chiede se condividerla e la invia tramite il servizio della comunità, senza account; il token GitHub diventa facoltativo. Si condividono anche le stagioni con una scheda propria, applicate agli altri solo se numero di stagione ed episodi coincidono. Elenco approvato aggiornato ogni giorno, controlli automatici e approvazione con un'etichetta, tessera Comunità in Inizio, passo Comunità nel setup e scelta della stagione in «Correggi un abbinamento». Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Pagina del plugin rifatta da zero con l'identità di AnimeClick: setup guidato al primo avvio e solo i passi nuovi dopo gli aggiornamenti importanti, vetrina degli ultimi anime aggiornati, cruscotto della collezione, libreria a locandine con titoli e trame uniti per anime, attivazione delle librerie a un clic e ricerca della scheda su AnimeClick per correggere un abbinamento. Corretti i conteggi dell'analisi di una singola serie, lo stato della condivisione comunitaria appena attivata e «Da verificare», che ora coincide con quanto «Sistema tutti i titoli» ricontrolla. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Scarta i titoli alternativi di un'altra stagione verificando il titolo inglese originale. Quando manca una fonte coerente, traduce il titolo inglese già valido; esclude i nomi dei file. Correzione trovata sul NAS in anteprima, senza salvare la proposta errata. Include le novità 1.2.1. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AnimeClick come unico provider remoto per le librerie anime: identificazione TMDB verificata, completamento dei metadati senza altri plugin e immagini integrate Fanart → TMDB → AnimeClick. Chiavi Fanart personale e di progetto nelle impostazioni, con link e verifica. Numerazione, campi bloccati e immagini esistenti conservati. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AnimeClick primo campo per campo: i valori generici lasciano spazio alle fonti configurate. Recupero italiano e traduzione dall’inglese anche per serie, film, generi e tag, senza mescolare titolo e trama. Le immagini conservano la precedenza dei provider ad alta risoluzione; nessun aggiornamento immagini o riparazione viene avviato dall’installazione. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Titoli episodio mancanti: ricerca su TheTVDB e TMDB configurati dopo AnimeClick, precedenza all’italiano e traduzione dei soli titoli inglesi con il profilo AI esistente. Verifica degli ID esterni, conservazione dei titoli compilati e indicazione della fonte nell’avanzamento. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

La tua libreria con analisi automatica, viste separate, avanzamento reale e interruzione dei lavori. Recupero dei soli titoli mancanti con protezione dei metadati esistenti. Abbinamenti della comunità e invio automatico delle correzioni su GitHub, entrambi facoltativi e disattivati di default. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

versions.changelog:
## Fixed
- Remove unnecessary logging. Episodes Jellyfin has not finished reading yet no longer log an error during the first library scan

## Developer
- Built for Jellyfin 12.2 (target ABI 12.2.0.0). Servers on Jellyfin 12.0 or 12.1 keep the previous release.
- Updated test dependencies (Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.11, NSubstitute 6.2, xunit 2.9.3, xunit.runner.visualstudio 4.0.1).

## Fixed
- A logo design file that cannot be read is no longer replaced with a single default design. The default is used until the file is fixed, and a copy of the damaged file is kept beside it as logos.json.bak
- Cleanup Backdrops only removes the extra backdrops the plugin generated. Fanart beside your media, backdrops from other providers, and files another item still uses are never deleted. Backdrops generated by earlier versions cannot be told apart and are left alone
- A configuration saved with missing sections is filled in and checked before it is written, instead of being saved and then failing on every start
- A metadata refresh renders one image of each type, and as many backdrops as the library keeps, instead of a full set of choices for every type
- Edit Images offers the full number of choices for every image type, including types the item does not have yet
- An episode or film only checks its own video file when new frames are needed, and a season or series looks up its episodes once per image instead of several times
- The server can fetch its own generated images when it runs under a base URL and its local address cannot be resolved
- Routine per item messages during a library scan are logged at Debug instead of Information
- Saving logo designs while the configuration is being saved no longer races
- The plugin catalog description now matches what the plugin does

## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.19.

## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Features
- Frames are no longer taken from inside media segments, so intros, credits, recaps, previews, and commercials stay out of generated artwork
- New Avoid Media Segments setting under Frame Extraction, with a checkbox for each kind of segment to avoid, all on by default
- Segments come from a media segment provider turned on for the library, so items without any extract as before

## Developer
- Changing which segments are avoided discards the idle frame pools, so the next refresh extracts under the new choice

## Features
- New Cleanup Backdrops scheduled task under Library that reduces every item on the server to a single backdrop, keeping the first and deleting the rest along with their files
- The task has no default schedule, so it only runs when started by hand or on a trigger you add

## Features
- Primary and thumb images can name a second and third design, adding their versions of the same frames to the Edit Images picker
- New Edit Images Cache setting for how long rendered choices stay available, default 30 minutes
- Edit Images reuses the choices it already rendered when switching image type or page, instead of rendering every image again

## Fixes
- The Edit Images cache is bounded by size at 256 MB and releases expired images on its own, instead of holding them until the next render
- Every design in one Edit Images render draws from the same frames, even while other items are extracting
- Posters pass over a logo Jellyfin only knows by web address and use the next logo that can be read

## Developer
- Settings saved before 12.0.2.0 are no longer brought forward, so update through 12.0.2.1 first when coming from an older version
- Code, pages, and docs say logo rather than series logo, since films draw their own

## Fixes
- The Profiles page loads again instead of failing on a backdrop setting that no longer exists
- Posters with a logo draw the logo selected for a film, season, or series instead of falling back to text

## Features
- Artwork Generator is Episode Poster Generator rebuilt, with the same settings and a much wider job
- The repository moved with the name; re-add it as jellyfin-plugin-artworkgenerator to keep getting updates
- Draws posters, thumbs, backdrops, and text logos, where before there were only episode posters
- Covers series, seasons, films, music videos, home videos, and anything else with a video
- Configuration is rebuilt in three parts, designs, logos, and profiles
- Profiles decide which items get which images and which design draws each one
- Every design renders portrait and landscape, so one design covers a tall poster and a wide thumb
- A design's two lines are now simply the title and the subtitle, whatever the item is
- Text position and alignment work on every design, not just the few that had them
- New Bloom design, pooling color from the frame behind the text
- New Grid canvas, tiling several extracted frames into one picture
- Logo designs build a text logo from any name field, with letter case, a line limit, and frame-filled letters
- Frame extraction is one set of server settings instead of a copy on every design
- Frames are ranked on tone, detail, contrast, and color rather than just clearing a threshold
- Optional setting drops a subtitle that only repeats the title
- A subtitle too long to fit can shorten to its code, shrink, or trim
- Two example designs per style, each showing a genuinely different look

## Fixes
- Seasons extract from their own episodes instead of falling back to the series backdrop
- Candidate images come from different episodes instead of clustering in one
- Heavily letterboxed frames scale back up to a usable size
- Portrait text is measured against both sides, so it no longer reads small
- Brush strokes stay thick on tall posters instead of piling into a cross
- Long titles trim at a word boundary rather than mid-word
- Descenders stay inside the safe area
- Borders, rules, and shadows scale with the poster
- A static graphic keeps its proportions
- An item with no name of its own says its one line in the larger type
- Generated images carry the item's metadata language

## Developer
- The generator, the settings model, and the configuration page are rebuilt around item kinds rather than episodes
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 that Jellyfin 12.0 ships
- Designs are found by reflection, so adding one needs a class and an enum value
- Every label, option, and default is read from the settings models
- The shared generator is split into pipeline, text, and overlay
- Frame analysis is a single pass, under a megabyte per frame instead of three and a half
- Every one-time upgrade of an older configuration sits in its own file, to be deleted whole once installs have moved on
- Tests hold the documentation, the templates, and US spelling to the code

## Features
- Shadows, rules, and the Frame border now scale with the poster, so they read the same on a 4K frame as on a DVD rip instead of turning into a hairline or a slab
- Long titles that do not fit two lines fill the first line with whole words and trim only the second, at a word boundary, instead of cutting both lines mid-word

## Fixes
- Frame drew no border at all for an episode without a name, and ignored the Show Title setting
- Cutout no longer lets a two line title run into the bottom of the cutout letters
- Split center-crops the series poster into its panel instead of stretching artwork that is not 2:3
- Brush honours the Show Episode setting and keeps a wrapped title inside the area the strokes leave clear
- Timeline keeps the marker dot inside the safe area on the first and last episode
- Text blocks are reserved from the font's real ascent and descent, so descenders no longer hang past the safe area

## Developer
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 packages Jellyfin 12.0 ships, since the plugin binds to the server's copies at runtime
- Text drawing moved from the removed SKPaint text members to SKFont, wrapped in a shared TextStyle so every style measures and draws with the same objects
- Standard and Split share one text stack; Numeral, Cutout, Brush, and Frame no longer hand-build their own paints
- Cutout renders through a canvas layer instead of a full-size scratch bitmap per poster; Split and Brush dispose their gradient shaders
- Letterbox detection scans the pixel buffer directly instead of a native call per pixel
- Bitmap scaling uses explicit cubic resampling now that FilterQuality is gone

Authenticate your Jellyfin with Authelia, and optionally create users who do not yet exist automatically.

Bonfire.description: Adds multi-user profile switching to Jellyfin. A single account can have up to five isolated profiles — each with its own watch history, parental controls, and library access.

versions.changelog:
**Fixed**

- On 2019 LG TVs (webOS 4.5), Bonfire did not start at all. [#34]
- With "Ask who's watching on startup" off, there was no Switch Profile button and no way to switch.
- After signing out of the iOS app, the previous account's profile stayed on the sign-in screen and carried over to the next account.
- On iPad, your own profiles could appear as a linked Bonfire, and Manage Profiles asked you to open yourself first.
- The profile picture in the header was drawn zoomed in and blurry.

**Fixed**

- Security: any account could run script in an administrator's browser through the Bonfire settings page. Please update.
- Security: a PIN typed into a TV or app sign-in screen could be guessed with no limit.
- Security: someone using a profile in a browser could take over the main account behind it.
- On Android TV, Roku and other TV apps, choosing a profile and entering its PIN was refused.
- A profile limited to one TV could be missing from that TV's sign-in screen.
- Skipping Quick Connect on known TVs also removed it for other people with the same TV model.
- Signing in on a TV could occasionally fail with a server error.
- Creating a profile could fail with "The supplied value is invalid". [#33]
- The profile picker ran off the bottom of the screen on a TV. [#31]
- A profile kept its old rating after its account's rating was lowered.
- Clearing your PIN, or using the emergency disable code, could stop your password working.
- An account with a PIN could not change its Jellyfin password.
- Creating two profiles at once could go over the profile limit.
- The Signed-in devices list in the dashboard could fail to load.
- The create form showed only four libraries at a time.

**Changed**

- A profile keeps every restriction set on its account, such as remote access, schedules and bitrate.
- Profiles in another household's Bonfire need a PIN, unless their owner allows switching on the home network.
- Hidden Bonfire profiles can no longer be opened.
- Removing someone from your Bonfire changes its code, so they cannot rejoin with the old one.
- Reopening the app keeps the profile you were using. Going back to your main profile asks for its PIN.
- Manage Profiles needs your main profile open.

**Added**

- Thirty starter avatars to pick from, on by default. Turn them off in Dashboard -> Bonfire -> Avatar Library. [#32]
- Picture quality for profile pictures and avatars: Dashboard -> Bonfire -> Picture quality.
- A New code button for your Bonfire.
- A loader for the Samsung Tizen app, so Bonfire updates reach the TV without rebuilding the app. [#16]

**Fixed**

- Giving a profile a new library in Dashboard -> Users was undone the next time anyone entered that profile. Grants made there are now kept. To take a library away from a profile, edit the profile. [#30]
- Turning on "Skip Quick Connect on known devices" took Quick Connect away from apps that already have a password screen. It now applies only to Android TV, which is the one that needs it.

**Added**

- Profiles can appear on the sign-in screens of Jellyfin for Roku, Swiftfin, Findroid and Wholphin, the same as Android TV. Turn off automatic sign in on the app, or it goes straight into the last account.
- Apps that have no user list of their own can enter a profile by typing the profile's name and its PIN.

**Changed**

- The README is shorter. Library artwork, Bonfire sharing and known limitations now have their own pages under docs/.

**Added**

- Profiles can now appear on the sign-in screen of apps that never load the web client, such as Android TV, and be opened with their PIN. New settings under Dashboard -> Bonfire -> TVs & Apps, all off until you turn them on.
- On those screens a profile shows the name you gave it, not the full account name.
- An account that owns profiles can sign in with its PIN as well as its password.
- Apps can be sent straight to the password field instead of a Quick Connect code.
- "Who's watching?" on startup can be set per device instead of everywhere at once.

**Works on Jellyfin 12.0.** The same build serves 10.11 and 12.0 — there is nothing extra to install.

**Fixed**

- On Jellyfin 12.0 the Switch Profile button was missing from the header. Its default layout keeps the old header in the page but hides it, and Bonfire was adding the button there.
- In the profile form, text boxes would not take a click and dropdowns would not open — the page jumped to the top instead. Jellyfin's account menu was being left open, and its focus handling and Bonfire's fought each other.
- The Switch Profile button could appear beside the wrong icon at the wrong size, then move a second or two later. It now appears once, beside your account icon.
- Importing avatars from a folder failed on Jellyfin 12.0, and on any server where an administrator had turned legacy authorization off.
- The Bonfire section on your profile page sat against the left edge while the rest of the page was centred.
- The rename and merge buttons in the device list were unstyled, and drew as empty boxes on televisions without an emoji font.

**Changed**

- Bonfire follows your theme's accent colour on Jellyfin 12.0, which publishes that colour under a new name.

**Fixed**

- Switching to someone's main profile wiped that person's library access, and their sub-profiles' access with it. If this has happened to you, re-tick their libraries in Jellyfin's user settings after updating. [#27]
- Switching into an administrator's account quietly removed their admin rights and hid them from the login screen. [#27]
- Restricting a profile to specific devices could lock it out of every device, including the ones you picked. [#16]
- On a TV, picking a profile changed the name at the top but left you in your main account — same libraries, same Continue Watching, same Next Up. [#16]
- On a TV, moving off the first profile jumped straight to Manage Profiles and no other profile could be reached. [#16]
- On a TV the profile cards had no size and the focus outline never appeared, so nothing looked selectable. Save could also sit below the bottom of the profile form with no way to reach it on a remote. [#16]
- The profile switcher said you were signed in as your main profile even while a sub-profile was in use.
- A profile, device or Bonfire group you had just saved could silently not be there.
- Anything added while the plugin's settings page was open was undone when an administrator pressed Save.
- One computer could appear several times in the device list, and devices that sent no name all read as "Unknown Device".
- Forgetting a profile's only allowed device silently made that profile available everywhere. It is refused now, and says which profiles are in the way.
- "Try again in 15 minutes" after too many wrong PINs. It now tells you the wait it is actually enforcing, which is usually far less.
- Device "last seen" dates reset every time Jellyfin restarted, and the device list never dropped hardware nobody uses any more.
- A language could stop loading until Jellyfin was restarted, dropping everyone back to English.
- Switching profiles on a light theme flashed a black screen, and a switch that went wrong left the screen blank for four seconds.
- The profile screen re-downloaded every profile picture on every page load. Your browser keeps them now.

**Added**

- Bonfire knows when it is on a television, and makes the profile pictures, text and focus outline large enough to use from across a room.
- Rename a device, or tell Bonfire that two entries are the same machine. "Tidy up duplicates" folds together the several devices one browser makes — a profile allowed on any of them stays allowed.
- A list of everyone signed in, with the household each profile belongs to, and a way to sign one device out.
- Export and import the plugin's configuration, so there is a copy of your profiles and PINs somewhere other than one file.
- The audit log can be filtered by name and date, and downloaded.
- Polish, contributed by danis101. [#26]
- TROUBLESHOOTING.md, which answers the most common report first: Bonfire does not edit index.html by default, so a file with no plugin tags in it is a healthy install.

**Changed**

- The Switch Profile button now sits next to your account icon in the header, instead of at the end of the row.
- The interface reads correctly on light Jellyfin themes, where separators and muted text used to be invisible.
- Bonfire does far less work in the background — most noticeable on a TV, and it steps back further while something is playing.
- The "restart to finish updating" notice now names the version running and the version waiting, so you can tell whether your restart worked. [#25]

**New**

- Bonfire no longer edits Jellyfin's `index.html`. The client script is added to the page as it is served, so there is nothing to re-apply after a Jellyfin update and no file permissions to grant. Patching the file stays available as a legacy option under **Advanced → Client script**. (#17, #11, #3)
- The switcher follows your theme's accent colour instead of always drawing Jellyfin blue.
- Profile screens use the whole window on a desktop instead of one phone-width column.
- The picker shows which profile you are currently watching as.

**Fixed**

- On Android, picking a profile could bring the picker straight back, over and over, and a PIN-protected profile could drop you at the account login.
- Picking a profile showed nothing at all for the second or two it takes, so the tap read as missed. The profile you picked now shows a spinner, and the screen no longer goes black while it loads.
- Opening a profile took several seconds and could drop you back on a screen you had already left.
- Bonfire rewrote `index.html` on startup even when set never to touch it.
- The settings page reported the client script as installed whenever the plugin was loaded at all, including on servers where nothing was reaching the page.
- Add Profile was missing from the Manage Profiles screen.
- Library names were cut off to "3D Movi…" when choosing artwork.
- **Upload avatars** and **Upload a folder** were unstyled text instead of buttons.
- "PIN Protected" showed in red and "No PIN" in green — the wrong way round.
- The audit log ran the time into the address as "12:09:28 PMIP".

**Changed**

- The plugin is called **Bonfire** in the Jellyfin sidebar.
- Plugin settings are split into tabs — General, Avatars, Accounts, Activity and Advanced — instead of one page five screens tall.
- Switcher Style and Your Bonfire move out of the profile grid into their own **Settings** screen. Bonfire Grouping is now called Your Bonfire.
- Add Profile appears on Manage Profiles only. The "Who's watching?" screen is people to pick from.
- Setting a profile picture is one panel rather than six controls. The paste-a-URL box is gone: a linked picture could not be cropped, was never stored on your server, and disappeared without warning when the link died.
- Libraries and their artwork are one list, with the artwork controls behind a switch.
- Delete is no longer as prominent as Save.

**New**

- Library artwork can be set per profile. Jellyfin builds a library tile from the items inside it, so a Kids profile could see a poster from a film it cannot open; each profile can now be given its own picture for a library, or none at all. (#19)
- Administrators can set the switcher defaults for the whole server, under Dashboard → Plugins → Bonfire. Anyone who has already chosen keeps their own setting. (#14)
- Avatars can be uploaded several at a time, or a whole folder at once. Administrators with a prepared set already on the server can point at its folder and import it. (#14)
- The profile picker has a Cancel button when you opened it yourself, so you can go back to what you were watching.

**Fixed**

- Switching a profile failed with "Invalid username or password" on Jellyfin 10.11.11, and signed the master account out. (#15)
- On Samsung Tizen, picking a profile changed the avatar but left you in the original account. (#15, #16)
- On a TV, the remote could steer the Jellyfin page hidden behind the Bonfire screen. (#16)
- The TV Back button raised Samsung’s "exit application?" prompt behind the Bonfire screen. Back now steps back one screen instead. (#15)
- "Switch Profile" now appears on the Settings page, not only in the header dropdown. (#14)
- Profile pictures could be zoomed but not dragged.
- Save and Cancel are scrolled into view when a remote reaches them, so long profile forms no longer look frozen. (#15)
- Pictures now load in clients that bundle their own web client, such as Samsung Tizen.
- A missing script tag in index.html now says which of the three causes it is. (#17)

**Changed**

- The emergency disable link appears only once an administrator has set a code.
- Error messages, hints and warnings cut down throughout.

First stable release of the 1.3 line, consolidating the 1.2.x pre-releases. ■ NEW — Tag-based content filtering. Each sub-profile can block or allow content by Jellyfin tag (for example "adults", "teens", "kids"), alongside the existing parental rating limit. Tags are inherited, so tagging a series or a whole library applies to everything inside it, and enforcement happens server-side — meaning it holds on every client, including ones that cannot show the profile switcher at all. Blocked tags are additive with the master account's, and an allow-list can only narrow the master's, so a sub-profile can never see more than its parent. ■ NEW — Reorganised profile editor. Creating and editing a profile is now grouped into four titled sections: Profile (name, colour, picture), Security (PIN, LAN bypass, auto-lock), Libraries, and Content & Device Restrictions. Previously every field sat in one flat list in the order features had been added. Sections are plain blocks rather than collapsible panels so D-pad focus order on TV stays predictable, and the layout adapts to phone widths. ■ NEW — The settings page now lists master accounts with their sub-profiles nested underneath, instead of two separate tables. ■ SECURITY — Fixed a stored cross-site scripting flaw in profile avatar images and colours. Because Bonfire groups render profiles from linked households on each other's switcher screens, a crafted value could run script in another user's browser and steal their session token. Values are now validated on the server and escaped on render. ■ SECURITY — Profile PINs are now stored as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes rather than unsalted SHA-256, under which a 4-8 digit PIN was recoverable almost instantly from the configuration file. Existing PINs keep working and are upgraded automatically the next time they are entered. ■ SECURITY — An account with no PIN can no longer be switched into from a shared Bonfire, and the local-network PIN bypass no longer applies when stepping into another household's account. Also removed an open redirect on the profile image endpoint. ■ FIX — The dashboard's client-script warnings are now accurate. They re-check index.html on every page load rather than reporting server-startup state, a "Re-check Now" button re-runs the injection without a Jellyfin restart, and the message names the specific cause — including whether Jellyfin can write the file at all. The advisory notice can be dismissed on installs where the file is not writable without elevating. ■ FIX — Permission-fix commands are generated for the account Jellyfin actually runs as, rather than covering every possibility at once. ■ FIX — Editing a profile no longer erases device whitelist entries for devices that are switched off, and the device picker is correctly scoped to your own household. ■ FIX — A saved PIN no longer displays as "No PIN" on your own network, and profile changes appear immediately instead of requiring a page reload. ■ PERFORMANCE — Profile switching no longer rewrites the entire audit log on the request, the client script is served with revalidation so browsers pick up updates on their own, and a listener leak that made the interface progressively less responsive over a session has been fixed.

⚠️ BETA RELEASE — not a finished release; please report issues on GitHub. ▸ Settings page: master accounts and sub-profiles were listed as two separate tables, so working out which profiles belonged to which account meant reading the "Master Account" column on every row. There is now a single list of master accounts, each with its sub-profiles collapsed underneath it behind a "2 sub-profiles" toggle. PIN status and Reset PIN are available at both levels as before. Any sub-profile whose master account no longer exists — normally the residue of a partially failed deletion — is listed separately under "Unlinked sub-profiles" rather than disappearing, so it can still be found and managed. ▸ The permission-fix commands are now generated for the account Jellyfin is actually running as, and the page states which account that is. Previously they had to cover every possibility at once: on Windows, Jellyfin runs either as a service (NT AUTHORITY\NetworkService) or as the signed-in user when installed as a tray/desktop app, so the icacls command granted Modify to ALL local users in order to work in both cases. It now grants access to exactly one account — the real one — which is both less to type and a considerably narrower permission on a file inside Program Files. ▸ The same applies to the Linux and Docker chown commands, which previously assumed the service account was named "jellyfin". That is the convention but not a guarantee, and the commands silently did nothing useful when it was not. If the account cannot be determined, the page falls back to the previous broader commands, so nothing is lost on unusual setups.

versions.changelog: An **animated GIF background now also moves in the live preview in Firefox**. It only moved in Chrome, Edge and other Chromium-based browsers before; Firefox kept showing a single frame. The preview now plays the GIF in real time at its own speed, redrawn up to about 15 times a second (very fast GIFs skip frames in the preview to keep time). Covers you applied were never affected: they always animated. Browsers that cannot decode an image frame by frame (Safari, for example) still show a still preview, but the applied cover animates as usual.

A polish release for the editor, driven by a full review of the page. **Spacing is fixed**: since the guided-steps redesign some controls sat flush against each other (the Restore button touched the Type dropdown, *In context* touched Dimensions) while other gaps were twice as big. Every step now has one even rhythm, and dropdowns line up with the buttons beside them. **Errors are readable**: when the server refuses a request you now see why — your session expired, the file is too large, too many requests, or the server's own reason for refusing a design — in your own language, instead of *"Unexpected end of JSON input"*, and nothing is left stuck on "Applying…". **Fewer surprises**: Restore, deleting a template and batch apply now ask before they act (like Reset backup already did), batch apply says how many covers it will replace and can no longer be started twice, loading a template asks before replacing changes you have not applied, and the browser warns before you close the tab with unapplied work — only when the design really differs from what you last applied, saved or loaded. Undo and loading a template **keep your background image** on the preview instead of dropping it, and an animated GIF background keeps moving. Choosing a **Custom** size or **Animated GIF** now shows their settings straight away, and **Save this design** and **Apply to several targets** are no longer tucked away under Advanced. Custom sizes stay between 100 and 2048 pixels, which is what the server accepts. The editor now **works from the keyboard and with a screen reader**: select layers with Tab and Enter, move the selected layer with the arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps; Alt, Ctrl and Meta combinations are left to the browser), and use the poster browser as a proper dialog that Esc closes and that keeps keyboard focus inside while you page through posters. Every icon button has a name. The poster browser follows **light themes** and the Jellyfin theme colours too. On narrow screens the layer **⋯** button works again. The title starts as the name of the target you pick, the Apply button says what it applies to (library, collection, playlist or Live TV), and switching the display language back to English no longer leaves Dutch or Spanish labels behind. Ctrl+Z now also undoes a slider or colour change, and is no longer intercepted on other dashboard pages. Existing designs and saved templates are unaffected and render exactly as before.

The live preview and the cover that actually gets applied now **agree on text effects**. A **shadow's softness** came out twice as wide on the applied cover as in the preview; it now matches, so a cover with a blurred text shadow looks slightly sharper than before once you apply it again. An **outline on semi-transparent text** used to stay fully solid on the cover however far you turned the opacity down; it now fades with the text, as the preview always showed, and outline corners are a little rounder. On **rotated text**, the cover turned the shadow along with the letters while the preview kept it falling the same way on screen; the cover now does what the preview shows. The preview itself had a few slips of its own: semi-transparent text with a shadow was drawn **slightly too dense**, the **in-context previews** (wide, square, poster) drew text, shadow and outline at full size so they spilled out of the little thumbnails, an **uploaded font** looked artificially bold when the weight was set to bold (the cover never was), and a **gradient from an old template** with fewer than two colour stops showed different colours in the editor, the preview and the cover. All three now show the same colours. Covers you have already applied are not changed until you apply them again. Fully opaque, unrotated text without a blurred shadow or an outline looks the same as before.

A **fix-up release for backups and the live preview**.
**Applying a cover a second time could be refused** with *"Could not back up the current cover"* on libraries that had no backup before 4.0.2.0. The backup was saved under one spelling of the library's id and looked for under another. Backups made by earlier versions are found again, so they keep working and the refusals stop.
**Covers made by this plugin are no longer saved as the "original".** The plugin now remembers the cover it applied last and never backs that up, nor anything in its own data folder. A backup is no longer made of a cover the plugin applied. If you applied covers with an earlier version before a target's first backup was taken (while trying the plugin out, for example), that backup may hold one of those test covers, and **Restore original cover** brings the test cover back instead of the real original. Covers applied by 4.0.2.0 are not recognised as plugin covers until you have applied once with this version.
The new **Reset backup** button next to Restore deletes a target's backup. It saves nothing itself: the next apply stores the cover the target shows at that moment as the new original, unless it is a cover the plugin applied. To fix a wrong backup, first put the cover you want to keep back on the library: upload it in Jellyfin (**Edit images** in the dashboard), or delete the poster and refresh metadata with *Replace existing images*. Then press **Reset backup**, then apply. This matters most if your old backup holds an early test cover, because your true original was overwritten before backups existed and has to come from you. Restores, backups and skipped backups are now written to the Jellyfin log.
In the editor, a **poster collage** background now shows in the live preview. It used to stay black until you pressed Show server render. An **animated GIF** background now moves in the preview instead of standing still, unless your system is set to reduce motion.

A **hardening and housekeeping** release — apart from the fixes below, nothing about how you design covers changes. Applied covers now go through **Jellyfin's own image handling**, the same path as uploading an image in the dashboard, so they are stored alongside the rest of your library artwork and, for covers applied or restored from this version on, **keep working even if the plugin's data folder is cleared** (covers applied by 4.0.1.0 and never re-applied still live in that folder); **Restore original cover** works exactly as before. If the current cover cannot be backed up first, applying is now **refused with a clear message** and the cover is left untouched, so the cover you had before you first used the plugin can always be restored (a cover you set in the dashboard after an earlier apply is replaced by the next apply, as with Jellyfin's own upload). A logo or icon layer scaled larger than **1.5× the canvas** now renders at most 1.5×, so old templates with huge logos render smaller. **Animated images are handled far more carefully**: the server only ever decodes the frames it actually needs (one for a still cover, at most 60 for an animated one). A long or high-resolution animated GIF is no longer turned away — the plugin simply uses as many of its frames as fit safely in memory — and only an image whose single frame is larger than 8192×8192 pixels is **refused at upload with a clear message**. **Ken Burns** covers no longer **stretch** a background whose shape differs from the cover, animated covers render faster, and a shrunk animated GIF keeps its blur and border in proportion. A single faulty text layer can no longer **blank out the whole cover** — it is skipped and everything else still renders. Size errors such as *"Dimensions too large"* are now shown as they are instead of a generic failure. Behind the scenes, the applied-cover folder no longer grows with every apply, applying to the same library or collection is now done one at a time so two applies can no longer overwrite each other, rapid repeated requests can no longer slip past the rate limits (rejected uploads now count toward the upload limit too), and saving a template while a batch apply runs is now safe. **TIFF uploads are no longer accepted** — browsers cannot draw TIFF in the editor, so they never previewed properly; convert to PNG or JPG. The background upload limit can now be changed with `MaxUploadSizeMb` in the plugin's configuration file (1–50 MB, default 5); values above about 28 MB may still be blocked earlier by the web server's own request-size limit.

Fixes the configuration page on Jellyfin 12, where **nothing worked**. Jellyfin 12 stopped accepting the older of its two ways of proving who you are, and the page was still using it — so every request it made was rejected before it reached the plugin. Libraries did not load, saved templates did not appear, the bundled fonts did not arrive, applying a cover did nothing, and opening the poster browser produced the cryptic message *"Failed to execute 'json' on 'Response': Unexpected end of JSON input"*, which was the rejection with no explanation attached. The page now identifies itself the same way the Jellyfin web client does, which works on Jellyfin 10.11 and 12 alike. **If you installed 4.0.0.0, update** — nothing was wrong with your settings or your covers, the page simply could not reach the server.

**Support for Jellyfin 12.** Jellyfin 12 moved to .NET 10 and changed its plugin ABI, so a plugin built for 10.11 cannot be built for both — this release is built against Jellyfin 12 and requires it. Nothing about designing or rendering covers has changed: your saved templates, applied covers and settings all carry over untouched. If you are **still on Jellyfin 10.11**, stay on **3.5.1.0** — your server will keep being offered that version and will not see this one, so nothing breaks by leaving it alone.

Fixes a small but confusing moment with **Live TV** targets. Live TV has no posters to build a mosaic from, so the **Poster collage** background is unavailable there — and if you had already chosen a collage and then switched the target to Live TV, the background silently changed back to **Image** without a word. The option is now greyed out with a line explaining why, in all three languages, so the change no longer happens behind your back. Nothing else about how covers render has changed.

Adds **Spanish**. The whole configuration page — every step, label, button, hint and message, plus the server's upload and validation errors — is now translated, joining English and Dutch. The page follows your Jellyfin display language, and regional variants come along for the ride: `es-MX` and `es-419` get Spanish just like `es-ES`. Alongside it, the translation files themselves were **cleaned up and put under test**. Roughly a hundred strings left behind by the v3 editor rewrite were still being carried (and would have had to be translated into every new language) — those are gone, and five new build-time checks now fail if a language drifts out of sync with English, if a `{0}` placeholder goes missing, or if a string is defined but never shown. No change to how covers look or render.

Adds an **overlay gradient** to the Background step — a colour that fades in over your background and sits under your text. It is the missing piece behind the look where a poster **resolves into a solid band of colour** at the bottom, with the title on top of it and readable no matter what the poster shows underneath. Each colour stop has its own **opacity**, so you can go from fully transparent to fully solid, use **two colours** for a duotone fade, or wash the whole cover. Four **presets** — Bottom fade, Top fade, Full wash and Duotone — get you there in one click, and switching between them keeps the colours you have already picked so you can try all four without losing your palette. The **Auto palette** swatches now recolour the selected overlay stop, so you can tint a cover with a colour taken straight out of its own artwork. The overlay works with every background type — image, poster collage, gradient or solid — and with animated covers. Existing designs and saved templates are unaffected and render exactly as before.
