versions.changelog:
Hotfix for 1.0.8.0 — the Issues tab went blank and unresponsive on servers with substantial history.

Root cause: the new per-row "last attempt" lookup in 1.0.8.0 ran a correlated subquery against the history table with no supporting index. On loaded databases the query stalled long enough that Jellyfin tore down the request scope mid-flight, which crashed MVC's result serializer with ObjectDisposedException — the Issues tab silently rendered empty and every button that depended on live issue data felt dead.

Schema v11 adds a covering index on history(issue_id, dry_run, fixed_at_utc). Non-destructive migration: SQLite builds the index from existing rows. No rescan, no history loss, no re-queue needed.

Measured ~450x speed-up on the correlated query (approx 5000ms -> approx 15ms per 500-id chunk on a 48k-row history), and GET /MediaDash/Issues?openOnly=true now returns a steady HTTP 200 instead of timing out and 500ing. 1526 / 1526 tests green.

Fixes #80.

Protection: right-click (or long-press) in the Files tab to protect any file/folder from scans and fixes, or push one into the issue queue.

"Original language" option added to audio/subtitle pickers. (#78)

Format converters for images, music and video (RMVB → MKV), with a first-run wizard step to enable them.

SMART monitoring is disable-able per server via right-click on the SMART pill. (#60)

Per-fixer disable toggle in Settings → Fix order.

Playability: catches damaged secondary audio tracks; books and comics refused with a doc-aware message; audio files with cover art no longer false-flagged. (#75, #76)

Repair + conversion safety: source identity captured before encoding, output verified against source duration/stream count, audiobook merges won't overwrite an existing .m4b. Alternate audio tracks preserved on RMVB → MKV remuxes.

Scanning: Photos library now covered; Overview breakdown includes Music/Books/Photos; `.txt` books aren't flagged as orphans; respects Enabled Libraries setting.

Cross-volume moves refuse symlinks/junctions and verify inventory before deleting the source.

Many UI fixes across Issues tab, Settings, Overview and Recycle. "Reset scan data" preserves Queued/Dismissed decisions.

Light-mode: Files-tab right-click menu and Protect dialog are now readable under the Light theme.

Calibre: no longer hangs on verbose installers; paths with spaces work; override path changes picked up without restart.

Hotfix for 1.0.7.6 Playability false-positives.

• Removed the bitrate-vs-size pre-filter that flagged efficient x264 rips (YIFY / small MP4 rips of Severance / Landman / Rage / Outlander at 400 MB–2.4 GB) as size-truncated. Decode-check already catches genuine tail-truncation with far fewer false positives.

• DRM detection: encrypted MP4/M4V/M4A/MOV (Fairplay / Widevine / PlayReady) detected via codec_tag_string=encv/enca and skipped instead of mis-flagged.

• Folder-based library items (BDMV / VIDEO_TS / mounted-ISO / BDRemux) no longer reported as missing files.

Anyone on 1.0.7.6 should update — the 1.0.7.6 repair ladder would try to salvage these false positives and recycle files that failed repair.

753 / 753 tests green. 15 / 15 real-file torture-test variants still recover end-to-end.

Repair broken files ladder (quick remux → drop broken streams → container coerce → re-encode) + F-014/015/016 malformed-row robustness sweep (dashboard, PlayabilityFixer, HasBlockingWarnings + 6 other JSON readers hardened) + Media Grouper year-suffix fix for TV reboots (#43 Doctor Who, Silo) + Track fix VobSub/PGS/DVB consent gate for MP4-family (#56) + Track/Playability/Transcode fixers widened to UnauthorizedAccessException on SMB/NFS/FUSE (#59) + Recycle bin 5 GB soft-warn for Proxmox LXC / Docker bind-mount (#58) + Errors tab: correct labels for pauses / skips / malformed-row / ffmpeg-on-corrupt-source + stable FNV-1a dedup + 10-minute review grace + plain-language messages everywhere.

753 / 753 tests green. 15 / 15 real-file torture-test variants recover end-to-end. One binary for Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.
Fix window + Low system impact mode + HW-accelerated re-encodes + Show ignored issues + one-per-session fix-run alert + midnight scan default + Media Grouper collision guard + Errors badge accuracy

1.0.7.4 is a small follow-up to 1.0.7.3's combined audio + subtitle cleanup pass, closing the last case where MediaDash could ffmpeg the same file twice in one fix run.

When a file had a queued re-encode AND queued track cleanup (unwanted audio or subtitle languages), it used to remux for the tracks first and then re-encode a second time. The re-encode already drops unwanted tracks by itself, so the first remux was wasted work — and if it didn't run first, it would fail with "nothing to remove" once the re-encode had finished. Now the fix run detects the overlap and lets the re-encode handle both jobs in one pass. Same recycle bin entry, one history row per issue, both track and quality issues flip to Fixed together.

User-visible impact: multi-language 4K remuxes that also need size reduction finish in half the time, and the Errors tab stops picking up spurious "nothing to remove" failures on files that were just re-encoded.

594 / 594 tests green. One binary for Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

1.0.7.3 addresses the loudest bug reports from GitHub issues and the r/jellyfin + r/JellyfinCommunity threads.

Recycle bin: overhauled with rich per-row metadata (BinPath, Provenance, Reason, IssueType, ActionText, RestoreHint, auto-purge countdown), origin-manifest sidecars so restores survive history loss, cross-volume consolidation of legacy bin locations, non-destructive restore that suffixes -restored instead of overwriting, and a 3 GB / 5 GB free-space floor that pauses fix runs and refuses config save on a full bin volume. New endpoints: /RecycleBin/OtherBins, /RecycleBin/Consolidate, /RecycleBin/DiskInfo.

Duplicate detection: keys now include ProductionYear so remakes stop collapsing (#3), keeper picker excludes symlinks and 0-byte files (F-098), DuplicateMinAgeDays default 7 to 0 with one INFO line naming vetoed count.

Fixer output: TrackFixer + TranscodeFixer restore source CreationTimeUtc and LastWriteTimeUtc so Recently-Added stays honest (#31); dry-run stale-failure path no longer flips vanished files to Fixed; per-sidecar history fan-out via FixResult.AdditionalRecycled gives every recycled sidecar its own Restore button; subtitle-provider quota mid-run is now detected and handled quietly.

Playability: cross-checks ffprobe format_name against extension so an MKV renamed .mp3 emits container-extension-mismatch (F-213). HasTruncationMarker no longer treats the benign Truncating packet warning as truncation - that warning fires on real-world MKV cluster boundaries, MPEG-TS packet alignment, and MP4 mdat overlap on files that play fine in Jellyfin (Reddit reports: friskyapple, oogoom, moonplaza, Commercial-Camp-8052). Only File ended prematurely now counts.

TrackFixer ffmpeg command gains -fflags +genpts at input and -avoid_negative_ts make_zero at output - fixes the mpegts sample rate not set / Could not write header failure on Blu-ray-derived .m2ts sources, and lets OutputVerifier accept legitimate long-form duration drift (#39, slack widened from fixed 2 s to max(2 s, dur x 2 percent)).

Combined ffmpeg pass (#28, #32): FixTask now detects same-file AudioLanguage + SubtitleLanguage pairs before the fix loop and routes them through a new TrackFixer.FixCombinedAsync so one ffmpeg drops both categories in a single pass instead of two back-to-back remuxes. Two history rows recorded, one bin entry, both issues flip to Fixed.

SMART noise dedup: SmartHealthProbeWmi caches per-drive-letter WMI failures and SmartHealthProbe caches per-device smartctl timeout / IO / non-zero-exit failures. First failure per device per session still emits the diagnostic; subsequent failures on the same device are suppressed until restart. Addresses the Errors-tab spam on NVMe + mount-point setups (#38, #23).

Files: new read-only Jellyfin logs shortcut at the file-browser root supporting listing + per-file download so users can attach logs to bug reports; ApiKey= param renamed from api_key= for Jellyfin 10.10+ compatibility.

Diagnostics: Copy diagnostics button relabelled Report an issue (copies diagnostics + opens issue tracker in a new tab).

One binary for Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

Reliability hotfix: fixes the "13 files locked, nothing holding them" report class by switching every scanner/probe (ArtworkScanner, NfoScanner, TrickplayOptimizeScanner, BookProbeService, FileHasher) from File.OpenRead (default FileShare.Read blocks concurrent moves/deletes on Windows and shows up as ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION 32) to a new MediaFileHelper.OpenSharedRead helper using FileShare.ReadWrite | Delete. Also splits FixTask's catch-all "disk error" into four accurate diagnostic keys — FixTask.FileMissing (marks issue Fixed so retry stops), FixTask.FileLocked (sharing violation post-retry), FixTask.DiskFull (real ENOSPC only, HResult 112/39/28), residual FixTask.IOError; every bucket gets a new Errors-tab entry with actionable copy. Adds a 5s per-library-root probe to ScanTask so a hard-mounted dead NFS/SMB share can't hang the ThreadPool and force LXC restarts — unreachable roots are skipped with a diagnostic pointing at soft,timeo=30,retrans=3 mount flags. Cleans up Ffmpeg.Timeout noise on Blu-ray remuxes: TrackFixer's 30-min first pass no longer surfaces to Errors (only the 5-hour retry's failure does), Track.RemuxRetry diagnostic removed as it fired on the happy path. New README Uninstall section explaining the remove-repo -> uninstall -> restart sequence so Jellyfin's Update Plugins task can't race the deleteOnStartup marker. Still one binary for both Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

Hotfix: startup purge of stale SmartHealth.Wmi diagnostics — upgraders from v1.0.6 kept seeing the benign 'No MSFT_StorageReliabilityCounter association found' and 'PowerShell counter fallback ran' rows even though v1.0.7's code stopped emitting them (the rows were persisted in the SQLite diagnostics table and reloaded on every boot). Post-v1.0.7 polish rolling in: file browser gains a read-only Recycle bin shortcut at the pseudo-root; every RecycleBin.LegacyBatchNeedsReview diagnostic on the Errors tab now carries a 'Merge into current bin' button that writes the ownership marker + purges the stale row so the card drops on the next refresh; new POST /MediaDash/RecycleBin/AdoptBatch endpoint backs it. tools/release.ps1 now accepts 4-part hotfix versions and pins gh release create --target to the local HEAD SHA — v1.0.7's tag landed on the PR #11 merge because release.ps1 was letting gh default to the remote's default-branch head. Still one binary for Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

Recycle-bin ownership marker + file-browser TOCTOU re-validation + timestamp width fix (from PR #11) + lazy legacy-adoption gate + zero-byte marker. New Settings: 'Pause fixes when the bin reaches N GB' size cap and 'Reset scheduled task' button (FixTaskSeeded flag makes ScheduleMigrator seed once instead of fighting the user on every restart). Hearing-impaired subtitle mode protects SDH/CC in the SubtitleLanguage scanner and treats HI as the required format for MissingSubtitles. SubtitleIgnoreRateLimit toggle routes provider searches through the manual-UI path. System Performance card show/hide preference. Canonical MediaFormats + SubtitleFormats extension sets. OrphanCleanupScanner rework with 186 new test lines. Windows SMART: per-model negative cache stops the ~1s PowerShell fallback re-spawning every 10 min for drives Windows won't populate; benign 'no reliability counter' diagnostics no longer spam Errors. UI polish: language chips 52->27 px, task-header pill matches sibling button height, hearing-impaired description trimmed. tools/deploy-local.ps1 auto-discovers plugin folder per ABI. i18n regenerated across 9 languages. Still one binary for Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

# Release v0.7.2.0                                                                                                                                                                                                              
Dieses Update verbessert die Suchfunktion um datumsbasierte Kriterien, ermöglicht Testläufe (Dry Run) ohne konfigurierten Speicherpfad und beinhaltet wichtige interne Strukturverbesserungen sowie Fehlerbehebungen bei der Titelverarbeitung.                                                                                                                                                                                                            

## ⚠️ Wichtige Hinweise                                                                                                                                                                                                          
*   **Kein Downgrade empfohlen:** Aufgrund von Änderungen am Speicherformat für Suchanfragen (Queries) sollte nach diesem Update kein Downgrade auf eine ältere Version durchgeführt werden. Die alte Version wird die gespeicherten Daten nicht mehr korrekt lesen können.                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
## 🚀 Neue Funktionen                                                                                                                                                                                                            
*   **Suche nach Datum:** Die Suche wurde erweitert, um Inhalte gezielt nach Datum finden zu können.                                                                                                                      
*   **Dry Run ohne Pfad:** Der Simulationsmodus (Dry Run) kann nun ausgeführt werden, selbst wenn kein Download-Pfad in den Einstellungen hinterlegt ist.                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
## 🛠️ Verbesserungen & Refactoring                                                                                                                                                                                              
*   **API-Entkopplung:** Die interne Anwendungslogik wurde von den externen Datenmodellen der MediathekViewWeb-API entkoppelt. Dies verbessert die Wartbarkeit und Architektur des Plugins (#83).

## Release v0.7.1.0

###  Dieses Update führt ein völlig neues System zur Pfadverwaltung ein, macht die Suche deutlich mächtiger und verbessert die Benutzererfahrung durch eine direkte Videovorschau.

 ## 🚀 Neue Funktionen
   * Kontextbasiertes Pfad-Management: Anstelle eines einzigen globalen Download-Ordners können nun spezifische Standardpfade für verschiedene Mediathek-Inhalte festgelegt werden:
       * Filme & Serien: Getrennte Basisordner ermöglichen eine saubere, automatische Integration in die jeweilige Jellyfin-Bibliothek.
       * Abonnements & Manuelle Downloads: Eigene Zielverzeichnisse sorgen für eine bessere Organisation Ihrer Medien.
   * Direkte Videovorschau (Play-Button): Suchergebnisse verfügen nun über einen Play-Button. Damit lassen sich die MP4-Direktlinks der Sender sofort im Browser öffnen, um Inhalte vor dem Download kurz zu sichten.
   * Intelligente Sucherweiterung:
       * Kombinierte Abfragen: Die Suche erlaubt nun die gleichzeitige Eingabe von Titel und Thema, um Treffer in großen Mediatheken (z.B. ARD/ZDF) präziser einzugrenzen.
       * Auto-Pre-Fill: Der Dialog für erweiterte Downloads wird jetzt automatisch mit erkannten Metadaten und Pfadvorschlägen (basierend auf der Videoanalyse) vorausgefüllt.
       * Optimierte Eingabe: Suchfelder wachsen nun dynamisch mit dem Text mit (auto-grow).
   * UI-Verbesserungen: Die Standard-Pfadeinstellungen in der Konfiguration sind jetzt einklappbar, um die Übersichtlichkeit zu erhöhen.

 ## 🛠️ Verbesserungen & Refactoring
   * Restrukturierung der Web-UI: Komplette Trennung von HTML-Struktur und JavaScript-Logik zur Verbesserung der Wartbarkeit und Ladezeiten.
   * Robuste Verzeichniserstellung: Die Logik zur automatischen Erstellung von Jellyfin-konformen Ordnerstrukturen wurde grundlegend verbessert.
   * Metadaten-Logik: Verfeinerte Integration von DuckDuckGo und TMDB-Suchen für eine bessere Zuordnung von Postern und Beschreibungen.

 ## 🐞 Bugfixes
   * Sicherheits-Update: Implementierung eines Schutzes gegen Path-Traversal-Angriffe bei der manuellen Pfadeingabe für Downloads.
   * Stabilität: Behebung von Fehlern in den Unit-Tests, die durch die Umstellung auf das neue Pfad-Schema entstanden waren.

* feat: Optional automatic folder creation and UI-Improvments, More by @CatNoir2006 in https://github.com/CatNoir2006/jellyfin-plugin-MediathekViewDL/pull/81


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/CatNoir2006/jellyfin-plugin-MediathekViewDL/compare/v0.7.0.0...v0.7.1.0

## Release Notes (v0.6.1.0 -> v0.7.0.0)

 #### Dieses Update verbessert die Stabilität und erweitert die Download-Möglichkeiten.

  ### 🚀 Neue Funktionen

   * M3U8-Support: Das Plugin lädt nun M3U8-Streams direkt herunter. Das erhöht die Kompatibilität mit vielen Sendern.
   * Audio-Extraktion: Tonspuren werden jetzt direkt aus dem Web extrahiert. Das spart Zeit und Datenvolumen.
   * OV-Sprache: In Abos kannst du eine Standardsprache für OV-Inhalte festlegen (z. B. 'eng').
   * Temp-Pfad: Der Pfad für temporäre Dateien ist nun frei konfigurierbar.
   * Bereinigung: Ein neuer Task löscht beim Start automatisch alte temporäre Dateien.
   * HTTP-Option: Downloads über HTTP können nun explizit erlaubt werden.

 ### 🛠️ Verbesserungen

   * Neues System: Die Download-Logik wurde für mehr Stabilität komplett modernisiert.
   * FFmpeg-Anzeige: Vorgänge wie M3U8-Downloads zeigen nun genaue Prozentwerte an.
   * Fehlerschutz: Automatische Wiederholungen (via Polly) machen Downloads zuverlässiger.
   * Jellyfin 10.11: Das Plugin wurde auf die neueste Jellyfin-Version aktualisiert.
   * Speicherprüfung: Die Prüfung des freien Speicherplatzes arbeitet nun genauer.
   * Doku: Die README wurde überarbeitet und enthält nun Bilder und neue Anleitungen.

 ### 🐞 Fehlerbehebungen

   * Gebärdensprache: Diese Inhalte werden nun korrekt immer als Video geladen.
   * Task-Trigger: Die Zeitpläne wurden an aktuelle API-Standards angepasst.

Mind the Gaps.description: Scans your library for gaps (missing movies in partially-owned collections and franchises, missing series content, unowned titles from actor and director filmographies, and related recommendations) using TMDB, Trakt, TheTVDB, and TVmaze, with music and book sources (MusicBrainz, OpenLibrary, Discogs), and reads the watchlists and want-lists you already keep on those sites. Presents an easy todo list for filling out your collection, diagnoses why a title is reported missing, surfaces where to watch each item, and can optionally mint native virtual placeholders for missing items.
Mind the Gaps.overview: Find what's missing and related in your library and build a todo list to complete it.

versions.changelog: 10.11.11.0 - Want to watch gains three options, all off by default and all requiring the arrived-titles playlist (contributed by David Rappo, @rappo, in PR 21): the home row can lead with the titles already on your playlist, a title comes off the playlist once it is watched (a series once every episode is played), and a movie or series page gets a bookmark button among its own. Plugin rows are reachable with a TV remote's D-pad. Not interested, off by default, lets each user hide a title from their own Web UI pages without hiding it for anyone else. A user with a parental rating limit sees the Web UI sections narrowed to the titles that limit allows, rather than none of them. The home Discover row, the Want to watch row, and the item page rows each have a placement setting; existing settings carry over. The Gaps Report's toolbar is grouped by what each control acts on, every header has a select-all, a line above the list says how many rows the filters hide, and Add to TODO is now Add to watchlist. The report is usable at phone width, and the settings page has collapsible sections, a search, and better screen reader support. A new scheduled task, Prune gaps from deleted items, takes deleted library items out of the report: a gap they were the only source of is removed, and one with other sources moves to the next. It has no default schedule; it waits for a running scan, and a second scan waits for the first. Recommendation groups link to the owned title they came from. Books get an OpenLibrary id field and albums and artists a Discogs id field in the metadata editor, with a link on the item's page; a dedicated OpenLibrary or Discogs plugin takes over when installed. Links are built from each title's ids when the report loads, so a link plugin installed later applies everywhere. The report takes far less memory and disk (on a library with 83,000 gaps, about 1.6 GB down to 200 MB in memory and 245 MB down to 131 MB on disk), loads in about half the time, and is written far less often during scans and where-to-watch lookups. Existing reports convert on first load; a report saved by this version cannot be read by an earlier one, so going back shows an empty report until its next scan.

10.11.10.0 - The Maintenance section has a Fulfillment queue for an administrator who fetches titles by hand. It folds every user's TODO list into one row per title, sorted by how many people still want it, names who is still waiting, and shows the streaming-service icons as soon as the queue opens, with the same links a TODO row already has. Mark fetched closes the title for every requester in one action, and Verify all checks the queue against the library and closes a title you already have, however it arrived. With Everyone's watchlist on (off by default), that same household list is a Discover source and leads the Discover view of every domain it has entries for. Send to the acquisition stack is done from the Gaps Report. The report's Send action has a quality profile picker, filled from the stack's own profile list and preselecting the profile you configured, so an older title the default profile cannot find a release for can still be sent. The report's My TODO list popup is gone; the Fulfillment queue is where an administrator sees every list. The report's multi-select bar can Acquire, Request, or Resolve a checked batch (Resolve applies one shared note), alongside Mint and Add to TODO. An administrator can manage another user's want-to-watch list. With "Want to watch: move arrived titles into a playlist" on, a title that is in the library moves into that user's own Jellyfin playlist the next time it is verified, so it shows up in every client. The playlist is named Want to Watch unless you change it, and only a real file counts as arrived. Amazon and web-search links for a book or album include the author or artist, on the report, the Web UI, and the Fulfillment queue. TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and OpenLibrary subjects are set with the same chip pickers the other curated sources use. A book's dialog loads its description from OpenLibrary when you open it. Studio pages, off by default, add a Missing from the studio row of that studio's movies you do not own, on the list page you open from a movie's studio credit. A library that sets a metadata fetcher order keeps TVmaze in the series check. TVmaze is not a Jellyfin metadata fetcher, so it is always asked and ranked last.

10.11.9.0 - Mind the Gaps now reaches into Jellyfin's own pages through an experimental, opt-in Web UI, with a master switch and one toggle per surface in settings, all off by default. A person's page lists what they made that you do not own, a movie or series page suggests titles like it that you are missing, an artist's page lists the albums you do not have, and a book page or an author's own page lists more by the same author. The home page can show a Discover row of the recommendations your scans found from titles you own and from lists that are public by nature (TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and TMDB's own feeds), never from a watchlist, wantlist, favorites, or a personal list. Click a card for a detail dialog with TMDB's synopsis, genres, runtime, rating, a trailer link, and a link to the title's JustWatch page, then send it to Radarr or Sonarr with the quality profile you pick; the dialog and the card grids can be driven from a keyboard or a TV remote. A user with a parental rating limit is shown none of these sections. With Want to watch turned on, every card carries a bookmark that adds the title to your own list, and the home page can show a Want to watch row of what you have listed and do not yet own. The TODO list is now kept per user, in the plugin's data folder, and removed when the user is deleted; the first administrator to open the old shared list takes it over, and an administrator can switch the report's TODO to everyone's lists to see and manage them. The Gaps Report loads faster: it fetches one tab at a time as slim rows, fetches a row's details only when you open it, revalidates what it already holds instead of downloading it again, and loads its script and stylesheet as separately cached files; the saved report is stored as one file per domain, and an existing report is converted automatically. A row shows up to two streaming-service icons, following your provider and monetization filters and wearing the service's logo (a service TMDB lists as several providers, such as a "with Ads" tier, shows as one icon and one provider filter entry), and clicking them opens the title's TMDB watch page. Gaps left behind by a source you have since removed or turned off are pruned on every scan, and a Prune stale gaps button under Maintenance does it right away. A TMDB list that cannot be read, such as a private one, no longer stops the other lists from being scanned, filling in a large library's series content is done in batches, and the scan log says how long each source took. New, and off by default: the report and the Web UI can load their posters, covers, and streaming-service logos through your server instead of each browser fetching them from TMDB and the other providers. Turn on "Keep the pages' images on this server" in the new Images section of settings; the server fetches each image once, from a fixed list of provider hosts only, keeps it under its cache folder, and sends the browser on to the provider whenever it cannot serve one, and a "Trim the image cache" scheduled task keeps the cache to the size you set (500 MB by default).

10.11.8.0 - The Gaps Report is reorganized around your library's domains: Movies, Shows, Music, and Books are now the primary tabs, each badged with its own gap count, with Set completion, Creator works, and Discover scoped underneath as a view you pick per domain, so only the active domain's data is loaded at a time. A Compact view toggle switches to a denser layout. Click a title to expand its detail in place: the overview, where to watch, and (outside Compact view) every information and action button tile inline instead of opening separate popovers; collapsed, the same actions live behind three icon popovers on the row, and a collapsed title's own browser tooltip shows its overview with no click at all. The toolbar is split into a filter row and an action row, and the settings page is reorganized into one collapsible section per provider (TMDB, Trakt, MDBList, Discogs, OpenLibrary, TheTVDB, IMDb, JustWatch), each badged on or off, with a search box that opens whichever section matches. Four new TMDB feeds, Top Rated, Popular, Upcoming, and Now Playing, can be turned on individually under Discover, and Jellyfin 12.0 is now a supported target alongside 10.11, each release building and shipping its own ABI-matched package. Gaps now show real cover art for books (bibliography and subject lists), music (MusicBrainz discography and artist works), and series completion episodes (TMDB, TheTVDB, and TVmaze all supply a still where they have one) instead of a blank thumbnail, falling back to the placeholder rather than a broken-image icon when a cover fails to load; MDBList entries carry a poster and description like every other source. A creator's page can be trimmed further with a minimum TMDB vote count for a movie credit and a minimum episode count for a TV credit. The TODO list shows an image and release date per entry. Sending a whole-series gap to Sonarr from a filmography, recommendation, or favorites entry sends the series' own title rather than the name of whatever surfaced it, and a rejected Radarr, Sonarr, or Jellyseerr request shows the service's validation message instead of a raw response body.

It is now built against 10.11.0 and loads on any 10.11.x server. The identification audit reports series whose episodes are split across two folders that map to the same season, listing each folder and its episode count so you can see which one to keep. The gaps report and the settings are separate dashboard pages now: the report opens without the settings form attached, the plugin's Settings button opens the settings, and resetting the scan rotation and removing minted items move to a Maintenance section on the report, beside the library they act on. Shared report links and exported audit dossiers still open the report. Missing Episodes.description: Scan your Jellyfin library, Sonarr, or TMDB for missing TV episodes and send them to Sonarr.
Missing Episodes.overview: Finds the gaps in your TV library with three scan sources (Jellyfin virtual items, Sonarr, TMDB) plus a gap-detection fallback, a clean per-show detail view, bulk Sonarr search, an Ignored list, scan history, live progress, and a sidebar entry.

versions.changelog:
Scan efficiency overhaul. UI is unchanged.
- Sonarr per-series episode fetches now parallel (8 in flight). 100-show library ~8s sequential RTT -> ~1s.
- Jellyfin-mode Sonarr enrichment parallelized the same way.
- TMDB season fetches parallelized (4 in flight, well under TMDB's rate budget).
- ApplySonarrHasFile rewritten O(N*M) -> O(N). HashSet + List.RemoveAll instead of repeated List.Remove; seasons indexed once.
- ignoredTvdb HashSet hoisted out of per-series loop.
- JSON persistence switched to async I/O (WriteAllTextAsync).
Output is identical for identical input — pure internal refactor.

Editorial Revamp UI with Classic toggle.
- New Classic/Revamp segmented toggle in the hero. Old look stays exactly as it was; flip to Revamp for a full editorial overhaul (magazine spread, not dashboard). Preference saved per-browser.
- Revamp direction: ribbon hero with eyebrow + giant missing-count numeral hoisted via grid-template-areas, terminal-style `>` prompt search, vertical timeline scan history with circular dots, premiere-poster billboard cards (no chrome), chapter-numbered season heads via CSS counter, episode codes typeset as tracked-out mono eyebrows, settings card with mono uppercase labels.
- All Revamp rules scoped to #missingEpisodesPage[data-me-style=revamp] so the v1.0.8 Classic look is fully preserved.
- Fix: locked Search button tooltip on TMDB-detected episodes (Id=0) used to say 'Configure Sonarr to enable searching' even when Sonarr was configured. Tooltip now distinguishes 'Sonarr not configured' vs 'Not tracked by Sonarr'.

Final security pass + README refresh.
- Removed the /debug/parse diagnostic endpoint. Served its purpose chasing the Office/TMNT bug; no longer part of the public API surface.
- Dropped the FileScan log line from Information to Debug. Doesn't leak filesystem paths into the default Jellyfin logs anymore.
- README updated to document the three-layer accuracy model (Jellyfin / filename parse / Sonarr hasFile), pure-Jellyfin mode tradeoffs, and the full security posture.

- Accuracy: when 'Only monitored' is on, TMDB mode used to count every TMDB-listed episode as expected even if Sonarr had it unmonitored. Now drops unmonitored entries from the missing list during Sonarr enrichment, trimming 'phantom missing' episodes the user never wanted tracked.
- UI: the Jellyfin method explainer now mentions when Sonarr enrichment is active — surfaces the hasFile fallback so it's not invisible magic.

Fix scattered-folder case (TMNT-style): files exist on disk under Sonarr-managed per-season folders that neither Jellyfin's path nor Sonarr's series.Path cover. Enrichment now uses Sonarr's per-episode hasFile flag as ground truth — any missing entry Sonarr knows is already on disk gets dropped, season Have bumps, and series with everything now present fall out of the missing list automatically.

Actually fix the Office/TMNT accuracy bug.
- Root cause: when Jellyfin's cached series.Path was stale (points at an empty folder after files moved) and Sonarr tracked the correct path, my filename parser walked Jellyfin's empty path and returned 0 episodes. Enrichment later overwrote Size/Path with Sonarr's values but by then present/missing counts were already wrong.
- Fix: in Jellyfin-mode scans the plugin now pre-fetches Sonarr's series list (if configured), and when Jellyfin's path has 0 files/0 bytes it retries the parser against Sonarr's path for the same show (matched by TVDB id). The better result wins.
- Added a /debug/parse diagnostic endpoint + scan log line for future debugging.

Real accuracy fix.
- Rewrote ProcessJellyfinSeriesAsync around a clean present/expected separation. Filename-parsed episodes now correctly land in the present set without double-counting with TMDB's expected set.
- Previously: shows like The Office read as 0/186 even though the folder had 144GB of correctly-named S##E## files because filename merge was running AFTER partial stat accumulation and TMDB mode was then double-counting Total. Now stats are computed once, at the end, from |present| and |expected ∪ present|.
- Stale last-result.json from prior versions is naturally overwritten on the first 1.0.4 scan.

Accuracy fix + security hardening.
- Jellyfin scans now walk the series folder and parse S##E## / 1x05 patterns from filenames. Catches episodes that are on disk but Jellyfin's library never imported (was showing shows with 144 GB of files as 0/186).
- XSS hardening: image URLs for posters/backdrops/thumbnails now set via JS with JSON.stringify escaping instead of inline style interpolation — can't break out of the url() literal.
- Large internal refactor: the full Jellyfin scan now delegates per-series to the same helper the rescan-one button uses. No duplicated logic.
- README rewritten with AchievementBadges-style copy-paste install block and security section.

- Progress strip now shows during a single-show rescan (it was hidden because it lived inside the list-view container).
- Click an ignored show to open its detail view; dedicated 'Remove from ignore list' button replaces the old confirm prompt.
- README updated with new features and a note about the harmless 'error occurred while getting plugin details' warning for manually-installed copies.

- Per-show rescan no longer triggers a full library scan in Jellyfin mode (was doing a full scan and returning one entry).
- Rescan now uses Sonarr's tvdbId-indexed series lookup (one call instead of a full dump) and runs under the shared progress tracker, so the UI progress strip fills in during a rescan.
- Size chip moved inside the poster — no longer overlaps the meta row.
- Smarter path reconciliation: prefer Jellyfin's path when its folder has content, fall back to Sonarr when Jellyfin's path is stale / empty.

Moonbase.description: Moonbase is the Moonfin server plugin for Jellyfin, powering settings sync, the Moonfin Web app at /Moonfin/Web/, a built-in theme editor with custom theme APIs, media bar and ratings integrations, and Seerr proxy/SSO with admin defaults and broadcasts across Moonfin clients.

versions.changelog:
Moonbase 2.4.0 is the server side of Moonfin 2.7.0. It builds the new seasonal Home row, gives custom rows each title's rating and holds them to parental limits, gets large MDBList rows loading, and matches anime with non-English library titles. It also syncs the settings the new clients added and bundles the Moonfin 2.7.0 web app.

Features:

- A seasonal Home row of holiday movies a user owns, plus Seerr suggestions, for New Year's, Valentine's Day, Easter, Pride, Halloween, Thanksgiving, Christmas, Lunar New Year and Diwali. Clients turn it on, and a new Moonfin Seasonal Keywords Sync task fills in TMDB keywords using the server-wide TMDB key.
- Custom row items carry the TMDB certification, overview, genres and runtime, and rows fetched with a user's own TMDB or MDBList key are cached for that user.
- The bottom bar style and tabs, the Friends button, detail screen sections and seasonal effect density now sync, with admin defaults for the bottom bar, the Friends button, the new seasonal effects, density, the seasonal row and the Great-Grandparents interface size.
- The bundled web app moves up to Moonfin 2.7.0, with friends and chat from the Achievement Badges plugin, the seasonal row and new seasonal effects, a remote control D-pad, Live TV recovery, Library Order and detail screen sections.

Bug Fixes:

- Anime markers match series whose library title isn't English or romaji.
- New request notifications reach every Seerr request manager by default.
- Large MDBList rows load, since the server keeps resolving them after the app gives up.
- TMDB TV chart rows open the right show instead of a movie with the same id.
- Custom rows respect each user's parental limit. Set a server-wide TMDB key, or limited users get empty MDBList, IMDb and Letterboxd rows.
- Jellyfin Enhanced's header buttons stop opening Moonfin Web.
- In the web app, Seerr notifications reach the browser, Seerr rows load without an eight second wait after sign-in, subtitles set to Off stay off, and home rows stop going blank on Firefox.

Moonbase 2.3.0 adds the backend for anime markers, scores recommendations on the server, and keeps a backup of its settings with a restore button. It fixes message text that could wipe every plugin setting on a restart, gets the scheduled tasks running on their own again on Jellyfin 10.11 and 12, and bundles the Moonfin 2.6.0 web app.

Features:

- Anime markers flag filler, mixed, canon and recap episodes using the Anime Filler List and Tenrai, and mark Subbed or Dubbed from the audio in your own files. It's off by default, under Integrations.
- Recommendations are scored on the server. On Jellyfin 12 that scoring plugs into Jellyfin's own similar items so every client gets it, and a switch under Integrations hands it back to Jellyfin.
- Moonbase keeps a backup of its server settings and offers to restore it if they ever come back reset.
- Clients can show when a series airs next through the server, even without Sonarr.
- Admin defaults for the metadata row, the loading animation, the screensaver, the new detail screen styles, Seerr missing collection items and availability badges, the Downloads and Live TV buttons, the Rate action button, fallback audio and subtitle languages, and the Grandparents interface size.
- The bundled web app moves up to Moonfin 2.6.0, with the Spotlight, Nouveau and Minimalist detail screens, Kids Mode, Achievement Badges, a redone Live TV guide, and fonts that no longer load from Google.

Bug Fixes:

- Message text can no longer corrupt the settings file, which Jellyfin answered by resetting every setting and sometimes removing the plugin on the next start.
- Applying defaults only changes what the admin actually set.
- Scheduled tasks run on their own on Jellyfin 10.11 and 12, and custom home rows now refresh daily.
- Notifications, the media bar and genre lists stop showing items a user isn't allowed to see.
- Hidden Continue Watching and Next Up items stay hidden on every device.
- Retro game artwork is far more reliable on large libraries, and PSP games can start in Moonfin Web once the new isolation checkbox under Retro Games is on.
- The Moonfin header button shows in the Jellyfin 12 web UI.

Moonbase 2.2.0 adds server messages, so an admin can write something once and have it show up in people's apps even when they were offline while it was sent. The admin defaults page grows a lot, with settings for another 96 options and fixes to the six controls that were writing values no client reads. Retro games find more of their artwork, and it now picks up new ROMs without a restart. A reinstalled Seerr no longer strands you logged out, and a zipped game now arrives as the ROM it actually is. The bundled web client moves up to Moonfin 2.5.1.

Features:

- A new Messages tab lets an admin write a message with a title and a Markdown body, pick a colour, choose how it shows up, pick who sees it, schedule a start and end date, add a link button, and order the list. Broadcast now saves what it sends, so a user who was offline still finds it.
- Admin defaults picked up settings for another 96 options, covering discovery rows, Since You Watched, music rows, sort direction for the home rows, player buttons, media segments, Cinema Mode for episodes, and a lot more.
- Six admin controls that were writing values no client reads now send the right ones, and row sorting was rebuilt to match the clients, which also adds the missing Playlist Order option.
- Retro games now watch the configured game library folders for file changes, so a new ROM or a per-library scan runs artwork reconciliation in the background instead of waiting for a restart, and games that came out as a false miss are retried once the matching has corrected them.
- The settings sync toggle was renamed to Moonbase Sync, and its description now says that enabling it is required for the Seerr and ratings integrations.
- The bundled web client picks up everything web relevant from Moonfin 2.5.1, including the messages window, a Seerr poster grid with a download progress bar, remote subtitle badges, Play and Resume on the long press menu, and personal ratings writing to Emby.

Bug Fixes:

- A reinstalled Seerr no longer strands you logged out. The plugin was reading every 403 as missing admin rights, so the stale session was never cleared. Now it checks whether Seerr still knows the session first, and a definite refusal clears the old session and signs in again.
- A zipped game now arrives as the ROM it actually is. The detail was naming the archive, so a client saved plain ROM bytes under a .zip name and failed to unpack them. It now names the file the endpoint actually sends, along with its real size.
- A pending artwork timer can no longer take the process down on shutdown, and the artwork delivery route rejects an unknown role instead of falling through.
- The websocket reconnects after a server restart, a busy server no longer reads as a connection timeout, and Escape closes the dialog on top instead of the page behind it.

Moonbase 2.1.0 is mostly about the retro games backend, plus a personal ratings API, audiobook bookmark sync, and the bundled Moonfin web app at 2.5.0.

Features:

- Retro games: arcade ZIPs are validated offline against FBNeo and MAME DAT files, and admins can upload a DAT per core through the plugin.
- Retro games: ROMs are identified by their contents through the libretro RDB databases, with per game core and backend overrides.
- Retro games: a server side artwork pipeline with a manifest, per game artwork priority, and cached thumbnails at the requested size and format. Reconciliation runs on plugin startup and after every library scan.
- Retro games: delivery and per user concurrency limiters, a real Moonfin bridge for the EmulatorJS web player, and archive hashing capped at 512 MB per entry.
- A personal ratings endpoint serves the calling user's ratings in one response, so clients can sort and filter libraries by them.
- Audiobook bookmarks and notes are stored on the server and synced between clients.
- Clients can read their own transcode jobs, so transcoded downloads show real progress and an ETA.
- Settings sync covers everything Moonfin 2.5.0 added: HDR subtitle style, per segment skip actions, home row sort orders, the Studios row, spoiler free toggles, personal rating style, media type badges, segment auto hide, swipe gestures, scroll sensitivity, Cinema Mode for episodes, external trailers, and the crash report toggle.
- Admin defaults page: home row toggles with per row sorting defaults, Seerr Watchlist and Seerr shortcuts rows, the Aya media bar style, a Recently Released series type default, and pushing a genre, collection, or playlist row now enables its category toggle.
- The plugin reports itself as Moonbase throughout the dashboard.

Bug Fixes:

- TV studios get their logos, since TMDB networks are now read alongside production companies. Network ids are namespaced apart from company ids and the logo cache index is versioned.
- Seerr provisioning reports why it stopped instead of a bare status.
- IMDb charts stopped returning 403.
- Admin defaults: browsing and details blur defaults no longer fail the whole save, the theme music volume default is saved, and the Continue Watching image type options send values the client understands.

Web App:

- Bundles Moonfin 2.5.0 with the first run setup wizard, the Aya media bar, the full set of library sorts and filters, personal ratings, Seerr browse shortcuts, a Live TV favorites row, a Studio row, Live TV series recording, spoiler free toggles, an expanded metadata editor, Vim style playback keys, per segment skip actions, an HDR subtitle style, and crash reports sent to your own server.
- Fixes for playback control flicker, the skip button, subtitle offset range, Seerr row hover and localization, Continue Watching and Next Up paging, library search with Group By, blurry search posters, context menu placement, studio logo matching, media bar gradient flashing, backdrop fades, source pickers losing ids, book summaries, right to left layouts, and internationalized server domain names.

Features:

- Added a Playback tab to the admin defaults page, covering autoplay, audio and subtitle language, subtitle mode, skip lengths, intro action, still watching behavior, Next Up timeout, and rewind durations.
- Added default pickers for Action Buttons and Seerr Discovery row order.
- Added profile properties for OLED mode, the player time labels, and the new home row options, so those settings sync between devices.
- Game ROM and BIOS routes answer HEAD requests, which is how clients check a file's size before downloading it.

Bug Fixes:

- The Playback admin tab now writes the keys, values, and units clients actually read. Several pickers were saving under names no client looked for, so those defaults silently did nothing.
- Resume Rewind and Unpause Rewind options match what the client offers, instead of listing durations it has no setting for.
- Removed admin controls that no longer map to anything a client syncs. The underlying profile properties stay in place, so device to device sync is unaffected.
- Fixed the label text on the Details Screen Blur setting.

Features:

- Push notifications now reach Moonfin apps even when they're closed, covering Seerr activity, new media added to your library, and admin broadcasts. Admins can point at a self-hosted relay or their own FCM service account.
- Custom home rows sync across device profiles, so a row you build on one device shows up on the others, and edits and deletions carry over.
- Added a Max Days in Next Up setting.
- MDBList gained a Test Key button that shows your plan and remaining quota, a Clear Cache button, a max items limit for official lists, and Roger Ebert as a rating source.
- Added button layout sync so clients keep their player and details button layouts per device type.
- Glass and 8-bit Hero joined the admin default theme picker, along with the 8-bit Gold accent.

Bug Fixes:

- Fixed MDBList rows dropping shows, since the item cap was applied unevenly across the separate movie and show lists.
- Fixed Rotten Tomatoes critic scores never matching.
- MDBList rate limits are handled properly now, with your quota checked before syncing and partial results kept instead of overwriting good cached data.
- Ratings are filtered by the requesting device's profile instead of always using the global one.
- Fixed the Ping response casing that made clients report Seerr as not configured, and Emby media bar items now come back in the shape clients expect.
- Fixed the Emby plugin settings page never loading.
- Cancelling a Seerr request you don't have permission to cancel no longer logs you out of Seerr.
- The settings updated broadcast only fires when a save actually changed something, which stops sync loops between devices.
- Fixed the Seerr media available webhook breaking on some Jellyfin versions.

Features:

- Added password-less Seerr sign in through a Quick Connect bridge, so users who log in with Quick Connect get signed into Seerr silently.
- Added a server-side Radarr and Sonarr calendar proxy so clients can show upcoming release calendars, reachable for non-admin accounts too.
- Widened settings sync from 87 synced settings to 207, backed by new settings profile properties.
- Hardened game metadata matching with accent normalization and fuzzy suffix matching for better ROM artwork and details.
- On Emby, Moonfin web assets are now served with an explicit content type so the frontend loads correctly.
- The bundled Moonfin Web client moves up to the latest codebase, bringing a music overhaul with a Songs sublibrary and shuffle controls, a rebuilt downloads engine, a retro games library browser, Emby Skip Intro via chapter markers, and new detail and media bar controls.

Bug Fixes:

- Fixed profile corruption by writing user data atomically, with a healing pass for files corrupted before atomic writes shipped.
- Fixed Since You Watched rows for non-admin accounts by adding the server-wide API key fallback and stripping.
- Content hiding preferences now merge into the global profile instead of overwriting it.
- Fixed the Rotten Tomatoes critics rating mismatch coming from MDBList.
- Fixed Seerr sessions being evicted on 403 Forbidden responses, and stopped a failed auto-login leaving Seerr stuck as unavailable.
- Many bundled web fixes across music resume, subtitles, multi-server library browse, the media bar, Seerr requests, and focus handling.

Features:

- Moonbase now runs on Emby servers in addition to Jellyfin, bringing settings sync, the Seerr proxy, custom rows, and the rest of the plugin's backend to Emby.
- The bundled Moonfin Web client was rebuilt from the latest codebase, picking up the Modern details screen, fully custom home rows with external sources, the Seerr overhaul with SSO through the plugin, a full admin panel makeover, TV Mode on web, the Theme Store and new themes, music and book updates, and user scoped settings.
- A new Active Downloads dashboard tab shows running downloads with live transcode metrics and lets admins cancel jobs.
- Seerr push notifications with webhook provisioning and fan-out, covering request updates, approvals and denials, issue reports, and added to library notices.
- Added a retro games backend with ROM archive extraction and a games thumbnail endpoint that fetches and caches libretro art server side.
- Server-side caching for custom rows, IMDb lists, MDBList official lists enriched with TMDB posters, and TMDB studio logos.
- The full home layout can sync as sections, many more settings sync through the plugin, and applying settings to users now autosaves.
- New collection order endpoints, a library write-access check endpoint, and Jellyfin 12 compatibility via the ApiKey parameter.

Bug Fixes:

- Empty API keys sent by old clients no longer wipe stored keys during a settings merge.
- Fixed Seerr session cookie detection, the null user list when overwriting all user profiles, the Rotten Tomatoes Audience rating source mismatch, and the manifest structure.
- Many web client fixes covering track switching during transcoding, subtitles, Live TV across Jellyfin and Emby, Emby login and progress issues, pagination, overview text formatting, and theme focus colors.

Features:

- The web theme editor gained a random theme generator that builds a complete, coherent palette from a random base and accent hue, while keeping your theme id, name, and description. The theme id validation message was also clarified.

Bug Fixes:

- Media Bar trailers on web were reworked so YouTube trailer playback and advancing to the next slide now work correctly.
- Web playback sessions are now reported as stopped when you close or navigate away from the browser tab, using a page exit beacon, so they no longer linger as active on the server.
- The sidebar now follows desktop behavior in desktop browsers, instead of using the mobile layout.
- Preferences are now parsed and type coerced more robustly for web compatibility, fixing settings that could fail to load or save when stored as browser strings.
- The refresh rate switching and audio output mode settings are now hidden on the web build, where they do not apply.
- ASS and PGS subtitles now render correctly on web, with the necessary fonts bundled.

## Features

- Refreshed the Moonfin plugin, now called Moonbase, experience with the Moonfin Flutter web app, now served from `/Moonfin/Web/`.
- Replaced the older JavaScript overlay frontend with a proper web client bundled from the Flutter web project at the Moonfin-Core repo and theme assets for a smoother setup.
- Added a built-in theme editor at `/Moonfin/Web/theme/`, including admin-managed custom theme uploads and validation.
- Added discovery endpoints for plugin web startup: `/Moonfin/Discovery` and `/Moonfin/Discovery/discover`.
- Added custom theme APIs and services for listing, retrieving, uploading or replacing, deleting, and validating themes.
- Improved settings sync and admin tools with better global/profile behavior and admin broadcast support.

Native Trickplay.description:
Generates HLS I-frame variants so Apple TV / AVPlayer clients get native
scrubbing thumbnails on the transport bar — no client-side overlay needed.
One-time ffmpeg cost per item, then cached.
Includes a configurable daily prune scheduled task (orphan removal,
age-based eviction, optional LRU size cap) so the cache doesn't grow
unbounded.
Native Trickplay.overview: Native HLS trickplay for AVPlayer-based clients (Apple TV).

versions.changelog: When Jellyfin played a video without converting it, the trickplay playlist could name the wrong video format (for example HEVC for a 10-bit H.264 file), so the Apple TV prepared the wrong decoder and took much longer to start. The playlist now names the format Jellyfin actually sends, including 10-bit H.264 (High 10). No change for HDR or Dolby Vision videos.

Videos whose HEVC stream declares a level above 5.0 (common with certain x265 encodes) were rejected by the Apple TV when served through the trickplay-enabled playlist, and the player fell back to the thumbnail track. The playlist now also offers a level 5.0 entry, the same approach Jellyfin uses for its own playlists, so these videos play normally with scrubbing thumbnails intact. No change for other videos.

- Fixed: trickplay playlists and image segments now enforce each user's library access and parental controls. Previously, any signed-in user could request the scrubbing thumbnails of items outside their allowed libraries.
- Improved: the dashboard's item list loads dramatically faster on large libraries (it no longer reads every cached playlist from disk just to show cache status).
- Improved: changing "Concurrent encodes" now takes effect immediately — no server restart needed.
- Fixed: corrupt video files could make HDR detection time out, producing washed-out thumbnails for HDR content.
- Fixed: searching with an extremely large season or episode number could error the item list.
- Hardened the release pipeline: build steps are now pinned to exact, immutable versions.

After updating, restart your server once as usual. No cache regeneration is required.

If you reinstall Jellyfin (or its database gets rebuilt) and point the plugin back at your existing cache folder, the plugin now relinks every cached entry to your library automatically — no re-encoding, no lost cache.

- New: orphaned cache entries (from a reinstall or database rebuild) are automatically relinked to your items at server startup and before every scheduled prune run.
- New: the dashboard shows a warning banner with a one-click "Relink orphaned entries" button whenever orphaned entries are detected.
- Fixed: Cache Status no longer counts orphaned entries as cached (previously it could show 100% coverage while every item listed as "not cached" and playback re-encoded).
- Fixed: the daily prune task no longer deletes a reinstalled server's still-valid cache — it relinks first and only removes entries that truly match nothing.

Update, restart your server once, and your cache reconnects on its own within about 30 seconds — or press the new Relink button on the plugin dashboard.

Fixes playback stalling on Apple TV when audio is passed through unchanged (stream copy). The playlist could advertise the wrong audio format, which made the player wait forever for audio it was never going to get. If playback ever froze right after turning subtitles off, this is that fix.
Fixed playback breaking on SDR variable-bitrate files when trickplay is enabled. Affected videos could freeze mid-playback or get stuck on a loading screen when resumed; they now play normally.

* On HDR sources, tone mapping now runs on the GPU when your ffmpeg build supports it (OpenCL for Intel QSV / VAAPI / AMD on Linux, CUDA for NVIDIA, Metal on macOS). The previous CPU tone-mapping path was the dominant cost on HDR content — moving it to the GPU is the bulk of the speedup. Falls back to the old CPU path automatically when no GPU tone-mapping filter is available.

* The ffmpeg filter chain now thins frames down to the trickplay rate (one every couple of seconds) before any per-frame work runs. Previously every decoded frame was transferred GPU → CPU before being discarded — for a 2-hour 4K HDR source that's hundreds of thousands of wasted full-resolution transfers.

* New "GPU tone-mapping for HDR" toggle in the plugin settings, on by default. Disable it if GPU tone-mapping misbehaves on your hardware — encodes still benefit from the filter-chain reorder.

* Encodes that hit a GPU tone-mapping issue now fall back to CPU tone-mapping automatically (keeping hardware decode), and only drop to full software decode if the hardware decoder itself fails. The dashboard's hardware-path column shows what's actually in use (e.g. "QSV+OCL", "VideoToolbox+VT") so you can see the path each encode is taking.

A user on an Intel iGPU reported that a 2-hour 4K HDR film took ~90 minutes to generate on the prior version. The same encode finishes in roughly 10 minutes on this version.

Previously, if you deleted a library from Jellyfin, the plugin's
"Find & select items" list and the daily pre-generation task kept
seeing items from the removed library until Jellyfin's next library
scan cleaned them up — which meant inflated totals on the dashboard
and the nightly task wasting time encoding files that were no longer
in any library.

The plugin now scopes its lookups to the libraries currently visible
in Jellyfin, so the moment you remove a library the dashboard total
matches the Cache Status widget and the pre-gen task stops touching
those items.

No action required — just update the plugin and the next dashboard
load will reflect the correct counts.

Avoids advertising an iframe trickplay variant whose playlist resolves
to a valid-but-empty stub on cache miss — that combination can stall
AVPlayer on tvOS 26 with seek-shifted on-demand transcodes. Trickplay
appears on the next playback session once the warmup task generates
the cache.

* Search results above 200 items now load progressively. Default page is 500; 'Load more' appends the next batch and 'Load all' pulls everything matching the current filter.
* New 'Select all N items matching this filter' link appears once you've checked some visible items in a paginated result. Click it to select every match — including items not yet rendered. The bulk Generate or Evict action then operates on the entire match set, not just the page in front of you.
* Selection persists across pagination — checking an item on page 1 stays checked when you load page 2.
* 'Clear selection' link in the banner dismisses an all-matching selection. Filter, sort, or search changes also reset selection automatically.

versions.changelog:
Burger-menu på brede skærme.

Jellyfin 12 viser kun burger-knappen i smalle vinduer. Denne version lægger en
burger-knap i venstre side af app-baren på brede skærme også. Den åbner den
samme menu - med ekstra-punkterne øverst og Seerr Requests-linksene - og
skjules igen, mens en video spiller.

Slås til under "Burger menu on desktop screens". Ingen effekt på Jellyfin 10.11
eller i smalle vinduer.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Baggrundsbilledet på detaljesider lægger sig ikke længere oven på Jellyfins eget. Jellyfin tegner selv et baggrundsbillede i vinduer over 1000 px, og det kunne nå frem, mens vores stadig blev hentet - så lå der to lag og tonede hen over hinanden. Kontrollen sker nu lige før billedet sættes ind, i stedet for inden hentningen begynder.

Målt på Jellyfin 12: ved 1200 px vinder Jellyfins eget, ved 900 px vores. Begge dele sker, og i begge tilfælde vises nu præcis ét billede.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Baggrundsbilledet på detaljesider hentes nu i vinduets egen bredde i stedet for det dobbelte. På en skærm med skalering bad siden før om et 2560 px bredt billede til et 1268 px vindue; nu er det 1280 px - omkring en fjerdedel så mange bytes, og en størrelse serveren som regel har lavet i forvejen.

Billedet ligger bag et mørkt slør, hvor detaljerne alligevel ikke kan ses. Kort og plakater er uændrede: de ses tæt på og hentes stadig i skærmens egen opløsning.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Den natlige billedopvarmning tager nu kun titler, der er kommet til inden for de sidste 45 dage. Hele biblioteket køres igennem om søndagen, så billedstørrelser, en ny app begynder at bede om, stadig bliver lavet på forhånd.

Målt på serveren: den natlige kørsel så på 69.174 billeder for at lave 7.513 af dem og tog halvanden time, fordi resten allerede var lavet og kun blev tjekket.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Det første kort, du holder musen over efter en sideindlæsning, viser nu også forhåndsvisningen. Rækken kom på skærmen et halvt sekund før den begyndte at lytte efter musen, så den første bevægelse blev tabt - derfor virkede det næste kort med det samme, og det første bagefter.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Forhåndsvisningen på Fortsæt afspilning starter med det samme i stedet for efter tre sekunder, og klikker du på kortet, fortsætter afspilningen dér, hvor forhåndsvisningen er nået til.

I browsere uden forbindelse til serverens fjernbetjening starter klikket stadig - dér fra det gemte sted, et par sekunder før billedet på skærmen.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Et klik på Fortsæt afspilning afspiller med det samme, også i browsere hvor Jellyfins fjernbetjening ikke har forbindelse - dér endte klikket før på afsnittets side.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Forsiden står stille igen på Jellyfin 12.

- Fortsæt afspilning og Næste afsnit er én række igen, og Trending virker igen. Den gav op, når andre havde set mange afsnit den seneste måned.
- Rækkerne hopper ikke længere rundt, mens forsiden indlæses, og billederne på Fortsæt afspilning skifter ikke: de viser seriens billede, ligesom Jellyfins egen række.
- Ingen S/E-mærker på Fortsæt afspilning.
- Filmbibliotekernes redesign (Anbefalet til dig, favoritter og filtre) er fjernet, så bibliotekerne ser ud som i Jellyfin selv.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Hurtigere billeder overalt: forsiden, søgningen og detaljesiderne.

- Jellyfin laver et billede i en ny størrelse første gang, nogen beder om den, og det tager 0,1-0,5 sekunder pr. billede. Apps beder om lidt forskellige størrelser på hver enhed og i hvert vindue, så de fleste billeder blev lavet forfra. Størrelserne rundes nu til en kort liste, så et billede lavet til én enhed genbruges af den næste, og kvalitet over 90 sættes ned til 90 - et plakatkort fylder omkring en tredjedel mindre uden synlig forskel. Gælder alle apps.
- Ny planlagt opgave "Warm image cache" (dagligt kl. 03:00) laver plakater, baggrunde, logoer og skuespillerbilleder på forhånd i de størrelser, jeres apps faktisk bruger. Nye film og afsnit klares et par minutter efter, de er kommet ind. Opgaven sætter farten ned, når nogen bruger serveren. Første kørsel på et stort bibliotek tager et par timer.
- "Mere som dette" og samlinger på detaljesider huskes i 30 minutter pr. bruger. Jellyfin 12 bruger op til 1,5 sekund på at regne dem ud hver gang. De glemmes, så snart du ser eller markerer noget som favorit, eller biblioteket ændres.
- Søgningen henter skuespillere og instruktørens andre film, når du holder pause i skrivningen, i stedet for ved hvert tastetryk. Skuespillerne vises, så snart de er kendt, uden at vente på instruktørens film, billeder længere ude i rækkerne hentes først, når de kommer frem, og søger du på det samme igen, står det der med det samme.
- Mens plakater og portrætter hentes, vises en sløret udgave af billedet i stedet for en tom grå boks.
- Det hele kan slås fra under Speed i indstillingerne.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Afsnitsnummeret er tilbage på forsiden på Jellyfin 12.

- Når en serie har fået et nyt afsnit, viser Jellyfin 12 selve afsnittets kort i "Nyligt tilføjet" i stedet for seriens kort med antallet af usete afsnit. Det tal var det, New Badges skrev S/E-nummeret ind i, så mærket forsvandt. Afsnitskortene får nu selv et mærke med fx S4E7 samme sted og i samme stil.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

versions.changelog: Release v0.2.7.9 - Resolved Jellyfin server startup and dashboard crashes across 10.9, 10.10, and 12.0: safely extracted hardware acceleration engine via reflection to prevent TypeLoadException on Jellyfin 10.10+ where HardwareEncodingType was refactored; consolidated NotificationsConfigurationController constructor with [ActivatorUtilitiesConstructor] to guarantee deterministic DI resolution; protected dashboard injection middleware using StreamResponseBodyFeature and defensive Response.HasStarted guards against unhandled response mutation exceptions; guarded NotificationSecretStore and PluginServiceRegistrator startup with defensive try/catch logging; fixed client-side React DOM reconciliation crash (DOMException: Node.insertBefore) on dashboard updates by setting display:none instead of removeChild on heading elements; and moved pageshow listener from document to window to resolve Firefox PageTransitionEvent TypeError.

Release v0.2.7.8 - Redesigned playback cards with EasyUI Dark Precision styling, interactive cursor-tracking SpotlightCard glow, animated Playing equalizer bars, dual-track transcode buffer bar, and live transcode speed/throttle badges. Added a rolling 20-sample bandwidth sparkline and clickable stream-method filter chips to the summary strip. Simplified the density toggle to Compact (expandable on click) and Extended (always expanded inline). Hardened Discord webhook validation (supporting PTB/Canary domains and structured API error messages), auto-saved unsaved Discord/Telegram inputs when clicking Test, added Tailscale/WireGuard CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10) local IP classification and bounded geo-cache pruning, and consolidated backend admin authorization and DTOs.

Release v0.2.7.7 - Fixed the real cause of 'Telegram only sends when I click Test': every event-type checkbox (Playback Start, Stop, etc.) defaulted to off, so real playback events were silently dropped at the delivery queue's event-enablement check while the Test button, which bypasses that check, kept working. New installs now default Start/Stop to on, and existing installs are auto-recovered at save time if notifications and a destination are active with zero event types ever configured -- without overriding an explicit choice made in the same save. Saving Discord or Telegram settings now also persists the current event-subscription checkboxes, instead of only the separate Preferences section doing so. Fixed 'Copy Diagnostic Report' being permanently blocked when opened from Jellyfin's own standard Dashboard -> Plugins route, which always carries a '?name=playbackcard' query string the report's own validator was rejecting. Poster image upload failures (Discord, Telegram) no longer drop the notification outright, both now fall back to a plain text message if the image itself gets rejected. Parallelized the Local Network/Remote geolocation lookups so a page with several concurrent remote sessions and a cold cache no longer waits on them one at a time.

Release v0.2.7.6 - Discord/Telegram notifications now attach the item's poster image directly, uploaded as part of the same request rather than a link back to the server, so it works even on servers that aren't internet-reachable; falls back to text-only when no image is cached (on by default, can be turned off). The summary strip gains a live bandwidth gauge showing total outbound bitrate, split by Local Network vs. Remote when that badge is enabled, plus an optional percentage against an admin-configured upload limit. Sessions paused a while now show a warning pill (escalating from amber to red past an hour) so a forgotten paused stream holding server resources doesn't go unnoticed, and a badge appears when one account has more than one stream running. The Send Message admin action now offers quick-fill presets, and the Info panel gets a Copy Report button producing a sanitized per-session technical summary (no username, device, or IP) for sharing in a forum post or issue. Added a Recent Sessions shelf -- a short in-memory history of finished playback, cleared on restart, no database. Also fixes two Telegram bugs: saving a bot token no longer requires a Chat ID to already be set, and notification duration text no longer wraps past 24 hours.

Release v0.2.7.5 - Added a second Info view: click Info while 'Right' is selected (next to the existing 'Down' toggle) to open a centered dialog with the poster on the left and the full Tautulli-style Product/Player/Quality/Stream/Container/Video/Audio/Subtitle/Location/Bandwidth field list on the right, instead of expanding the card in place. The original Down behavior is unchanged. Transcode reasons are now itemized with red/amber severity, shown both as a details-panel banner and as warning rings on the affected pills, so it is clear at a glance why a stream is transcoding and how serious it is. Compact/Extended switches and opening Info now animate instead of snapping open. Also adds a strictly opt-in (off by default) Local Network/Remote badge, with an optional city/country lookup for remote sessions via a third-party geolocation service -- the raw IP address is never exposed or logged.

Release v0.2.7.4 - Added detection for stale, superseded plugin version folders left behind after an update. Jellyfin's own plugin loader can, in rare cases, silently keep running an old build instead of a newer one already installed (a real bug in Jellyfin itself, tracked upstream as jellyfin/jellyfin#17699) -- when that happens, fixes from later releases never take effect, with no error shown anywhere. The plugin now checks for this at every startup and logs a warning if found, and the System Diagnostics section shows a banner naming the older folder(s) with an explicit 'Remove' button per folder. Removal is always an admin-confirmed, one-click action -- never automatic -- and it refuses to remove anything unless it can positively confirm the folder belongs to this plugin and is strictly older than the version currently running.

# 🧭 Plugin Pages, Ready for Jellyfin 12 Plugin Pages **3.0.0.0** brings the plugin forward for **Jellyfin 12**, updating the way custom pages are injected into the Jellyfin web client and fixing the user-facing plugin settings flow for Jellyfin's latest architecture. This release also drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7**, while introducing a new plugin-facing API that makes it much easier for other plugins to add and manage their own pages. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12**. * Added a new public **Plugin Interface** allowing other plugins to register pages programmatically through `PluginInterface.RegisterPage(JObject)`. * Added `PluginInterface.RemovePage(string id)`, allowing plugins to unregister pages they previously registered. * Updated Plugin Pages' web-client injection to work with the changes introduced in Jellyfin 12. * Updated user-facing plugin settings pages to work with Jellyfin 12. * Updated the underlying Jellyfin dependencies and integration points required by the new server/web-client architecture. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Reworked page injection to account for changes to the Jellyfin 12 web client. * Improved compatibility for plugins that use Plugin Pages to expose user-facing pages inside Jellyfin. * Updated the user plugin settings integration so pages opened through Jellyfin's user menu continue to behave correctly on Jellyfin 12. * Dependent plugins can now manage their pages at runtime rather than directly modifying Plugin Pages' configuration. * Cleaned up legacy compatibility code that is no longer required now that older Jellyfin versions are being dropped. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed custom plugin pages failing to inject correctly into the **Jellyfin 12** web client. * Fixed user-facing plugin settings pages not working correctly on Jellyfin 12. * Fixed cases where pages registered through Plugin Pages could result in a **Page not found** experience after Jellyfin web-client changes. * Fixed compatibility issues caused by changes to Jellyfin's client-side routing and page-loading behaviour. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility Plugin Pages now provides a public plugin-facing API for registering and removing pages. * `PluginInterface.RegisterPage(JObject)` can be used to register a page directly with Plugin Pages. * The supplied `JObject` is deserialised into Plugin Pages' `PluginPage` model and registered immediately with the page manager. * `PluginInterface.RemovePage(string id)` can be used to unregister an existing page by its ID. * Plugins no longer need to directly modify `Jellyfin.Plugin.PluginPages/config.json` in order to dynamically add their own pages. * Plugins can now register pages during startup and remove them again during shutdown or when their configuration changes. This should be considered the **preferred integration path for dependent plugins going forward**, replacing direct manipulation of Plugin Pages' configuration where possible. The new API is additive, so existing configuration-based integrations are not inherently broken by the update. Plugin developers are, however, encouraged to migrate to the new interface for cleaner lifecycle management and better compatibility with future Plugin Pages releases. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12**. * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier Plugin Pages release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Plugin Pages continues to require a compatible version of **File Transformation**. * Plugins that depend on Plugin Pages should also be updated to versions compatible with Jellyfin 12. * The new `PluginInterface` is additive; plugins using the previous configuration-based approach can continue to work, but the programmatic API is now the recommended integration method. ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.
