Plugin Update Notifier.description: Shows a notification badge on the admin's profile avatar and an entry in the profile menu when plugins have been installed, updated or removed and the server needs a restart. The entry opens a dashboard page listing which plugins changed, their old and new versions, and each release's changelog, plus a history of what earlier restarts applied. Source, docs and issues: https://github.com/mihaif7/jellyfin-plugin-update-notifier
Plugin Update Notifier.overview: Badges the admin avatar when plugins change and a restart is pending.

versions.changelog:
## ✨ New Features

- **Notify chosen users**: tick non-admin users on the new **Settings** tab to show them the badge too.
- **Counts only**: they see how many plugins changed, and can't dismiss or restart.

## 🎨 Improvements

- **Tabbed plugin page**: the page is split into **Updates** and **Settings** tabs.

## ✨ New Features

- **Removals are tracked**: uninstalling a plugin now shows on the **Plugin Updates** page and badges your avatar, just like an install, until the restart that applies it.
- **History of applied changes**: a collapsible **Previously applied** section lists what earlier restarts made live, grouped by restart. It keeps the last 50 changes and can be cleared.
- **Built for Jellyfin 12.0 and 12.1**: each release is now published once per server version, so the catalog offers a build that targets your server exactly.

## 🐞 Bug Fixes

- **One card per plugin**: installing and then updating a plugin before a restart shows as a single change, and installing then removing one shows nothing at all.
- **Manual task runs are safe**: running the plugin's startup task by hand from Scheduled Tasks no longer clears changes that are still waiting for a restart.
- **Sturdier saved state**: a damaged state file is kept aside as `updates.json.unreadable` instead of being overwritten, and one bad entry no longer costs the rest.

## 🐞 Bug Fixes

- **Nothing runs for non-admins**: the script checks who you are first, instead of every user's browser polling once a minute for an admin-only answer.
- **Far fewer checks**: every five minutes instead of every minute, and paused while the tab is in the background.
- **Smaller checks**: each check now asks only for the number it needs, instead of downloading every plugin's full release notes and throwing them away.
- **Switching tabs is free**: returning to the Jellyfin tab no longer triggers a fresh check.
- **Lighter on the browser**: the plugin now only keeps an eye on the page while a notification is actually showing, rather than constantly, for everyone.

## 📋 Notes

- The badge can now take up to five minutes to appear after a plugin is updated, rather than up to one. Opening the user menu always shows the current count.

## ✨ New Features

- **Plugin icon**: the plugin now has its own icon in the catalog and in your plugin list, instead of a blank placeholder.

## 🐞 Bug Fixes

- **Readable changelogs**: a plugin's release notes on the **Plugin Updates** page now appear properly formatted. Bold text, headings and links show as intended, instead of displaying the raw formatting characters around them.

## 📋 Notes

- Nothing to reconfigure. Updating takes only the usual restart.
- Still Jellyfin 12 only. The avatar badge and profile-menu entry need the [JavaScript Injector](https://github.com/n00bcodr/Jellyfin-JavaScript-Injector) plugin; the dashboard page works without it.

## Plugin Update Notifier 1.0.0.0

First release, for Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin installs plugin updates in place but only applies them on the next server restart, and nothing in the UI tells an administrator that a restart is pending. This plugin closes that gap: it watches plugin install and update events and surfaces a clear, dismissible reminder until the server is restarted.

### Features

- Avatar badge: a dot appears on the admin's profile avatar the moment a plugin change leaves a restart pending.
- Profile-menu entry: a "Plugin Updates" item in the user dropdown, shown only to administrators, with a count of what changed.
- Dashboard page: lists every changed plugin, its old and new version, the release changelog, and a link to each plugin's source.
- Shared dismiss: dismissing hides the reminder for every admin session, not just one browser; a later plugin change brings it back.
- Self-clearing: the reminder disappears on its own after the restart it was asking for.

### Requirements

- Jellyfin 12 (this release uses APIs not present in 10.x).
- The avatar badge and profile-menu entry additionally require the [JavaScript Injector](https://github.com/n00bcodr/Jellyfin-JavaScript-Injector) plugin (4.0.0.0 or newer). The dashboard page works without it.

Poster Overlays.description: Draws a small badge onto the primary image - the edition, the resolution and the video range - so two entries of the same film can be told apart on the tile. The badge is re-applied whenever a provider replaces the cover.
Poster Overlays.overview: Edition, resolution and HDR badges drawn onto the poster.

versions.changelog: If the plugin stopped working with "The poster overlay state file ... could not be read", this release is for you. The state file is now written atomically, so a server that dies mid-write can no longer leave it empty - which is what happened on the reference server when the VM was killed during the nightly run. An image uploaded just before a crash is now recognised on the next run, and a cached original without a record is never overwritten. New task "Rebuild poster overlay state": run it with the dry run on first. It rebuilds a record only where drawing today's badges onto the cached original gives the cover on the item again, and lists everything else by name without touching it. Do not delete a damaged state file - the old error message advised that, and it was wrong.

Nothing changes visibly in this one. The preview picker on the settings page now tells the server explicitly not to substitute collections for the films inside them when searching. That was already the behaviour, but only because Jellyfin happens to switch it off for searches by itself - and because the search box never queries with fewer than two characters. Neither is something this plugin controls, so it now says what it means. Badges, rendering and the scheduled task are untouched.

The report about folder names that disagree with the video stream over HDR is now a setting, and it is off by default. It only says something if your folder names carry release tags - if you name folders "Film (Year)", every HDR title would be counted as a disagreement. Turn it on under Operation if the tags are there. The badges follow the video stream either way, with the report on or off.

Names the file behind "the image could not be decoded" instead of only the film, so a broken cover can be found without searching by hand - and fixes a case where that message could not be reached at all, because the renderer threw on a file its decoder cannot open rather than reporting it. The HDR/DV disagreement between folder name and video stream is now summarised once per run instead of printed for every film: it is the ordinary case, not an exception, and it was burying the messages worth reading. The v12 build now targets Jellyfin 12.0.0 rather than a release candidate.

Fixes a badge that could not be taken off again. When an item lost its last badge - a duplicate was deleted, or it never really had a twin - the plugin was supposed to put the untouched cover back, and never did: the restore asked for a lock its own caller was already holding, then failed silently. A run with 222 items to restore restored none of them and reported a missing cache that was present. If your library carries labels that no longer apply, the next nightly run clears them.

Fixes the audio badge appearing on films that have no second copy at all.

Peers were matched by any shared provider id, which swept in TmdbCollection - an id every film of a series carries. All fifteen Star Wars films therefore counted as copies of one another, their audio formats differed, and a badge appeared where the rule says there should be none. Only ids that name a title are used now: IMDb, TMDb, TVDB and the custom id an NFO can set.

Also fixes the badge never appearing in the previous version, where copies were grouped by Jellyfin's presentation key. That key groups the rows of a series, but for a film it falls back to the item's own id unless the files were merged as alternate versions by hand, so two ordinary copies never shared it.

The badge itself is unchanged: ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on, drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it, describing the track in the language you set rather than the technically best one.

Fixes the audio badge never appearing. It was grouping copies of a film by Jellyfin's presentation key, which groups the rows of a series but not of a film: for a film that key falls back to the item's own id unless the files were merged as alternate versions by hand, so two ordinary copies never shared it and the badge was skipped every time. Copies are now matched by provider id.

The badge itself is unchanged: ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on, drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it, and describing the track in the language you set rather than the technically best one.

Adds an audio-format badge - ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on - drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it. Off by default.

The restriction is the point. Measured on a library of 2,346 films: of 105 groups holding more than one copy of a film, 7 differ in nothing the existing badges could show except the audio format. Every other film has no second copy at all, so a format badge there describes a file nobody is comparing to anything.

Which track it describes is configurable, as a list of languages, best first - the first one any track carries wins. This matters more than it sounds: 437 films carry several languages in different formats, typically a German AC3 beside an English DTS, and taking the best track badges such a film "DTS", which is true about the file and about a track its owner never selects. Setting a language therefore draws fewer badges rather than more, which is the intent.

Spelling is forgiving because the server is asked rather than a table in the plugin: "de", "ger", "deu" and "German" all name one language, for every language Jellyfin knows. A file with a single track always reports that one, whatever the preference says.

Within the chosen language only the best track counts - a film with Atmos, a DTS-HD track and a stereo commentary is an Atmos film. The label carries as much as the job needs: where two copies are both plain DTS and differ only in the channel layout, the layout is added.

The setting for merging Dolby Vision and HDR is now spelled MergeDolbyVisionAndHDR in code. Stored configurations are unaffected - the file keeps the old spelling on purpose, so a value anybody switched off stays switched off.

Adds an audio-format badge - ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on - drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it. Off by default.

A file with a single track always reports that one, whatever the preference says. Spelling is forgiving, since ISO 639-2 gives several languages two codes and files in the wild use both.

Every other film has no second copy at all, so a format badge there says something true about a file nobody is comparing to anything.

The label carries as much as the job needs. The format alone settles most cases; where two copies are both plain DTS and differ only in the channel layout, the layout is added. Where even that is equal nothing is drawn, because "two audio tracks" is not something a badge can usefully say. Only the best track counts - a film with Atmos, a DTS-HD track and a stereo commentary is an Atmos film.

Grouping follows Jellyfin's own presentation key, the one it uses to decide which rows are shown as a single tile, rather than an id read out of the provider list.

Posterizarr.description: Local asset metadata provider and real-time WebSocket sync engine. Instantly maps and updates posters, backgrounds, seasons, and title cards without library scans.
Posterizarr.overview: A companion plugin for Posterizarr that maps local assets to Jellyfin library items and connects to Posterizarr's real-time WebSocket stream (/ws/events) to instantaneously apply rendered artwork in under a second.

versions.changelog: Official Release 3.3.7

Official Release 3.3.6

- **BoxSet & Collection Support**: Added Primary, Thumbnail, and Backdrop image resolution for collections across Jellyfin and Emby.
- **Asset Path Resolution**: Resolves Collections directory at root or within subfolders, supporting both nested folders and flat file structures.
- **Smart Name Normalization**: Handles '[boxset]' tag stripping, '&' vs 'and' variants, illegal character sanitization, and automatic 'Collection' suffix matching.
- **Metadata Refresh Detection**: Implemented HasChanged check using file timestamps so library refreshes detect updated assets on disk.
- **Real-Time WebSocket Sync**: Added collection asset handling to automatically invalidate cache and update artwork via WebSocket stream.
- **Opt-In Setting**: Added UpdateCollection configuration toggle (default false) in plugin configuration page.
Official Release 3.3.5

Official Release 3.3.4

- **WebSocket Real-Time Sync**: Added background listener service connecting to `/ws/events` for instant image updates.
- **Direct Image Application**: Streams and persists image updates directly using internal provider APIs upon receiving events.
- **Enhanced Configuration Page**: Added Real-Time Sync toggle, Posterizarr URL input, and API key configuration with live connection test diagnostics.
- **Volume Latency Tolerance**: Added 2-second retry loop for newly created image files.
- **Catalog Image**: Configured `imageUrl` in repository manifests.

Official Release 3.3.3

- **Persistent State Caching**: Added `posterizarr_sync_cache.json` in the plugin data directory to track file sizes, timestamps, and image metadata. Unchanged assets are skipped instantly in memory with zero network I/O.
- **Directory & File Caching**: Added `AssetPathResolver` to cache root library shares and folder file listings. Reduces tens of thousands of remote SMB/NFS round-trips to a single query per media folder.
- **Parallel Async Sync Task**: Upgraded `PosterizarrSyncTask` to use `Parallel.ForEachAsync` with adaptive concurrency, replacing single-threaded sequential processing.
- **Tiered Image Verification**: Added 4KB header and file-length pre-checks to eliminate continuous ~30 MB/s full-file MD5 hash calculations across the network.
- **Debug Mode Toggle**: Debug messages (`[Posterizarr DEBUG]`) are now directly controlled by the plugin's `EnableDebugMode` setting and visible in the Jellyfin log viewer without changing server logging configurations.
- **Emby Optimization**: Added same-path timestamp comparison to prevent double-hashing identical local files in Emby.
- **Performance Benchmark**: Successfully verified on a 39,000-item library, reducing task runtime from **32m 51s to 13 seconds (~151x faster)** with near-zero network and disk utilization.

Official Release 3.3.2

- **Jellyfin 12.0.x & 10.11.x Multi-Targeting**: Compiled for both `.NET 9` (Jellyfin 10.11.x) and `.NET 10` (Jellyfin 12.0.x) with target-specific ABI dependencies (`10.11.0.0` and `12.0.0.0`).
- **Automated Dual Packaging**: Manifest and release pipelines now generate separate distribution archives (`Posterizarr.Plugin_v3.3.2.zip` and `Posterizarr.Plugin_v3.3.2-jf12.zip`).
- **Emby API Token Authentication**: Updated media server logo upload headers to use `MediaBrowser Token="{token}"` format, resolving upload failures on Emby servers.

---
Official Release 3.3.1

Official Release 3.3.0

- **Accurate Title Card Matching**: Title cards are now resolved by their true episode number rather than list order, eliminating mismatched artwork when shows have episode gaps or irregular numbering.
- **Improved Season & Arc Matching**: Shows with named story arcs or custom season titles (such as anime like *One Piece*) now group seasons correctly, fixing missing season artwork and eliminating sync errors.

Official Release 3.2.0

- Added granular image type toggles: Poster, Season, Titlecard, Backdrop, Thumbnail (configurable per-type from plugin settings)
- Scheduled sync task now uses the same image type configuration as the image provider
- Added `ReplaceThumbwithBackdropExclusively` - upload backdrop to Thumbnail slot only, skip actual Backdrop upload
- Fixed `ILoggerFactory` injection in `PosterizarrSyncTask` (was incorrectly using `new LoggerFactory()`)
- Thumbnail toggle defaults to OFF to avoid accidental overwrites
Official Release 3.1.4

PostgreSQL Database Provider.description: Production-ready PostgreSQL backend for Jellyfin. Bidirectional SQLite migration, near-instant search, health diagnostics, read-only SQL console and scheduled maintenance — no core modifications required.
PostgreSQL Database Provider.overview: Reemplaza SQLite por PostgreSQL como motor de base de datos de Jellyfin. Incluye migración bidireccional SQLite↔PostgreSQL, búsqueda casi instantánea con índices GIN, health check automático al arrancar, consola SQL de solo lectura, mantenimiento programado (VACUUM/REINDEX/Backup) y un host seguro de esquemas privados para otros plugins.

versions.changelog:
## Español

### 3.1.0 — Retención de respaldos, endurecimiento y nueva interfaz

**Novedades**
- Retención de respaldos: define cuántos días se conserva cada backup (0 = sin límite, valor por defecto) y cuántos de los más recientes se conservan siempre (5 por defecto). Solo se borran archivos con el nombre que genera el plugin; cualquier otro archivo de la carpeta no se toca. Se aplica tras cada backup, con la nueva tarea programada «PostgreSQL Backup Retention» (diaria, 03:00) y con el botón «Depurar respaldos ahora», que muestra una vista previa y pide confirmación. Funciona igual en Windows, Linux y macOS.
- Interfaz renovada con el mismo diseño que JellyTV: pantalla completa y responsive, selects y checkboxes propios, título con descripción y pestaña Mantenimiento reordenada (operaciones, respaldos con retención, tareas programadas). Los resultados y avisos salen como notificaciones abajo a la derecha: las operaciones en curso muestran un indicador y los éxitos desaparecen solos. VACUUM, respaldos, optimizaciones, reparación y migración piden confirmación con el mismo modal, que ya no se cierra al pulsar fuera. «Actualizar estadísticas» pasa a Health.
- Aviso en el log, en el estado y en la interfaz cuando hay copias obsoletas del plugin junto a la que está en ejecución (por ejemplo una carpeta antigua marcada como eliminada), que Jellyfin puede seguir cargando.

**Seguridad y fiabilidad**
- **Cambio de comportamiento:** `Search/Instant` ahora exige un usuario autenticado. Antes era anónimo y permitía listar `BaseItems` sin sesión.
- La consola SQL se ejecuta en una transacción de solo lectura con límites de tiempo y rechaza las comillas de dólar, que permitían ocultar una segunda sentencia.
- La caché de consultas invalida también las escrituras de `SaveChanges` y al confirmar transacciones; antes podía servir datos antiguos hasta 30 s.
- Guardar la configuración valida la conexión cuando PostgreSQL está activo, rechaza cadenas vacías, escribe `database.xml` de forma atómica (con copia `.bak`) y la API ya no devuelve la contraseña en claro.
- Los agregados `min/max(uuid)` se dan por creados solo tras un intento exitoso; `pg_dump` y `psql` se terminan al cancelar y un volcado fallido ya no deja un `.sql` parcial.
- Las fechas se convierten a UTC al leer y escribir, y la variable `JELLYFIN_PG_DISABLE_QUERY_CACHE=1` permite descartar la caché al diagnosticar.

Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 o posterior y .NET 10.

---

## English

### 3.1.0 — Backup retention, hardening, and a new interface

**What's new**
- Backup retention: choose how many days each backup is kept (0 = keep forever, the default) and how many of the newest backups are always kept (5 by default). Only files named the way the plugin names them are deleted; any other file in the folder is left alone. It runs after every backup, through the new «PostgreSQL Backup Retention» scheduled task (daily, 03:00), and with the «Prune backups now» button, which shows a preview and asks for confirmation. It behaves the same on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
- Redesigned interface matching JellyTV: full-width and responsive, custom selects and checkboxes, a page title with description, and a reordered Maintenance tab (operations, backups with retention, scheduled tasks). Results and alerts appear as notifications at the bottom right: running operations show an indicator and successes dismiss themselves. VACUUM, backups, optimizations, repair, and migration ask for confirmation with the same modal, which no longer closes when you click outside. «Refresh statistics» moves to Health.
- A warning in the log, the status endpoint, and the interface when stale copies of the plugin sit next to the running one (for example an old folder marked as deleted) that Jellyfin may still load.

**Security and reliability**
- **Behavior change:** `Search/Instant` now requires a signed-in user. It used to be anonymous and could list `BaseItems` without a session.
- The SQL console runs in a read-only transaction with time limits and rejects dollar quoting, which could hide a second statement.
- The query cache also invalidates `SaveChanges` writes and transaction commits; it could previously serve stale data for up to 30 s.
- Saving the configuration validates the connection when PostgreSQL is active, rejects empty strings, writes `database.xml` atomically (with a `.bak` copy), and the API no longer returns the password in clear text.
- The `min/max(uuid)` aggregates are marked as created only after a successful attempt; `pg_dump` and `psql` are terminated on cancel and a failed dump no longer leaves a partial `.sql`.
- Dates are converted to UTC on read and write, and `JELLYFIN_PG_DISABLE_QUERY_CACHE=1` lets you rule out the cache when diagnosing.

Requires Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 or newer, and .NET 10.

## Español

### 3.0.4 — Fechas, búsqueda, guardado y migración

- Corrige el cierre de Jellyfin Android TV al abrir bibliotecas: el caché de consultas descartaba `DateTimeKind.Utc` al bufferizar y el cliente recibía fechas sin zona horaria, que sustituía por su valor mínimo y hacían fallar la conversión. Las columnas de fecha se bufferizan como UTC y el lector restaura el `Kind` como segunda barrera.
- Nueva migración que normaliza fechas no finitas o mínimas ya guardadas en `BaseItems`, y normalización de los centinelas `DateTime` y `DateTimeOffset` antes de escribir.
- La búsqueda deja de distinguir mayúsculas y minúsculas e incluye título visible, título original y título para ordenar, con índice trigram sobre `SortName`.
- Corrige el error 500 al abrir la ficha de un artista o persona: las filas duplicadas se resuelven con una actualización sin cambios sobre la clave primaria en lugar de `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, que informaba 0 filas y EF Core trataba como conflicto de concurrencia.
- Corrige la migración SQLite → PostgreSQL: se conserva el historial de rutinas de código ya aplicadas, identificadas por el nombre de la migración. Sin él, Jellyfin volvía a ejecutar rutinas que esperan `library.db` y el arranque fallaba con `no such table: TypedBaseItems` (#9).
- El proveedor fija `QuerySplittingBehavior` en `SingleQuery`, igual que el proveedor SQLite, y deja de llenar el log con `MultipleCollectionIncludeWarning`.

Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 o posterior y .NET 10.

---

## English

### 3.0.4 — Dates, search, saving, and migration

- Fixes Jellyfin Android TV crashing when a library is opened: the query cache dropped `DateTimeKind.Utc` while buffering, so the client received dates without a time zone, replaced them with its minimum value, and failed converting it. Date columns are buffered as UTC and the reader restores the `Kind` as a second safeguard.
- New migration that normalizes non-finite or minimum dates already stored in `BaseItems`, plus normalization of `DateTime` and `DateTimeOffset` sentinels before writing.
- Search is no longer case-sensitive and now covers display, original, and sort titles, with a trigram index on `SortName`.
- Fixes the 500 returned when opening an artist or person page: duplicate rows are resolved with a no-op update on the primary key instead of `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, which reported zero affected rows and EF Core treated as a concurrency conflict.
- Fixes the SQLite → PostgreSQL migration: the history of code migrations already applied is preserved, matched by migration name. Without it, Jellyfin re-ran routines that expect `library.db` and startup failed with `no such table: TypedBaseItems` (#9).
- The provider pins `QuerySplittingBehavior` to `SingleQuery`, matching Jellyfin's SQLite provider, and stops flooding the log with `MultipleCollectionIncludeWarning`.

Requires Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 or newer, and .NET 10.

## Español

### 3.0.3 — Integraciones privadas, mantenimiento y estabilidad

- Nuevo host seguro para esquemas privados de plugins: registro, migraciones aisladas y acceso sin exponer credenciales ni el esquema `public` de Jellyfin.
- Nueva pestaña **Integraciones** para revisar esquemas registrados, consultar una muestra limitada de datos, ver métricas por tabla y administrar `ANALYZE`, `VACUUM (ANALYZE)` y `REINDEX` por esquema.
- Las tareas programadas mantienen `public` y solo los esquemas privados autorizados por el administrador.
- Health incorpora métricas de presión de buffers, bloques leídos, uso temporal y WAL para diagnosticar consultas lentas.
- Estado actual detecta el motor activo sin esperar la validación SQLite; esta continúa en segundo plano y se vuelve a comprobar antes de revertir.
- Se refuerza el aislamiento de identificadores en operaciones de exploración y mantenimiento de esquemas privados.
- Documentación actualizada en español e inglés, incluida la integración para desarrolladores, exportación SQLite segura y orientación para Docker.

Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 o posterior y .NET 10.

---

## English

### 3.0.3 — Private integrations, maintenance, and stability

- New secure host for private plugin schemas: registration, isolated migrations, and storage without exposing credentials or Jellyfin's `public` schema.
- New **Integrations** tab to review registered schemas, inspect a bounded data sample, view per-table metrics, and manage `ANALYZE`, `VACUUM (ANALYZE)`, and `REINDEX` per schema.
- Scheduled tasks maintain `public` and only private schemas explicitly enabled by an administrator.
- Health adds buffer-pressure, blocks-read, temporary-I/O, and WAL metrics for slow-query diagnosis.
- Current status detects the active engine without waiting for SQLite validation; validation continues in the background and is checked again before rollback.
- Strengthens identifier isolation in private-schema exploration and maintenance operations.
- Updated Spanish and English documentation, including developer integration, safe SQLite export, and Docker guidance.

Requires Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 or newer, and .NET 10.

## Español

### 3.0.2 — Estabilidad, integridad y exportación segura

- Corrige la normalización de `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset` y arreglos antes de escribir en PostgreSQL, evitando errores de Npgsql por `Kind` incompatible.
- Las escrituras concurrentes de `UserData` y las actualizaciones completas de elementos usan upserts atómicos para reducir conflictos durante actualizaciones bajo demanda.
- La activación de PostgreSQL valida la conexión antes de modificar `database.xml`.
- Se elimina la restauración automática de backups y la restauración manual no reemplaza objetos existentes por defecto.
- Las consultas concurrentes idénticas de inicio se consolidan mientras se llena la caché.
- La exportación PostgreSQL → SQLite crea y valida un `library.db` SQLite real; evita el archivo inválido que impedía iniciar Jellyfin.
- La exportación ya no copia ni marca a ciegas el historial de migraciones.

Verificado con Build Release, pruebas unitarias e integración real contra PostgreSQL. Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16+ y .NET 10.

---

## English

### 3.0.2 — Stability, integrity and safe export

- Fixes normalization of `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, and arrays before PostgreSQL writes, avoiding Npgsql errors caused by incompatible `Kind` values.
- Concurrent `UserData` writes and full item updates use atomic upserts to reduce conflicts during on-demand updates.
- PostgreSQL activation validates the connection before changing `database.xml`.
- Automatic backup restore was removed, and manual restore no longer replaces existing objects by default.
- Identical concurrent home-screen queries are coalesced while the cache is populated.
- PostgreSQL → SQLite export creates and validates a real SQLite `library.db`, preventing the invalid file that stopped Jellyfin from starting.
- Export no longer blindly marks or copies migration history.

Verified with a Release build, unit tests, and real PostgreSQL integration tests. Requires Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16+, and .NET 10.

versions.changelog: Bug-fix release for Jellyfin 12 (12.0 to 12.2), from a review of the whole plugin. Data safety: with Replace in place, a file that changes during the encode - an upgrade imported under the same name by Sonarr or Radarr - is no longer overwritten or deleted; the encode is discarded instead. A stray control character in a setting no longer wipes the whole configuration at the next start, and a configuration file that cannot be read is now backed up before Jellyfin replaces it. Jobs queued for a profile that was later deleted fail instead of running under the default profile. Containers such as mpegts are written with extensions Jellyfin indexes (.ts), so replacing a recording no longer drops it from the library. Playback: surround audio re-encoded to AAC uses a standard channel layout, so Apple clients no longer drop the track (6.1 becomes 5.1), and HEVC in MP4 is tagged hvc1. Portrait phone videos, odd frame sizes and text subtitles in mpegts or avi no longer fail. H.264 High 10 and 4:2:2/4:4:4 files are no longer skipped as already compliant, so they are queued once. Queue: after a restart, waiting jobs no longer start before Jellyfin has set its ffmpeg path (they failed on Docker), a server stop no longer records the running job as failed, and one file can no longer be encoded twice at once. Settings page: edits are no longer lost when switching or adding profiles. Behaviour change: Container conditions now go by the file extension, so mov no longer matches .mp4 files and mkv no longer matches .webm (matroska still covers both).

Jellyfin 12 support. This build targets Jellyfin 12.0 and 12.1 (.NET 10). Servers still on 10.11 stay on the 0.10 line, which remains in this repository and keeps being offered to them - a 10.11 server will not be offered this build, and it would not load there. Nearly everything carried over unchanged. The one part of the plugin that used an API Jellyfin 12 changed is "Add as alternate version", which now links versions by item id rather than by file path, as 12 requires. On 12 that output policy also no longer waits five minutes and then warns that the merge was skipped: Jellyfin 12 recognises the companion file as a version of the source from its name, so the plugin now sees that the grouping is already in place and says so instead (issue #15). Includes the container crop fix from 0.10.1.0 (issue #14). If you are on 12 with 0.10.x installed: it does load there, but its alternate-version merge fails on 12 and is logged as a warning - updating to this release fixes that.

Bug-fix release for Jellyfin 10.11, with the same fixes as 0.11.1.0 for Jellyfin 12, from a review of the whole plugin. Data safety: with Replace in place, a file that changes during the encode - an upgrade imported under the same name by Sonarr or Radarr - is no longer overwritten or deleted; the encode is discarded instead. A stray control character in a setting no longer wipes the whole configuration at the next start, and a configuration file that cannot be read is now backed up before Jellyfin replaces it. Jobs queued for a profile that was later deleted fail instead of running under the default profile. Containers such as mpegts are written with extensions Jellyfin indexes (.ts), so replacing a recording no longer drops it from the library. Playback: surround audio re-encoded to AAC uses a standard channel layout, so Apple clients no longer drop the track (6.1 becomes 5.1), and HEVC in MP4 is tagged hvc1. Portrait phone videos, odd frame sizes and text subtitles in mpegts or avi no longer fail. H.264 High 10 and 4:2:2/4:4:4 files are no longer skipped as already compliant, so they are queued once. Queue: after a restart, waiting jobs no longer start before Jellyfin has set its ffmpeg path (they failed on Docker), a server stop no longer records the running job as failed, and one file can no longer be encoded twice at once. Settings page: edits are no longer lost when switching or adding profiles. Behaviour change: Container conditions now go by the file extension, so mov no longer matches .mp4 files and mkv no longer matches .webm (matroska still covers both).

Fixes correct encodes being thrown away after they had finished (issue #14). A Matroska file can ask for its picture to be cropped in the container rather than in the video stream - common on UHD remuxes, where 280 lines off the top and bottom turn a 16:9 frame into a 2.40:1 film. ffmpeg 7.1 and later, including the one bundled with Jellyfin 10.11, applies that crop by itself, so the encode came out right; but the check that runs before an output is kept compared it against the uncropped size, decided the shape was wrong, and discarded the file - after however many hours the encode had taken, and on every file carrying this metadata. The crop is now read from the source, and the check accepts the picture as it is displayed as well as the uncropped frame, because an older ffmpeg ignores the crop and produces the uncropped one. It still rejects what it exists to catch: embedded cover art encoded in place of the film. The displayed size is now used everywhere else it matters too: a cropped file that already fits a resolution cap is no longer queued for nothing, the VideoWidth and VideoHeight rule conditions describe the picture you actually see, and a resolution cap no longer enlarges a cropped picture to reach a limit it was already under. Files without crop metadata - nearly all of them - behave exactly as before.

Two requested features. A daily processing window (issue #7): set "start processing at" and "pause processing at" in 30-minute steps and transcoding is confined to those hours, so a download that lands at 19:00 no longer starts encoding while you are using the machine. Outside the window nothing new is claimed and a running encode is frozen exactly where it is at the OS level - no CPU used, no progress lost - while items are still evaluated and queued, so the queue simply drains when the window opens. A stop time earlier than the start is an over-midnight window (22:00 to 06:00); equal times mean all day, so ticking the box before choosing times cannot stop the queue for ever. Times are the server's own local time, like Jellyfin's scheduled tasks. The control center now explains an automatic pause rather than just looking idle: it names the window and the time processing resumes, and the job list greys a frozen encode the way a manual pause already did. "Resume queue" outside the window asks for confirmation and then runs until the window's next edge, after which the schedule takes over again. A manual pause still overrides everything and still survives a restart. The single-item search now matches file names (issue #8): every word you type is matched against both the item's label and its full file path, so a show name, an S03E06, a 1080p or a release-group tag finds the file - alone or in combination. Typing a series name lists its episodes, grouped and in season/episode order, which was impossible before because Jellyfin's own search only ever compares an item's own name - for an episode that is the episode title, not the show, and never the path. Results are capped at 100, with a line saying how many matched in total.

Fixes a muxer error that killed jobs outright, adds hardware decoding, and fixes the queue's Pause on macOS. Audio is now negotiated against the output container the way subtitles already were: a track the container has no tag for is re-encoded instead of copied. Copying an mkv source's TrueHD track into mp4, or an aac track into webm, made the muxer reject the output header, so the whole encode died within seconds of starting - on every attempt, until the job hit the failed-attempt limit. Copy still means copy wherever the container allows it, which is all of Matroska and the common case for mp4, so profiles that already worked emit exactly the same command as before. A profile whose target audio codec the container cannot hold falls back to one it can. New "Hardware decoding" option (General): ffmpeg can decode the source on the GPU instead of the CPU, which is a large share of the work on 4K HEVC material and is worthwhile even when you encode in software. The list is built from what your own ffmpeg reports. It is off by default, because that list says what the binary was built with rather than what this machine can actually open - a method the host cannot open makes every job fail, so change it, run one job and check the queue page before leaving it on. Pausing the queue on macOS wedged the worker: the encode was suspended but the call never returned, leaving a stopped ffmpeg that nothing could resume, cancel or kill. The signal is now sent directly rather than by running /bin/kill. Also: the end-to-end test suite no longer skips itself silently on machines whose ffmpeg is not in one of three hardcoded locations, and a write-only field is no longer serialised into every queue-file write.

Splits the queue page into a control center and a paged job list, fixes issue #5, and closes a long list of defects found by a full audit. The plugin page used to fetch every job every two seconds and render a row for each one, which on a large library meant megabytes per poll and a table hundreds of screens long. The main page is now a control center - the counts, what is encoding with its progress and ETA, the next few jobs and the last few finished - with the full queue and history behind their own paged, searchable page. Issue #5: replacing a file in place with a different container renames it (Movie.mp4 to Movie.mkv) and left Jellyfin's database pointing at the deleted path, so playback failed with a file-not-found error until some later library scan; the item is now repointed at the new file, its container and size corrected, and its media info re-probed. Data safety: ffmpeg could encode embedded cover art instead of the film, and because verification only compared duration - which the audio track satisfies on its own - the original was then deleted for it under Replace in place; the stream map now excludes attached pictures and verification also checks the output's shape and audio tracks. Pausing could freeze an encode with nothing left to resume it. A clean restart no longer records a running encode as a user cancellation, waits for encodes to stop instead of orphaning ffmpeg, and sweeps the part-finished temp files that every cancel and crash used to leave behind for good. Rules: Container conditions are matched against what ffprobe actually reports, so "Container Equals mkv" matches an mkv and "NotEquals mp4" no longer matches every mp4; AudioCodec and AudioChannels are answered over every audio track instead of only the first, so a remux whose commentary is muxed ahead of the main track is no longer skipped; -preset is only passed to encoders that accept it; an image subtitle Matroska cannot store no longer aborts the encode; and an admin's own -vf is merged with the plugin's instead of being silently discarded. Also: queue writes are batched, so a sweep no longer rewrites a multi-megabyte file once per queued item, and "Cancel all" no longer does the same per cancelled job.

Answers issue #4 with a debug switch, and fixes four defects that switch made visible. New "Explain every decision in the log" option (General): each item logs what ffprobe found, every trigger-rule condition with its configured value, the value it was compared against and whether it passed, and the reason anything was skipped - so a rule that does not fire can finally be diagnosed. Fixes: a matched rule is no longer silently vetoed by the compliance check, which never looked at file size or bitrate (profiles that re-encode material already in the target codec can now switch off "Skip files already matching this profile"); a profile that would write its output over its own source is refused instead of dropping "Movie (1).mkv" beside it and re-encoding that copy on every sweep; a 10-bit source keeps its bit depth when the chosen encoder supports it, and HDR is no longer forced to 8-bit while keeping its HDR tags; and duration-based rules no longer die silently on files whose container reports no format-level duration. Also: a non-media file fails with a clear message instead of a raw ffmpeg error, an alternate version Jellyfin already grouped by filename is no longer listed twice in the version picker, the paused state survives a restart, and the finished-job history can be capped.

Two requested features. Profiles gain a "Keep original if the transcode is not smaller" option: after an encode is verified, if the new file is not smaller than the source it is discarded and your original is kept untouched — useful when re-encoding to a more efficient codec that can still produce a bigger file on some content, with no manual per-file size comparison across the library. The source is then remembered as handled, so the automatic sweep does not re-encode it on every run. Also adds a new VideoDurationMinutes trigger-rule condition, so a file-size threshold can be scaled by video length instead of a single blanket size — e.g. "duration under 30 min AND size over 350 MB".

Adds on-demand single-item pre-transcoding. From the Queue & status page there is now a "Transcode a single item" panel: search for a movie or episode by name, pick an encoding profile, and queue just that one — independent of the trigger rules and the automatic sweep (it is still skipped at run time if the item is already compliant). Also fixes the queue list appearing frozen during a slow (e.g. 4K) encode: the progress bar, elapsed time and estimated time remaining now keep updating while a job runs, instead of only redrawing when the whole-number percent changed.

QualityGate.description: Quality Gate lets Jellyfin administrators cap the resolution a user may be served. The cap is measured against the media's actual height, read from its video stream, so it holds whatever the file is called. Media above the cap is served as a capped transcode, or as a lower-resolution version of the same item where one exists, and requests for the original file are refused. Useful for bandwidth management and tiered access.

versions.changelog:
COMPATIBILITY: Plugin now targets Jellyfin 12.1 (was 10.11.8)

CRITICAL FIX: UTF-8 encoding in Telnet client — file paths with non-ASCII characters (é, ó, ñ, á, í, ú) are now sent correctly to Liquidsoap, fixing ~80% of silently skipped tracks
FIX: LiquidsoapClient.cs now uses UTF-8 encoding for all Telnet communications instead of ASCII (ASCII corrupted accented characters into '?' causing 'Nonexistent file or ill-formed URI' errors)
FIX: Telnet response reading also uses UTF-8 encoding for consistency
NOTE: Recommended radio.liq changes to further reduce latency and track skipping: disable enable_autocue_metadata(), reduce crossfade to 1.5s, add normalize_url=false to http.get

FIX: NowPlaying JSON year field now returned as quoted string (was unquoted integer causing JSON parse errors in external apps)
FIX: Artwork proxy now actually resizes images based on maxWidth parameter using Jellyfin IImageProcessor (was serving original full-size image regardless of maxWidth value)
FIX: Artwork proxy now uses async IImageProcessor.ProcessImage for proper image processing with SkiaSharp backend

CRITICAL FIX: Eliminated duplicate track reports — Jellyfin was reporting the same song 2-3 times (A,A,A,D,E,E,E pattern) while Icecast played correctly
CRITICAL FIX: NowPlaying JSON and Android app now show the correct current track instead of stale data from duplicate on_track callbacks
FIX: TrackChangeController made fully async — removed .GetAwaiter().GetResult() that caused thread pool starvation and request deadlocks
FIX: Duplicate suppression — same track reported within 15 seconds is suppressed (handles Liquidsoap firing on_track multiple times per play)
FIX: Removed backward drift correction — it caused duplicate track sends to Liquidsoap queue, making playlists longer than expected
FIX: Schedule change now takes immediate priority — RefillQueueAsync aborts if schedule changed, preventing old playlist from continuing past its time slot
IMPROVE: GetCurrentlyPlayingIndexAsync replaces VerifyPositionAsync — only detects stuck tracks, no longer modifies _nextTrackToSend counter

CRITICAL FIX: Liquidsoap stuck detection — when Liquidsoap stops advancing (codec error, corrupt file), the plugin no longer spams queue.append every 5 seconds in an infinite drift correction loop
FIX: VerifyPositionAsync now returns current track index to RefillQueueAsync for stuck detection
FIX: RefillQueueAsync pauses queue refill when Liquidsoap is stuck (same track across consecutive checks)
FIX: Automatically resumes normal refill when Liquidsoap advances past the stuck track
FIX: ResetState clears stuck state (_isStuck, _lastKnownCurrentIdx)

FIX: Tracks silently dropped by Liquidsoap (codec issues, corrupt files) no longer cause premature playlist end — plugin now detects position drift every 5 seconds
FIX: Position verification compares Liquidsoap reality (current_track + queue.length) vs plugin counter to detect skipped tracks
FIX: Playlist now loops automatically when all tracks exhausted but schedule is still active — prevents dead air
IMPROVE: VerifyPositionAsync runs as part of RefillQueueAsync cycle — minimal overhead (one extra Telnet query)
IMPROVE: Detailed warning log when tracks are skipped with exact count of dropped tracks

FIX: NowPlaying endpoint now returns isPlaying=false when radio stops — was stuck showing last track forever
FIX: ResetState() now clears CurrentTrack so the endpoint correctly reflects when transmission has ended

NEW: Public artwork proxy endpoint at /RadioOnline/NowPlaying/Artwork — serves album art without authentication
NEW: No Content-Disposition header — displays inline in browser instead of downloading
NEW: Cache-Control: public, max-age=300 — browsers cache artwork for 5 minutes reducing server load
FIX: artworkUrl in NowPlaying JSON now points to the proxy endpoint instead of Jellyfin's internal image endpoint
IMPROVE: Content-Type detected from file extension (jpeg, png, gif, webp)
IMPROVE: Returns 404 gracefully if no track is playing or album has no image

FIX: NowPlaying artwork URL now uses album ID instead of song ID — songs don't have Primary images, the artwork lives on the parent album (folder.jpg)
FIX: Eliminates "does not have an image of type Primary" error
IMPROVE: NowPlayingInfo now stores AlbumId (falls back to ItemId if no album parent found)

Ratings.description: Professional rating system for Jellyfin. Rate media with 1-10 stars, view detailed user ratings on hover, and see rating badges on media cards. Optimized for large libraries with lazy loading.
Ratings.overview: Comprehensive rating plugin with star-based UI, average ratings display, detailed user rating popups, and performance-optimized card overlays for large media libraries.

versions.changelog: A new series gives one notification instead of one per episode. New episodes of a series you already have are grouped into one notification per season, showing which episodes arrived. Clicking a request pop-up opens that request, or the media once it is available.

Rating 10 is easier to reach. The red count on the request (+) button works on Jellyfin 12. Admins get a pop-up when someone makes a request, and users get one when their request is fulfilled. New-media pop-ups show posters and episode details again on Jellyfin 12.

Admins can remove any review. Users can hide their profile. New settings to turn off reviews and the Other Users tab. Ratings under 1 now save. Duplicates: Keep both button, correct series sizes, and no more false matches on music named "Track 01". Revision History updated.

Removes the "Unknown" cards with a blank poster and a "Not on server" tag from profiles. They were ratings of media that has since been deleted from the server and was rated before the plugin started remembering titles and posters, so there was nothing to show but the stars. They are now left out of the profile grid, reviews and activity. Deleted media that the plugin remembers keeps showing with its title and poster, as before. Nothing is deleted: if the media comes back to the library, its rating shows up again.

Fixes the stars and the reviews section appearing on library pages. Opening a library such as "Movies" or "TV Shows" from its header shows it on a details page, the same layout a movie uses, so the rating widget and "User Reviews" were added there too. People rated and reviewed the library itself, and the page then said you had rated "TV Shows". Libraries and folders no longer show the widget, and the server refuses a rating for them.

Adds a "Remove ratings left on libraries" button to the plugin's settings page, under the Jellyfin rating sync options. Updating does not delete ratings people already left on a library, and with the stars gone from library pages they could no longer remove them themselves. The button shows how many there are and on which libraries, including how many have a written review, and deletes them only after you confirm. The review text goes with them. Ratings on movies and shows are not touched.

Fixes plugin updates not reaching the browser at all. After updating, the page kept running the previous version's code, so everything fixed in a release looked like it had never been released, and only a manual hard refresh brought it through. The plugin adds its script tag to the page as Jellyfin sends it, but when the browser asked whether its copy of the page was still current, Jellyfin answered "unchanged" without sending the page - so there was nothing to add the tag to, and the browser reused its stored copy, still pointing at the old version's script, which is cached for a year on purpose and so was never re-requested. The page is now always sent in full and is no longer stored by the browser, so a new version shows up on the next ordinary page load. The large script and stylesheet keep their long-term caching.

Fixes the dashboard's Plugins page showing "An error occurred while loading plugins" after updating. Cleaning up the previous version's leftover folder removed it while Jellyfin was still running and still had it listed, and every later look at the plugin catalogue tried to write into a folder that was no longer there, which failed the whole page until Jellyfin was restarted. Only Linux and Docker servers were affected - on Windows the old files stay locked, so the folder was never actually removed. The cleanup now hands the old folder to Jellyfin to remove, the same way its own uninstall does.

Ratings can now be given to one decimal place from the rating window, not just from the stars on the movie page. Moving across the big stars shows the decimal you are about to pick and clicking takes it - 5.4, not 5 - and swiping on a phone does the same, with the star you stop on filled part-way to match. Previously each big star was a separate button, so the rating window could only ever give whole numbers. A decimal picked on the movie page also arrives in the window drawn correctly instead of being rounded down.

"No reviews yet. Be the first to write one!" is now a button. It looked like a caption, so people clicked it, nothing happened, and they scrolled back up to find the stars. It carries a pencil, highlights when you point at it, and opens the rating and review window.

Fixes a review not appearing after you write it. The review was always saved - the block of reviews further down the page just never re-read itself, so it kept showing whatever was there when the page opened, and the review only turned up once you had navigated away and back. That is why writing it a second time seemed to work: the first one had taken all along. The reviews now refresh as soon as a rating or review is added, changed or removed. A review written moments ago also used to be labelled "-1 days ago" instead of "Today", because the server stamps the time from its own clock and being a fraction of a second ahead of the browser was enough to push the age below zero.

Also fixes stale plugin folders being left behind after an update, mostly on Windows, where the old copy's file stays locked until Jellyfin restarts. The previous attempt deleted the old folder's meta.json to take it out of circulation, which turns out to do the opposite: Jellyfin treats a plugin folder with no meta.json as an active plugin named after the folder and loads it anyway. The result was two copies of this plugin running at once - doubled up services and duplicate endpoints, with the old copy able to answer requests - and a folder this plugin could no longer recognise in order to clean up. An old folder that cannot be deleted is now marked as deleted in its own manifest instead, which is what Jellyfin does itself: it is not loaded, and Jellyfin removes the folder at a later restart. Folders already left in the broken state are picked up and finished off.

Fixes the admin Ratings dashboard on Jellyfin 12, where every panel read "Failed to load" and the counters stayed empty. The dashboard's own pages were still identifying themselves the older way that Jellyfin 12 no longer accepts; they now use the current form, which Jellyfin 10.x accepts just as well, so one build covers both. The version shown at the top of the dashboard is now read from the plugin that is actually running instead of being typed into the page, so it can no longer drift out of date. The phone header also had a pass. Opening the plugin menu now keeps every button on a single line all the way down to a narrow phone, on a panel that spans the screen with even margins and rounded ends instead of sitting flush against one edge. The menu button and the account picture next to it were brought down to the size of everything else in the row, and while the menu is open the heading and the row-scrolling arrows underneath step out of sight so nothing shows through it. Closing it puts them straight back. The plugin's dialogs - media management, duplicates and the full ratings list - now fit inside a phone screen instead of pushing the page sideways.

A rebuilt rating system with real precision. Until now every rating was one of ten fixed steps, so a film was a 7 or an 8 with nothing in between. The whole star row is now a single sliding control: move across it and the stars fill smoothly under your pointer, a tenth of a star at a time, with the exact value appearing beside them as you go. Give something a 7.5 when 7 feels harsh and 8 feels generous. On a phone, swipe along the stars for the same control. The value appears while you are choosing and steps out of the way once you are done, so nothing clutters the page, and a deliberate press is still what saves a rating - simply passing over the stars never changes one you have already given. Everything you have rated before carries over untouched, and whole numbers work exactly as they always did.

Brings the header buttons back on Jellyfin 12. Jellyfin 12 rebuilt its web interface, and while it still leaves the old header in the page it collapses it to nothing - so the buttons were being created into something invisible. They now go into the new header, in the same place as before: immediately left of Jellyfin's own cast and search icons. The collapsed menu on phones is unchanged, and the buttons now also survive moving around the app, including in and out of the admin dashboard, which previously lost them until a manual refresh. Nothing changes on Jellyfin 10.x, where the old header is still used.

versions.changelog: Fix: re-added missing Pocket ID preset and other small UI fixes

The hardened OIDC rewrite on Jellyfin 12. Hand-rolled OIDC flow with Trust-On-First-Use discovery-endpoint pinning and an SSRF-guarded, DNS-rebind-pinned HTTP client. Account identity keyed on the OIDC subject, in its own identity-map file (migrated out of the plugin config on upgrade). Fail-closed role-to-policy RBAC with a server-wide admission allowlist. OIDC Back-Channel Logout 1.0. Client-secret indirection (Client Secret File / ENV_VAR reference). Auto-managed SSO login button in Branding. Rewritten admin config page. Opt-in, per-provider verified-email account linking that never binds an administrator account. Username/email/display-name/email-verified now fall back to the userinfo endpoint when the ID token omits them. Token-validation failures surface a plain-language reason (expired cert, audience/issuer mismatch, clock drift, JWKS rotation) instead of a bare error. Fixed OIDC-authenticated sessions showing a blank IP in Jellyfin's activity log. Fixed the Manage Library Access checkbox not responding to clicks. No configuration migration required from 2.0.0.0. Renamed to SSO-OIDC-Authentication (was SSO-OIDC Authentication) so the install folder no longer mixes a space with a hyphen; your saved settings are unaffected.

BREAKING: requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer will not load on 10.10/10.11 (stay on 1.0.7.x for those). Retargeted to .NET 10 and rebuilt against the Jellyfin 12.0 plugin API. Removed the vestigial IAuthenticationProvider.HasPassword override (dropped from the interface in 12.0). No functional changes to the OIDC login, RBAC, or Quick Connect flows.

Security: deny OIDC login when no RBAC role mapping (and no valid Default Role) matches the user's IdP roles, instead of silently letting login through with stale or default permissions — an intentional, unconditional fail-closed behavior change. Fix: declare style-src in the callback page's CSP and nonce the Quick Connect page's inline styles, closing a gap where that page was already CSP-non-compliant. Also: cosmetic redesign of the OIDC callback page (spinner, card layout, dark theme).

Security: evict stale entries from the rate limiter to prevent unbounded memory growth. Security: validate the OIDC picture-claim URL (scheme, host, redirects, size) before fetching it to prevent SSRF via a malicious/compromised IdP or self-service avatar. Security: block login/Quick Connect for a provider disabled mid-flow via an already-issued session token. Security: pin discovery and picture-fetch HTTP connections to the DNS-resolved address AuthorityGuard already validated, closing a DNS-rebinding TOCTOU gap. Also: OIDC callback page CSP now uses a per-response nonce instead of 'unsafe-inline'.

Fix: honor Jellyfin's Base URL setting in generated SSO links (login buttons, branding snippet, callback page) so they work behind a reverse-proxy base path. Feat: sign in native/mobile apps (Android, iOS/Swiftfin, Android TV) via a Quick Connect bridge, since the web login button doesn't reach them. Feat: sync the Jellyfin avatar from the IdP's picture claim on login, with a per-provider opt-out.

Feat: per-IP fixed-window rate limiting on OIDC auth endpoints. Fix: dead-code bug in ClaimParser where JSON array claim values were never parsed. CI: 77-test suite with AAA pattern coverage across all services and controllers.
Fix: role mappings added after a previous save were overwriting earlier ones. Rename plugin to SSO-OIDC Authentication.

versions.changelog:
Requests og Kalender i burger-menuen.

Når Jellyfin 12 kører med den gamle skuffe - f.eks. med New Badges' burger-knap
på brede skærme - lægges de to links nu også ind der, lige under Hjem. Menuen
lukker af sig selv, når man klikker på dem.

Styres af de indstillinger, der allerede findes (Requests-fanen og
Kalender-fanen). Ingen nye indstillinger.

Kun Jellyfin 12.

- Menupillen øverst findes nu også i et halvt vindue: ikoner, med navnet på den side du er på, og et hint på resten. På en telefon ligger alt i menuen som før.
- Den valgte knap i pillen er hvid i stedet for blå.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Hele topbaren i én knapgruppe på Jellyfin 12.

- Film, Serier og dine andre biblioteker er nu med i knapgruppen, efter Favoritter og før Tilføj og Kalender. Før stod de uden for, så gruppen så ud som en bar, der stoppede halvvejs.
- Det bibliotek, du er inde i, er fyldt ud i gruppen.
- Ingen tynd kant rundt om gruppen længere - over banneret lignede den en rest af den gamle topbar. Gruppen har nu en mørk, let sløret baggrund i stedet.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Ny topbar på Jellyfin 12.

- Hjem, Favoritter, Tilføj og Kalender er samlet i én knapgruppe, hvor den side, du er på, er fyldt ud. Før var Hjem slet ikke med, og den aktive side blev kun vist med blå tekst.
- Kortere navne: "Tilføj" og "Kalender" (på engelsk "Request" og "Calendar"), så topbaren også er plads til på en bærbar.
- Tilføj og Kalender virker nu også fra andre sider end forsiden - før skete der ingenting.
- Rettet: efter at have åbnet Kalender kunne både Tilføj og Kalender stå markeret, og i sidemenuen på mobilen kunne tre punkter være markeret på én gang.
- Rettet: at skifte fra Tilføj eller Kalender til Hjem eller Favoritter kunne vise to faner oven i hinanden.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Forsiden indlæses hurtigere.

- Kalenderens hukommelse - alle de titler, den har set - ligger nu i sin egen fil på serveren i stedet for i plugin-indstillingerne. Indstillingerne hentes af alle browsere ved hver sideindlæsning og var vokset til over 100 KB; nu er de få KB. Flytningen sker af sig selv, når serveren starter.
- Scriptet caches af browseren og hentes kun igen, når plugin'et er opdateret.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Udgivelseskalenderen viser ikke længere gamle film som Point Break og The Godfather.

TMDB registrerer hver gang en film bliver vist på tv eller lagt på en streamingtjeneste - i alle lande. Kalenderen tog den første dato den fandt, så en fransk tv-visning af Point Break fra 1991 dukkede op som en kommende udgivelse. Nu gælder:

- Film der allerede ligger i biblioteket, vises ikke i kalenderen.
- Kalenderen bruger den tidligste streamingdato, ikke den første der står på listen.
- En dato mere end to år efter filmens premiere er en genudgivelse og vises ikke.

Til Jellyfin 12.

"Test forbindelse"-knappen ser nu rigtig ud ved siden af Gem.

Efter sidste udgave var Gem-knappen tegnet om til Jellyfin 12's stil, men "Test forbindelse" lige under den sad tilbage i den gamle grå udgave, så de to knapper så ud til at være lige vigtige.

Den er nu en omridset knap i temaets farve — samme størrelse som Gem, men tydeligt den sekundære af de to, præcis som Jellyfin 12 selv tegner et sådant knappepar.

Kun udseende. Knappen gør nøjagtig det samme som før.

Indstillingssiden er tegnet om, så den ser ud som resten af Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin 12 har lavet sine egne indstillingssider om: felterne er nu fyldte bokse med en lille etiket øverst i selve feltet, i stedet for en label ovenover. Denne side fulgte stadig den gamle stil og stak derfor ud fra alt andet i dashboardet.

Felter, afkrydsningsfelter, overskrifter og Gem-knappen matcher nu Jellyfin 12's egne — samme højde, samme afrunding, samme farver. Farverne hentes fra Jellyfin 12's eget tema, så siden også følger med hvis du skifter tema.

Kun udseende. Der er ikke ændret noget i hvad siden gør, eller i indstillingerne selv. På Jellyfin 10.11 ser siden ud præcis som før — den nye stil slås kun til, hvis serveren rent faktisk er 12.

Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12.

Fanerne "Tilføj Film/Serie" og "Udgivelseskalender" er flyttet med. Jellyfin 12 har lavet hele den øverste menulinje om, og den gamle fanerække findes stadig i siden men bliver aldrig tegnet — så fanerne blev lagt et sted ingen kunne se dem. De sidder nu i den rigtige menulinje sammen med Favoritter, Film og Serier, og i menuen i siden på telefon.

Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende adgangsnøglen på (X-Emby-Token), så alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt. Uden det svarede serveren 401.

Indstillingssiden kunne ikke åbnes på Jellyfin 12. Pluginet kørte, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun siden, hvis den selv beder om at komme i menuen.

Accentfarven læses nu direkte fra temaet. Før blev den gættet ved at male en usynlig knap med Jellyfins egne klasser og aflæse farven — men Jellyfin 12 tegner sine knapper på en ny måde hvor den klasse ikke findes, så gættet slog fejl og faldt tilbage til en fast farve.

Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan kun installeres der. Kører du stadig 10.11, bliver du på den forrige udgave, som virker uændret — serveren vælger selv den rigtige. Grunden til at der skal være to: 10.11 og 12 kører på hver sin udgave af .NET, så det samme build kan ikke køre begge steder.

Udgivelseskalenderen viser ikke længere gamle film som Point Break og The Godfather.

TMDB registrerer hver gang en film bliver vist på tv eller lagt på en streamingtjeneste - i alle lande. Kalenderen tog den første dato den fandt, så en fransk tv-visning af Point Break fra 1991 dukkede op som en kommende udgivelse. Nu gælder:

- Film der allerede ligger i biblioteket, vises ikke i kalenderen.
- Kalenderen bruger den tidligste streamingdato, ikke den første der står på listen.
- En dato mere end to år efter filmens premiere er en genudgivelse og vises ikke.

Til Jellyfin 10.11 - samme rettelse, uden ændringerne fra 12-udgaverne.

Server Sync.description: Server Sync keeps a pool of Jellyfin servers in step. Each server scans the others it is told to in priority order and pulls missing or updated content, metadata, people, user settings, playlists, and watch history. Servers that both run the plugin also tell each other about changes as they happen, so an edit or a play made on one shows up on the others within seconds, and the scheduled scan remains the safety net. Watch history merges three way against what the servers last agreed on, and other values resolve on where and when they were last edited, so the newest edit always wins.
Server Sync.overview: Keep several Jellyfin servers in step: content, metadata, people, users, playlists, and watch history.

versions.changelog:
## Changed
- Servers no longer need the same Server Sync version. Live changes, history negotiation, and conflict checks work between any two versions that speak a compatible protocol, so a pool can be updated one server at a time. Releases up to 12.2.8.1 only talk to exactly their own version, so this first update still needs every server in the pool updated
- Check Link and the Queue explain a protocol mismatch, naming which server to update
- After Sync Content downloads or removes files, Jellyfin refreshes just the folders that changed instead of scanning every library. A run that touches many folders still runs one full scan
- A file that arrives as a live change refreshes only its own folder
- The recycling bin only expires files and trickplay folders the plugin put there. Anything else in that folder is left alone, however old

## Fixed
- A source server that is slow to answer or briefly busy is asked again instead of failing the read. One timed out page no longer throws away a server's whole listing for the run
- A library that changes while it is being scanned is listed a second time, so pruning still runs instead of being skipped on every busy library
- A download that drops partway resumes from where it stopped, and starts over if the file changed on the source in between
- Downloads running at the same time hold disk space for each other, so several large files can no longer fill a disk together. A file that only fits once another download finishes waits for it
- Recycling a file from deep inside a library no longer fails on the filesystem's name length limit
- Recycled files renamed to avoid a name clash now expire with the rest
- A live change for an item the other server did not have yet no longer silences that item's changes for a day once it arrives
- A peer that spells its server id in a different case is one peer in the queue, so its changes count once toward its limit and are never applied twice
- An Ignored content row keeps its retry count through a scan, like every other table

## Developer
- The wire protocol is versioned separately from the plugin, through the X-ServerSync-Protocol and X-ServerSync-Min-Protocol headers and the ProtocolVersion and MinProtocolVersion fields on Capabilities. A peer without them is matched on its exact plugin version
- Reads use a small pool of read connections beside the write connection, so the dashboard and lookups no longer wait behind writes
- Scans write their rows in transactions of 250 instead of one commit per row, and prune and retire in batches
- Every sync table builds its upsert from one shared column list, so the rules for Ignored rows and synced hashes are written once
- Reads that time out, drop, or meet a busy server are retried up to three times with backoff and Retry-After. Writes are never retried there
- The source client is split by area and its paging loops share one walker that keeps each caller's own error handling
- The Sync dashboard script is split into modules per table and the queue
- The refresh and sync task bases share their server connection and run recording code
- Schema v31 stores inbound hint origins in one case and merges duplicates
- New tests cover the retry handler, resumable downloads, disk space holds, recycled names, batched writes, read connections, protocol checks, changed folders, the table manager base, the content and playlist tasks, and playlist storage

## Fixed
- A change from another server for an item this server does not have waits up to six hours for the item instead of seven days, then is dropped with one short log line per server rather than an entry per change. A new item brings its metadata with it, so nothing is lost.

## Developer
- Built for Jellyfin 12.2 (target ABI 12.2.0.0). Servers on Jellyfin 12.0 or 12.1 keep the previous release.
- Updated test dependencies (Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.11, NSubstitute 6.2, xunit 2.9.3, xunit.runner.visualstudio 4.0.1).
- Microsoft.Data.Sqlite follows Jellyfin 12.2 at 10.0.11.
- The integration harness runs on the jellyfin/jellyfin:12.2.20261005-225228 image.

## Fixed
- A download whose source stops sending is abandoned as stalled after two minutes without data and retried, instead of holding Sync Content forever
- Deleting a file from the Sync tab deletes only that file, its companions, its thumbnails and trickplay, never another version or file in the same folder
- With Remove empty folders on, a deleted item that leaves its folder holding only title artwork and nfo files removes those and then the folder, for deletions from the Sync tab and automatic ones alike. Any other file or subfolder keeps the folder untouched
- Disc folders and multi part items are refused on the Sync tab with a reason, instead of being reported deleted. An item whose file is already gone has only its stale library entry removed
- The recycling bin takes an item's thumbnails and trickplay with it and clears them out with the rest when they expire, never touching folders it did not put there
- Image copies in Metadata, People and User sync give up after two minutes without data instead of waiting forever
- A server that connects and has nothing to download forgets its earlier connection failures
- The download circuit breaker counts failed downloads across runs and only resets after a download succeeds
- The unused LastConnectionCheck setting is gone. Saved settings that still hold it load as before
- The plugin catalog description matches the plugin
- The multi server plan in the docs is marked historical and uses the current mode names
- Updated Jellyfin.Sdk to the stable 2026.10.12 release

## Security
- Changing a server's address on the Servers tab drops its stored API key or sign in, so it is never sent to the new address. The page clears the key field and says to enter the key or sign in again
- The publish workflow reads the release notes through gh and checks the downloaded checksum, so a release body can never run as a shell command

## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.19.

## Developer
- Hidden titles go back to Synced when they return on the source or Removed files leaves Ignore, instead of staying Ignored after the .ignore is removed
- Integration tests cover Removed files set to Ignore, switching between Keep, Delete and Ignore, a user's own .ignore, and a single gone episode
- Integration tests cover updating from 12.2.7.0 and from older versions with the Whitelist

## Developer
- Removed files has a new Ignore option that hides a movie or show folder with a .ignore file once everything in it is gone from the source, and never hides a season on its own
- Hidden titles show again when they come back on the source or when Removed files leaves Ignore, and a .ignore the plugin did not write is never touched
- Waiting deletions are cancelled when Removed files is not Delete, so switching to Keep or Ignore never removes a file
- Deleting a file from the Sync tab keeps its row as Ignored so it is not downloaded again, and queueing it brings it back
- Updating from before 12.2.7 adds API keys and every administrator to the Whitelist once, so servers that pull from this one keep working
- The Servers tab says where to add the Whitelist row when the other server refuses this one
- A server running another Server Sync version never overwrites edits recorded here, and changes for it wait in the queue until both match
- An item a peer changed that is announced more than ten times in ten minutes stops being announced, so two servers can never echo a change forever. Deletions always go out
- Playlist copies are recorded in the sync database, moved over from playlist-copies.json, and rebuilt from their tags after a reset
- Playlist copies keep their tags after Jellyfin refreshes them
- Upkeep forgets copies of deleted playlists and removes replacement backups left next to finished downloads
- Identify names each result after its server
- The README is shorter and the API reference moved to docs/API.md
- The docs say plainly that both servers must keep the same folder structure under each mapped library

## Developer
- Playlists sync between servers for mapped users, with each item matched by its path and items not on this server left out until they arrive
- Playlist edits and deletions are sent as they happen. Pull keeps the parent's copy, Push overrides the other server, and Sync keeps the newest edit
- Playlist sharing and public access are copied when the new Sharing option is on
- Playlist Sync needs a user mapping, and playlists of users without one never leave their server
- Test Connection shows what the key can do on that server, who it belongs to, and whether it may download media
- Test Connection says whether the other server's whitelist lets this key in, and why not
- A standard user's key works for Pull, Push, and Sync, limited to what that user can see and that user's own history, settings, and playlists
- Sync Content skips a server whose key may not download media and logs why
- Check Link reports the access the other server holds for this one
- The sync endpoints only accept administrators from servers on the Servers tab and users on the new Whitelist, each with the locations they may call from
- Whitelist host names are remembered and looked up again when a caller stops matching, so dynamic DNS keeps working
- Refused sync calls are logged with the user, the address, and the reason
- Servers that pull from this one without being on its Servers tab need a Whitelist row after updating
- The plugin's endpoints moved from /ServerSync to /Sync
- Every sync type in Settings shows what a standard user and an administrator can do
- Settings descriptions are shorter, and retries, approvals, and download speed are tables
- Settings groups the sync types under Synchronization
- User Sync and History Sync only use the key's own user when the key is a standard user's
- The new Permissions page in the docs lists what each function needs
- Identify lists every server that has the item, in the Servers tab order, and picking one keeps the item on that server
- The image picker shows the images of every server that has the item, each named after its server
- Log entries strip control characters from values another server sends

## Developer
- Activity entries for changes sent again, paused peers, and rejected requests name the items involved and say why
- Activity entry details start with a capital letter
- Metadata provider image previews load from the server's External URL when one is set, so a server reached at an internal address still shows them

## Developer
- The metadata provider matches by the item's provider ids when the file path does not match, and seasons and episodes by the show's ids with their season and episode numbers
- The metadata provider logs why it found no match for an item
- A server that could not be reached or runs another version is asked again after 30 seconds

## Developer
- Every server in a pool must run the same Server Sync version. Calls from another version are refused, and Check Link names both versions. Update every server together
- Hints are answered with a code that says what the receiver did with them
- Each server tells the others what it wants from them, so changes outside its mapped libraries, users, and filters are never sent
- A change the other server turned away is held back from it for a day, or until the settings on either side change
- A hint for an item a server does not have yet waits up to seven days and applies when the item arrives. The queue view shows these as waiting for the item
- A server that already holds the same or a newer edit answers straight away without fetching anything
- Server Sync is a metadata and image provider for every media type. Enable it in a library's metadata and image fetchers to fill new items from the servers it pulls from
- Content and Metadata scans read only what changed on each server. A full scan runs every 24 hours, set by Full Scan Every under Processing
- Peer status reads need the asking server's id and its pairing
- Removed unused API routes
