ShareLinks.description: Adds secure, expiring guest-share links for Jellyfin items using temporary hidden users, one-use token redemption, restrictive policies, and scheduled cleanup.
ShareLinks.overview: Temporary guest links for Jellyfin movies and episodes.

versions.changelog: Fixes shared movies failing with "media could not be found" when an intro plugin like Local Intros is installed (#23). The intros aren't part of the share, so the guest couldn't open them and playback stopped before the movie. Guests now skip intros, and any video or audio a guest can't open is left out of what the server sends them, whichever plugin or endpoint it came from.
Fixes share links on Jellyfin 12 and the ShareLink button missing on new Docker installs.

Fixes redemption on Jellyfin 10.11.9 and later (#19). Jellyfin changed the signature of the method the plugin uses to set a guest's password, so every link failed with a MissingMethodException and the guest landed on the dead-link page. The plugin now picks whichever version of that method the server has, so the same build works on every 10.11 release. Tested on 10.11.8 and 10.11.11.

Guests are now blocked from other plugins' API endpoints on the server, not just hidden from their UI in the browser. A share guest holds a real Jellyfin token, so anything that only hid a button left the endpoint answering it. Jellyfin's own API is untouched: the share tag already limits it to the shared title, and playback needs it. The config page lists your installed plugins with a checkbox each, so you can let one through when it genuinely needs to serve guests, such as an intro skipper. The guest hidden selectors setting is renamed to say what it is: cosmetic, it tidies the view and enforces nothing. Also fixes the dashboard devices page coming up empty after a share expired: deleting a guest left its device row behind, and a device whose user is missing makes Jellyfin fail the whole device listing rather than skip one row.

Fixes a season share exposing the rest of the series: the tag was going onto the season's parent series, and Jellyfin treats a parent's tags as belonging to all of its children, so every other season became visible to the guest. Tagging now only ever goes downwards. Take this update if you have shared a season with a link that is still live. Also in this release: a link can be made multi-use from the create popup so several people can use it until it expires, with a configurable ceiling on how many watch at once (ten by default), and the dashboard gains a "Clean up finished links" button that removes revoked, expired and failed records.

The ShareLink button now sits in its own section at the bottom of the item menu, and only appears for a movie, series, season or episode instead of turning up on things like a cast member. It is properly admin only again: the current user was cached for the whole page, so switching accounts in the same tab could leave the button visible to a normal user (the server always refused them). Share tags are hidden from everyone except admins, on the title and in the tag filter. Security: one-use links can no longer be redeemed twice, the configured maximum expiry is respected, the raw token is dropped from storage when a link dies, the token secret file is 0600, guest accounts can no longer sign in from the login page at all, and the runtime reflection shims around Jellyfin's APIs are gone.

Series and seasons can now be shared, not just single movies and episodes: the share tags the whole tree so the guest can browse and play everything inside it, and cleanup strips it all again. Expired or invalid links now show a friendly page that redirects to the Jellyfin home instead of raw JSON. The guest hidden selectors setting now defaults to empty.

ShareLink button on the item menu, temporary guest users confined by tag policy, expiring links with a date/time picker, admin dashboard with revoke, and a configurable guest lockdown that hides tag/genre/studio/cast links, the add-to-playlist and add-to-collection actions, and other plugins' UI. The creation popup is localized in English and French. Guest sessions are now minted server side: no password is ever stored or sent anywhere, the guest page only carries a session token, and expired guests are cleaned up every 30 minutes.

versions.changelog: - Fix: the v1.0.3.0 sidebar entry didn't actually appear — Jellyfin gates main-menu items on `EnableInMainMenu`, not just `MenuSection`. Setting both now puts Show Tracker in the dashboard sidebar.
- Improvement: the Show Tracker page now appears as its own entry in the Jellyfin Dashboard sidebar (Server section), instead of being buried under Dashboard → Plugins → My Plugins → Show Tracker.

- Feature: clicking a show's poster or title in the dashboard now opens that show's page in your Jellyfin library (jumps straight to the seasons/episodes view). Expand/collapse on the rest of the row still works for inspecting missing episodes inline.

Falls back to title/airdate matching, detects absolute (anime-style) numbering, and flags shows where the TVMaze match is likely wrong (e.g. anime vs. live-action remake with the same name).
- New per-show `MatchMode` and `MatchConfidence` fields, surfaced in the dashboard as a "Match info" note.

SmartCovers.description: Cover provider for Jellyfin libraries. Renders PDF first pages with a built-in PDFium, takes the image named as the cover, else the first page, of CBZ and CBR comics, finds the cover inside EPUB and MOBI files, and pulls embedded artwork from audio files and folder audiobooks with Jellyfin's ffmpeg. When the file has no cover and online fetching is on (the default), fetches one from Open Library and then Google Books.
SmartCovers.overview: Cover extraction for books, audiobooks, comics, and music — with online fallback via Open Library & Google Books.

versions.changelog: Audiobooks that are a folder of tracks get a cover: the book identity now comes from the folder (climbing out of disc folders), covers already on disk are found under any name, folder items get a cover, and one lookup serves a whole book. MOBI/AZW covers. A daily scheduled task retries items that never got a cover. Edition and narration tags are stripped before searching. A crafted MOBI header can no longer index past the record.

Fix plugin loading as NotSupported on Jellyfin 10.11 servers: the CBZ/CBR archive reader (SharpCompress) is now merged into SmartCovers.dll, so the plugin scanner no longer hits an unresolvable reference. No separate SharpCompress.dll is shipped anymore.

Address review findings: stricter BMP validation (DIB header check), exclude unverifiable TIFF entries from comic candidate selection, bounded single-pass candidate selection for pathological archives, and ship THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md inside the plugin zip.

CBZ/CBR comic-archive cover extraction: first page in natural order (or an explicitly named cover entry), content-sniffed format detection so mislabeled archives work, RAR4/RAR5/solid support, junk filtering and magic-byte verification. BMP artwork detection added.

Fix a crash that could take down the whole Jellyfin server when the PDFium native library failed to load. Restore PDF cover rendering on Windows (x64/x86/arm64). Honor the JPEG quality setting. Harden native-library resolution across platforms.
Built-in PDF rendering via PDFium (no poppler-utils needed). Music library support. SkiaSharp 3.x compatibility.
Rename to SmartCovers (Jellyfin branding compliance). All namespaces, DLL, and provider names updated.
See https://github.com/GeiserX/smart-covers/releases/tag/v5.0.0.0

SmartLists.description: Create smart, rule-based playlists and collections in Jellyfin — for movies, shows, music, or anything your library holds. A single genre rule takes seconds; stack rules into groups and you can express almost anything. Either way, they keep themselves up to date.

versions.changelog:
Features:
- Bumpers per break: a break can now play up to 10 bumpers back to back. The new "Take turns between bumper rule groups" option gives each bumper rule group its own pool, so every break can follow a pattern such as ident, commercial, ident (#542).
- Missing items (admin page): see which entries of a list's external lists are not in your library, with their position, title, type and IDs, and download them as CSV (#544).
- New Is 3D rule field for videos. Jellyfin detects 3D from tags in the file name, such as [3D MVC] or .3D.hsbs (#538).
- New Match alternate versions option: rules also check each alternate version of a movie or episode, such as a 3D or 1080p copy behind a 4K version. The video is added when any of its versions matches. The option appears below the rules when a rule checks something that can differ between versions, such as Is 3D, Resolution or File Name (#538).
- Is Favorite has a new parent favorite option, to match items whose album, season, series or folder is a favorite - for example every track on the albums you have favorited (#535).
- The SmartLists sidebar entry is now hidden from users who can't use the user page (while it's disabled, or when they're not in Allowed Users). Administrators always see it. Requires Plugin Pages 3.0.0.0 or later (#558).

Bug Fixes:
- Security: smart playlists and user-owned smart collections could include items from libraries the user has no access to. Lists now only contain items from libraries the user can see. The same applies to bumpers: bumpers from a library the playlist's user can't access are left out.
- When an external list can't be fetched (for example the provider is down or there's a network error), lists that use it are now left unchanged for that refresh instead of being emptied (#555).
- External List Order could sort by positions from other playlists' external lists when several lists refreshed together, such as with Refresh All (#543).
- Resolution rules could skip a movie whose alternate version has a higher resolution than its main version (#546).
- Scheduled playlist refreshes now run through the same refresh queue as every other refresh, so they no longer overlap other refreshes (#539).
- An all-users playlist with a rule tied to one user (for example Is Favorite for user B) now refreshes every user's copy when that user's data changes, not only that user's own copy.
- Per-group Max Items and Rule Group Order no longer drop or misplace episodes added through a Collections rule's "include episodes within series" option.
- During a refresh of several lists, a list with a Library Name rule and a list without one could share the same item pool, so one could show missing items or the other could miss them.
- The list Actions menu now opens upward when it would otherwise be cut off at the bottom of the screen (#561).
- The page shown to users without access to the user page no longer breaks the Jellyfin layout.

Improvements:
- Cover images now use the image library built into Jellyfin. Manual installs: delete SixLabors.ImageSharp.dll from the plugin folder; repository installs are not affected. Uploaded GIF, BMP and TIFF covers are no longer badged or cropped, and an animated WebP keeps only its first frame while the badge is on.
- The refresh status API no longer returns batchCurrentIndex and batchTotalCount; they were always empty.

Full changelog: https://jellyfin-smartlists-plugin.dinsten.se/changelog/stable/

Features:
- New rule field: Aspect Ratio (under Video). Filter by a video's display
  aspect ratio such as 16:9 or 2.35:1. Comparisons are proportional, so
  "less than 1:1" matches every portrait video and "greater than 1:1" every
  landscape one - no need to list each ratio.
- Live TV Channel media type for smart collections. Group channels from any
  Live TV tuner into a collection with rules such as Name, Tags or Is
  Favorite. Collections only - Jellyfin playlists cannot hold channels
  (#290).
- "Hide when empty" is now "Min Items": a list stays hidden until it holds
  at least that many items, instead of only while it is completely empty.
  Found under Limits next to Max Items, with a matching default in
  Settings. Existing lists keep their current behaviour with no changes
  needed.

Bug Fixes:
- MDBList official list URLs (mdblist.com/lists/official/movies/... and
  .../shows/...) returned no items. They now load, and the JustWatch
  Streaming Charts list keeps the country, period, provider and genre
  filters from the pasted URL (#525).

Full changelog: https://jellyfin-smartlists-plugin.dinsten.se/changelog/stable/

Same plugin as v12.0.1.0 - no functional changes. It exists so that servers
upgraded from Jellyfin 10.11 to Jellyfin 12 automatically pick up the correct
build.

Bug Fixes:
- Upgrading Jellyfin from 10.11 to 12 left the plugin showing "Not supported".
  Each release published its 10.11 and its 12 build under the same version
  number, so a server that had installed the 10.11 build kept it after the
  upgrade - Jellyfin saw no newer version to offer, and the 10.11 build cannot
  run on Jellyfin 12. This release is published for Jellyfin 12 only, so those
  servers now see an update and repair themselves. Jellyfin 10.11 servers are
  unaffected and stay on v12.0.1.0.

Full changelog: https://jellyfin-smartlists-plugin.dinsten.se/changelog/stable/

The first stable release for Jellyfin 12, and the biggest update yet - 22 release
candidates of work since v10.11.30.2. Jellyfin 10.11 is still fully supported.

Jellyfin 12:
- Full support for Jellyfin 12, including the final 12.0.0 release
- Jellyfin 10.11 continues to receive the same updates

New features:
- List templates: one-click starting points on the Create tab
- Hide when empty: a list disappears while nothing matches, and returns on its own
- Group results into collections: turn an item search into a collection of collections
- Collection and Playlist media types: build collections of collections or playlists
- Smart collections now carry genres, studios, parental rating and total runtime
- Smart list badge on generated covers, with a setting to turn it off
- Integration API so other tools can create and manage smart lists
- Bumpers, and random group selection
- New rule field: User Rating
- Date rules can include items whose date is missing from metadata
- New settings for default media types and for hiding new lists when empty

External lists:
- New providers: ListenBrainz and Scrob
- Music lists match tracks via MusicBrainz, one library item per matched track
- User-Agent setting for when a provider starts blocking requests

Sorting:
- Least Recently Watched Round Robin, and Shuffled Round Robin
- Round Robin can group by Collection and order items within each group
- Crossover episodes that aired close together play back-to-back, with an Air Window setting
- Play Count (all users) and Last Played (all users)

Improvements:
- Large speed-up for expensive rules - people, languages, resolution and more are read once per refresh
- Parent tags, studios and genres are found at every level above an item, including the library
- Only fully watched episodes advance the Least Recently Watched rotation
- Weekly cleanup removes leftover playlists and collections whose list is gone
- Rule groups are named consistently throughout; the sort option is now Rule Group Order

Bug fixes:
- Titles containing numbers sort correctly - "Season 2" before "Season 10"
- The Resolution sort did nothing and left lists sorted by name
- Episodes came back unordered when Season/Episode was combined with another sort
- A series showed a play count of 0 even when every episode was watched
- Items with no release date no longer match "before", "older than" and "not equals"
- IMDb lists, charts and awards failed to load with a "Forbidden" error
- Configuration pages loaded blank behind a reverse proxy, or with Cloudflare Rocket Loader
- Smart collections disappeared when the TMDbBoxSets plugin was installed
- Duplicates left behind by a failed deletion are detected and cleaned up
- List names can contain : * ? < > | " / and \ again
- Saving a list now reports why it failed instead of appearing to do nothing
- A failed save no longer discards what you typed
- Deleting a list right after editing it no longer brings it back

Existing lists may change:
- Rules checking parent values now look at every level above an item, so they match more
- Music lists are the most visible case: artist folder and library values now count
- Similar To applies within its own rule group instead of filtering the whole list
- Smart collections now carry aggregated genres/studios/runtime, so other lists may match them
- Include-only checkboxes are migrated automatically to Name rules

Full changelog: https://jellyfin-smartlists-plugin.dinsten.se/changelog/stable/

SponsorBlock.description: Skip sponsored segments in YouTube videos using SponsorBlock data.

versions.changelog: Add an opt-in Jellyfin metadata source for YouTube IDs. Preserve filename and custom-regex matching as the default, read validated Youtube provider IDs imported from NFO uniqueid metadata, and expose the source choice in plugin settings.

Add Jellyfin 12 support. Retarget to .NET 10 and Jellyfin Controller 12.0.0-rc3, implement the new media-segment cleanup contract, and preserve the event-driven SponsorBlock workflow without enabling the core library segment scan.
Serialize SponsorBlock processing to avoid concurrent refresh and playback work for the same item. Bump the plugin version for local installation.

Add Done state with convergence-based polling. Videos older than 30 days (by YouTube publish date) are fetched once and frozen. Videos younger than 30 days are polled daily until segment data is unchanged for 5 consecutive checks, then frozen. Stale segments are now deleted when SponsorBlock data disappears. Daily scan task refactored to a clean two-phase dispatcher.

Add dedicated SponsorBlock log file (log_SponsorBlock_YYYYMMDD.log) in Jellyfin's log directory. All info/warning/error events now write to both the main server log and the dedicated file, so the plugin appears as a separate log entry in the Jellyfin dashboard.

Add comprehensive logging to the orchestrator and triggers. Every decision point (scope check, path empty, ID extraction failure, state-machine skip, segment write, state transition) now logs at information or debug level, so issues are diagnosable directly from the Jellyfin log dashboard.
Fix EnumerateScoped to discover Episode and Movie items, not just standalone Video. YouTube libraries imported as TV Shows store items as Episode type, which BaseItemKind.Video did not match.

Fix automatic loading for old archives and restore DLL-only release packaging. The daily refresh now discovers selected-library videos older than the sanity-check window, old untracked items use their Jellyfin DateCreated for the 48-hour decision, and NoData rows recheck after cooldown instead of being terminal.

Add a one-shot Force Scan button for existing archives. Admins can backfill every video in the selected libraries once, while the normal daily refresh stays limited to tracked Pending and HasData items. Includes duplicate-scan protection and status endpoints.

Repair pruned SponsorBlock segments on playback. When Jellyfin refreshes a changed media file it can delete generated MediaSegment rows while the plugin state still says HasData; playback start now verifies that Jellyfin still has segment rows and re-fetches/recreates them if they were pruned.

versions.changelog: Fixes for 1.8.0, almost all reported by users of it. JELLYFIN 12.1: StarTrack appears in the new Material-UI top bar - 12.1 moved navigation there and the nav drawer the My Ratings link used is not in that layout (#27). FIXES: opening a film from My Ratings no longer freezes page scrolling (six code paths closed the overlay and only one released the scroll lock, leaving the whole web UI unscrollable until a reload) (#27); Back closes My Ratings instead of navigating the page behind it (#27); half stars are cut at the middle of the glyph again (#27); 'out of ten' now applies to your own ratings too, not only community averages - panel, recent list, cards, diary and comparison (#27); Letterboxd 'Verify login' opens its session the way a real push does - it never used FlareSolverr, so a correct server still failed it, and a stale pasted cookie was used forever and never questioned, which is worse than none - it now retries without your cookies and on a fresh challenge and says what actually fixes a Cloudflare block (#24); the self-check no longer reports a failure for a read-only index.html, the normal state in Docker, on a server that is injecting perfectly well by its other route (#20); a duplicate copy of a film in the library no longer collects a second rating on import. NEW: StarTrack tells you when your browser is running a cached old copy of it, with a Reload button, and never reloads on its own (#20); a My Ratings button in the rating panel (#28); remove from watchlist directly from the watchlist (#28).

NEW: StarTrack tells you when your browser is running a cached old copy of it, with a Reload button, and never reloads on its own (#20); a My Ratings button in the rating panel (#28); remove from watchlist directly from the watchlist (#28).

Jellyfin 12 support from one codebase: two builds, 1.8.0.0 for 10.11 and 1.8.0.1 for 12; the catalogue picks the right one. LETTERBOXD: 'Sync everything' imports your whole profile live - every rating including films rated but never logged, every dated diary entry, then watchlist, likes and Top 4 - with never-logged films placed in the order you rated them; watchlist sync works again (Letterboxd removed the RSS feed, the page is read instead); likes, Top 4 and sign-in get through Cloudflare via an optional FlareSolverr, and back off politely with a visible note without one; imports never overwrite reviews or dates they do not carry; a known year is a matching constraint (Fall 2022 is not The Fall 2006); duplicate library copies rate the one you already rated; likes are dated by the viewing, not the import. SIMKL: pull converges (#19) - any shared id matches. FIXES: tick boxes hidden by global CSS themes; poster badges fetched in one batch instead of one request per card; settings-load failures say so instead of showing everything unticked. Two-way Letterboxd and Serializd, plus season ratings. LETTERBOXD: push ratings, watched status, likes, your watchlist and dated diary entries back, either as a CSV that needs no password or as an hourly automatic push; an overwrite toggle decides whether a push may change a rating that already exists remotely (off by default). SERIALIZD (new): the television-only counterpart to Letterboxd. Importing needs only your username, because the diary is public - no password is stored; pushing series, season and episode ratings needs the account password, encrypted at rest. SEASONS: a whole season is now rateable alongside movies, series and episodes, with its own panel, overlay tab and Top 4 row. Season ratings are deliberately withheld from Letterboxd, Trakt, Simkl and Yamtrack, which have no concept of them. DIARY: a dated 'log a watch' control, automatic logging when playback finishes, and automatic rewatch detection. FIXES: Simkl import returned nothing at all (#19); the post-playback rating popup missed the playing item on 10.11.11 (#21); the hide-Letterboxd and hide-External-Sync toggles had no effect (#23); the TV rating panel opened but the stars could not be reached with a remote (#8); the release zip shipped without meta.json, so manual installs reported 'Not supported' (#22); the widget injection corrupted index.html on every update, leaving self-referential script tags that made browsers re-download the page as JavaScript - existing damage is now repaired automatically. In-place upgrade; no StarTrack data migration.

Media-page and TV/webOS fixes plus native-rating and BaseURL follow-ups. Issue #11/#8: keeps one canonical clickable StarTrack badge, removes legacy and attribute-stripped ghost copies, and reliably hides Jellyfin's delayed native community-rating node when replacement is enabled. Issue #8: whole-star controls are D-pad focusable/selectable with webOS-compatible focus feedback. Issue #12: adds an elevation-gated, idempotent admin backfill for existing ratings into Jellyfin's native per-user rating field. Issue #13: native item, poster, and avatar requests consistently respect Jellyfin's BaseURL sub-path. Release workflow now uses .NET 9. In-place upgrade; no StarTrack data migration.

TV/webOS accessibility, reverse-proxy sub-path support, native-rating mirror, and media-page badge fixes. TV / webOS (#8, locksoft): the media-page rating badge is now a focusable button the TV remote's D-pad can reach, is always shown on TV (dimmed when an item has no ratings yet) so there's always something to select, and shows the rating number in white (IMDb-style). The floating Rate pill is reachable by the D-pad, the post-playback rating popup is usable with a remote, and Large / Large (TV only) sizes now apply correctly on a TV. A per-device rating size (Normal / Large / Large (TV only)) can be set from My Ratings -> Preferences. Reverse-proxy sub-path (#13, LinkdxTTV): the widget and all its API calls now respect Jellyfin's BaseURL sub-path setting, so StarTrack works when Jellyfin is served under a path like /jelly behind nginx. Native rating mirror (#12, damientkyt): an optional 'Also save ratings to Jellyfin's native rating field' setting (off by default) mirrors each StarTrack rating into Jellyfin's built-in per-user rating (0.5-5 stars mapped to 0-10), so it shows in Jellyfin's own UI and works with library filters and backups; it is cleared when you remove the rating. Media-page badge (#11 / #8, khutede / locksoft): the badge no longer duplicates, goes stale, or disappears on web and iPad. In-place upgrade, no data migration.

Community bug-fixes and options (#8, #10, #11). The rating badge no longer appears two or three times on media detail pages (Jellyfin caches the page DOM; stale copies are now cleared) and the badge is clickable to open the rating panel. It drops the '(1)' count for a single rating, and a new 'Compact media-page badge' option shows just the score. The badge now sits before the IMDb / Rotten Tomatoes / community ratings so your own rating reads first. Review length is now an admin setting (default 10000; lower it, e.g. 1000) - completes #10 (thanks @debrunbaix). New 'Rating badge size' option (Normal / Large / Large on TV only) enlarges the poster badges, the floating Rate pill and the whole rating panel including the clickable stars - handy on 4K TVs; 'Large on TV only' auto-applies on TV web clients and stays normal on phone/desktop. The floating pill and badge are now reachable with a TV remote's D-pad (OK/Enter opens the panel). All new settings translated in 8 languages. Also fixes injected-widget cache-busting so plugin updates reliably reach browsers. No data migration needed.

External Rating Sync — two-way sync of your StarTrack ratings with Trakt, Simkl, and Yamtrack. Connect an account (Trakt device-code, Simkl PIN), pick One-way or Two-way, and StarTrack mirrors ratings in both directions with newer-wins conflict resolution so a fresh local edit is never clobbered by a stale remote value. Syncs automatically every 10 minutes. Also pushes watched history (marks films/episodes played on the service) and likes (Trakt Favorites + a 'StarTrack Liked' list). New one-shot Backfill button seeds the whole service from your existing library; Simkl gets a dedicated date-accuracy repair pass (rewrites watched/rated dates instead of stamping everything 'today'). Yamtrack has no public API in released builds, so StarTrack exports an IMDb-format CSV you import via Yamtrack → Import → IMDb (marked experimental). Issue #8 part 1: the poster rating badge corner is now configurable (top-right default / top-left / bottom-right / bottom-left) so it no longer collides with Jellyfin's watched checkmark. Full 8-language i18n for all new UI. No data migration needed; existing files are unchanged.

Fixes Members tab + activity feed on Jellyfin 10.11.9+ where IUserManager.Users was removed from the interface. Also dedups the unified activity feed: rating-and-diary pairs for the same item on the same day no longer surface twice (Letterboxd RSS sync writes both — only the richest variant is shown now).

- NEW: administrators are exempt from stream limits by default ("Exempt administrators", can be turned off)

- Fixed users locked out after a stop by clients that keep their session alive (AFinity progress reports, Swiftfin without a stopped report, jellyfin-android native player): a stopped device no longer counts for up to 10 minutes
- Sessions that cannot receive the stop command are now stopped server side
- Hard block now also identifies requests using legacy token headers (X-Emby-Token, X-MediaBrowser-Token, X-Emby-Authorization, Emby scheme), ignored by Jellyfin 12 by default
- A deleted user's limit is removed from the configuration
- Jellyfin 12 build: compatible with Jellyfin 12.0 to 12.3

- Fixed plugin failing to load on Jellyfin 10.11.0-10.11.10 ("incompatible version of one of the shared libraries", issue #19): now built against Jellyfin 10.11.0 instead of the latest 10.11.x

- Fixed missing plugin logo (and 404 on disable/uninstall) on Jellyfin 12: the Jellyfin 12 DLL reported version 1.1.0.0 instead of its package version; each build now carries its own version (10.11 = 1.1.0.x, Jellyfin 12 = 1.1.1.x)
- Fixed a crashed client's ghost session getting the user's new, legitimate stream stopped (up to ~10 min lockout): the PlaybackStart limiter now uses the same fresh-check-in, per-device count as the HTTP gate
- Transcode kill no longer falls back to killing every job of the device when the client sent no PlaySessionId
- Custom web message now works on servers with a BaseUrl (the injected script used an absolute /StreamLimit path)

- NEW (BETA): HTTP-level hard block — over-limit streams are rejected before any byte is served; works on every client (Swiftfin, Infuse, external players)
- NEW (BETA): single clean custom message on web clients (replaces the built-in dialog)
- NEW: default max streams for users without an explicit limit
- NEW: config migration from pre-1.1 installs (normalizes legacy entries)
- Fixed silent failure where one invalid config entry disabled every limit (#5/#8/#18)
- Fixed device logout (a session id was passed where an access token was expected)
- Kill transcode jobs of blocked streams; optional device logout
- Admin-only stream limit API; removed Newtonsoft.Json
- Fixed duplicated users in the config page dropdown (#16) and empty popup (#6)

versions.changelog:
Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12.

Adgangsnøglen: Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende den på (X-Emby-Token). Det ramte Subtitle Guard hårdere end de andre plugins — tolv forskellige kald sendte den gamle vej, og de svarede alle 401 på Jellyfin 12. I praksis betød det at alt det der foregår fra selve siden holdt op med at virke: workers, køen, historikken, knapperne på detaljesiden. Alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt.

Indstillingssiden kunne slet ikke åbnes på Jellyfin 12. Pluginet kørte, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Det er den side hvor workers tilmeldes, så uden den kunne en ny worker ikke sættes op. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun siden, hvis den selv beder om at komme i menuen.

Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan kun installeres der. Kører du stadig 10.11, bliver du på 2.1.0.0, som virker uændret — serveren vælger selv den rigtige. Grunden til at der skal være to: 10.11 og 12 kører på hver sin udgave af .NET, så det samme build kan ikke køre begge steder.

Bemærk: selve sync-workeren er urørt. Den kører for sig selv og er ikke berørt af hvilken Jellyfin-version serveren har.

Undertekster der hører til en anden version af filmen bliver nu erstattet i stedet for at blive stående for evigt.

Baggrund: en rapporteret film (Superbad) havde undertekster der var så forkerte at man ikke kunne se om de kom for tidligt eller for sent. Filen er den uklippede udgave på 118,7 minutter, mens underteksten hører til biografudgaven og slutter 15 minutter før filmen gør. Indskudte scener fordeler sig ujævnt gennem filmen, så afvigelsen er ikke konstant - derfor kan man ikke pege på en retning.

Synkroniseringen var uskyldig. ffsubsync måler sammenhængen til -50.569 - altså negativ, modsat korreleret - og nægtede helt korrekt at røre filen. Til sammenligning gav seks afsnit med rigtige undertekster +40.205 til +177.137 og under 0,2 sekunds forskydning. Problemet var at intet i kæden så kunne redde filen: den ene reparation der virker - at transskribere lyden - var blokeret af netop den undertekst der var forkert. Filen kunne aldrig blive rigtig.

Workeren registrerer nu den slags som `subtitle-mismatch`, og en sådan undertekst tæller ikke længere som at elementet 'allerede har undertekster'. Den bliver transskriberet i stedet. Originalen gemmes som .bak inden den erstattes, hvis navnene støder sammen, så det altid kan fortrydes.

Bemærk: Whisper navngiver efter det sprog den finder (fx .en.srt), så en forkert undertekst der hedder .eng.srt bliver ikke overskrevet - den nye lægger sig ved siden af, og begge er synlige i afspilleren. Den forkerte kan slettes i hånden.

Kræver worker 2.3.0 eller nyere.

Manuelle klik (Fix undertekst-sync / Generér undertekster / Prøv igen) springer nu foran den natlige kø i stedet for at vente bag den - en natlig batch-kørsel kunne lægge hundredvis af filer foran et enkelt klik, så "Tilføjet til kø" reelt kunne betyde en lang ventetid. Bemærk: kræver genstart af Jellyfin for at tage effekt (denne del af rettelsen ligger i selve plugin'et, ikke i sync-workeren).

Selvdiagnosticerende advarsel hvis siden virker helt ustylet: en statisk boks øverst forklarer at File Transformation-pluginet formentlig mangler eller er inaktivt (det plugin der får Subtitle Guards egen kode til at køre) - synlig som ren HTML uden nogen afhængighed af JavaScript, og gemmes automatisk igen så snart pluginet faktisk kører korrekt. Ramte en ven der installerede pluginet og fik en helt ustylet side uden nogen forklaring; nu står årsagen der direkte i stedet.

Linux/Windows-vælger på 'Tilmeld ny worker': skift mellem Linux-kommandoen og den nye Windows-installer (PowerShell) - Windows GPU-maskiner (fx en gaming-pc) kan nu være workers med samme funktioner som Linux (sync, transskription, oversættelse). Workers males ikke længere 'Offline' under modelindlæsning: har workeren svaret inden for de sidste 3 minutter, vises seneste kendte status med en ⏳-note ('genstart ikke workeren') i stedet - vigtigt nu hvor workers frigiver hukommelsen efter endt arbejde og derfor genindlæser modeller ved hver natlig kørsel. Rettet: 'Seneste rettelser'-listen oversættes nu også i engelsk tilstand (den blev renderet før sprogvalget var indlæst).

Ny 'Test worker-rettigheder'-boks under Workers → Stier. Genererer en færdig kopiér-og-indsæt-kommando til check-permissions.sh, som tester ÆGTE læse/skrive/slette-rettigheder som den faktiske tjeneste-bruger på en worker (i modsætning til ls -l, der ofte lyver på netværks-mounts). Mappen udfyldes automatisk ud fra 'Inkluderede biblioteker' (med path mapping anvendt), men kan rettes til en hvilken som helst mappe. Ingen worker-opdatering nødvendig (scriptet hentes fra GitHub, når kommandoen køres).

Subtitle Guard 2.0 - feature-komplet udgave klar til at dele. NYT: engelsk UI (vælger øverst på siden - hele pluginet kan nu skifte mellem dansk og engelsk); 'Getting Started'-knap med fuld opsætningsguide (erstatter '?'); førstegangs-velkomst på Workers-fanen når ingen workers er tilmeldt; worker-version vises pr. maskine med markering af maskiner der halter efter poolen; 'Gendan originale undertekster' (alle workers gendanner ALT de har ændret, fra .bak-backupper - med er-du-sikker-bekræftelse); 'Gendan standardindstillinger'-knap (nulstiller alt undtagen worker-tilmelding, stier og sprog); Whisper-panelet forudfyldt med de anbefalede standarder. FORBEDRET: transskriptions-progressbaren animerer nu; Status-fanen opdaterer sig selv hvert minut, har fået en 'Tjek igen'-knap, og fejl forsvinder AUTOMATISK når et senere forsøg lykkes (viser nuværende tilstand, ikke historik); Pool-status-kortet er fjernet. RETTET (worker 2.0.0, ruller selv ud): 'Ryd kø' kunne miste kapløbet mod arbejdstrådene så jobs alligevel kørte - køen ryddes nu atomisk og bevarer pause-tilstanden; en pauset men ledig worker kunne stjæle nyindsendte jobs - de holdes nu i køen til der genoptages. Alt funktionelt testet mod en kørende worker-instans (21/21 checks, inkl. æøå gennem SRT-skriveren).

Indbygget opsætningsguide, CPU-transskription igen, og en Whisper-indstillings-UI. Et nyt '?' i toppen af plugin-siden åbner en fuld trin-for-trin guide til at sætte workers op - med et fremhævet afsnit om at worker-kontoen SKAL have skriverettigheder til medierne (ellers fejler alt med 'permission denied'), inkl. SERVICE_USER og gruppe-fix. CPU-workers kan nu transskribere igen: routingen er ikke længere CUDA-only, men styres af transskriptions-rollen - Workers-listen advarer om at CPU giver lavere kvalitet og anbefaler GPU. Ny sektion under Transskription: Whisper-indstillinger (model, beam size, VAD + tærskel/padding) med en forklaring til hver, som genererer en færdig kopier-og-indsæt-kommando du kører på den ønskede worker (indstillingerne sidder pr. worker, så de gemmes ikke i pluginet). Desuden en ny 'Aktivér dansk oversættelse'-kontakt, så hele oversættelsesfunktionen kan slås fra. Nye CPU-workers vælger nu selv Whisper-model ud fra kerner/RAM ved installation (small, eller medium på ≥4 kerner og ≥6 GB RAM; large-v3 er GPU-only i auto-valget, men kan stadig vælges manuelt). Selve pluginet kræver ingen worker-opdatering; auto-modelvalget gælder ved (gen)installation af en worker.

Fejl-triage, historik-forbedringer, kvalitetspas, live fremdrift, auto-oversættelse og multi-GPU. Status-fanen får et rødt triage-kort der grupperer fejl efter årsag (skriverettigheder, manglende mount, model-cache osv.) med konkrete løsningsforslag og en 'Prøv fejlede igen nu'-knap der sætter alle tre opgaver i kø. Transskriptions-historikken viser nu seneste status PR. EMNE (gamle fejl forsvinder når et nyt forsøg lykkes) og fejlede rækker får en 'Prøv igen'-knap. Whisper-output renses for hallucinationer (thanks-for-watching/subtitles-by-boilerplate og gentagelses-loops). Emne-sidens 'Generér undertekster'-knap viser nu live fremdrift ('Transskriberer... 42%' -> 'Færdig'). Ny indstilling: automatisk en->da-oversættelse i kø straks efter en vellykket engelsk transskription (til som standard). Installeren understøtter nu flere instanser pr. maskine (INSTALL_DIR/SERVICE_NAME/WORKER_PORT/GPU_INDEX), så fx en 3080 + 2060 kører som to uafhængige workers. Worker-delen ruller selv ud via auto-opdateringen.

Metadata-hotwords til Whisper. Før hver transskription bygges automatisk en kort, rangeret liste af navne og særegne termer fra emnets Jellyfin-metadata - serie-/film-/afsnitstitler, karakternavne, skuespillere, tags/collections og egennavne udtrukket lokalt fra resuméer (afsnit kombineres med serie-metadata) - og gives til faster-whisper's hotwords, så 'Chrisjen Avasarala' staves rigtigt i stedet for fonetisk gætværk. Dubletter fjernes (mest specifikke form vinder), apostroffer/bindestreger/accenter bevares, og listen er begrænset (75 termer / 800 tegn, konfigurerbart). Nye indstillinger under Transskription: aktivér (til), maks. termer/tegn, skuespillere (til), instruktører/forfattere (fra), resuméer (til), studier (fra), debug-log (fra - normalt logges kun antallet). Cachet pr. emne og ugyldiggjort ved metadata-ændringer; intet metadata forlader serveren. Worker-delen ruller selv ud via auto-opdateringen. Bemærk: hotwords er en bias, ikke en garanti - de øger sandsynligheden for korrekte stavemåder markant.

Subtitle OCR.description: Converts embedded image-based subtitle tracks (VobSub/DVD and PGS/Blu-ray) to external SRT or ASS files using nOCR pattern matching. Pure managed code: no Tesseract and no native libraries, using the ffmpeg your server already ships. The .nocr database format is interchange-compatible with Subtitle Edit, so databases trained or corrected in its GUI drop straight in. A scheduled task scans your Movie and Episode libraries and writes a subtitle file beside each image-based track. OCR text is optionally spell-checked with Hunspell and corrected with Subtitle Edit's OCR fix lists, both fetched on demand.
Subtitle OCR.overview: OCR image-based DVD and Blu-ray subtitles to SRT or ASS

versions.changelog:
Recognition is far more accurate and roughly three times faster. The bundled Latin database carries glyph shapes trained on real disc fonts, so few characters read as the unknown box. A file gives up every subtitle track in one pass rather than one pass per track, tracks recognize in parallel (Max parallelism leaves half the cores to playback), and image buffers are reused, so a run no longer drives the full garbage collections that interrupt playback. The matcher takes the best matching glyph rather than the first the database lists, reads case from the image's own x-height and cap height, splits a merged glyph pair, matches a multi-segment glyph on shape at any size, and follows the line's italic state so a stray mid-word italic reads as the run around it. Whether a track is light text on a dark outline or the reverse is read off the track itself, per track, so the Invert luma setting is gone, and word spacing is calibrated to real disc fonts.
Output keeps more of the disc. ASS carries the color the subtitles were drawn in as its style, with an override only on the lines that differ, places an off-center sign on the full alignment grid, escapes a literal brace, and rounds its timecodes; Auto picks ASS for a track that is positioned or uses more than one color. A cue never ends after the next one begins, a too-short cue is held to a 750 ms readable minimum, and a re-sent duplicate cue merges with its neighbor.
Text correction covers misread digits (a 1 between letters as l or I, a 0 as o), the two-letter words It, Is, In and If, a lowercase l after a speaker label, split contractions and quotes, punctuation spacing, a leading speaker dash, curly quotes, and padded sound-cue brackets. An accented Latin letter foreign to the track's language folds to its base ("Nothing" for "Nothińg"), keeping each language's own accents and leaving cast and character names alone. Spell-check protects names in singular and plural and runs before sentence casing, so a misread at the start of a line resolves against the dictionary instead of freezing into a name. The l-to-I fixes are English-only, so French keeps its elided articles. Language and hearing-impaired detection read a cue's words, not its markup, so close languages like Danish and Norwegian separate, and a track the database cannot really read is discarded rather than shipped.
The extraction log is its own dashboard page, with a Reprocess all button that runs the reprocess task and shows its progress, and a per-row reprocess for a single item. New settings: Fold foreign accents (on), and Aggressive OCR fixes (off) for the riskier digit twins 5/S and 8/B on a poorly scanned disc. The plugin is built against 10.11.0, the target ABI it declares, so it loads on every 10.11 server.

Output format is now selectable: SRT, ASS, or Auto, which decides per track and writes ASS only when a cue sits away from the bottom of the screen (PGS carries the position), so an ordinary track keeps the universally supported format. OCR text is spell-checked with Hunspell, protecting Title-case proper nouns and words drawn from the item's Jellyfin metadata (title, overview, series, cast and character names) so show and character names survive. Subtitle Edit OCR fix replace lists are applied when present; dictionaries and fix lists download on demand and re-download once older than a configurable age. A track with an undetermined language now has one detected from its OCR text and is named accordingly, and the track title, forced, hearing-impaired, and commentary flags appear in the file name so commentary tracks are identifiable. A hearing-impaired track is recognized from its own text when the source flags nothing, which is the norm for a remuxed disc. New OCR corrections cover misread apostrophes in contractions, mid-word capital X, V, and I, optional ellipsis folding, and bogus italic runs around single characters and punctuation. An unread glyph now costs nothing when matching a word against the dictionary, so "batt□e" resolves to "battle" and a damaged name can be restored from the item's metadata. A new "Reprocess extracted subtitles" task re-OCRs every logged file from its source with the current settings. Each file is probed with a single ffprobe pass rather than two, and only one OCR or reprocess task runs at a time.

Detect image-based subtitles by probing every Movie and Episode with ffprobe, since Jellyfin does not store PGS/VobSub streams in its metadata. A per-file cache skips files that are unchanged and were probed within a configurable window, with a force-rescan option. Word spacing now scales with subtitle line height, fixing spaces inserted between every letter on HD Blu-ray text. New options: extract only selected languages, discard a track whose dropped-event ratio is too high (removing any stale SRT), and a filename tag ({name}.{lang}.OCR.srt, shown as the subtitle title) so the plugin only ever overwrites or deletes its own output. A config-page modal lists every extracted file with a link to its movie or episode. The scheduled task now sits under its own category.

Initial production release. OCRs embedded image-based subtitles (VobSub/DVD and PGS/Blu-ray) to SRT files using nOCR pattern matching, with Subtitle Edit-compatible .nocr databases. Pure managed code: no Tesseract, no native dependencies. Optionally skips image tracks whose language already has a text subtitle.

Tracearr SSE.description: Streams playback start, progress, pause, stop, session connect and disconnect, library item added, removed, and downloaded, converted downloads, scheduled task lifecycle, and server CPU/RAM stat events as Server-Sent Events, plus a hello event carrying the plugin version. Built for Tracearr. Works with any SSE client.
Tracearr SSE.overview: Real-time playback, session, library, download, task, and server stat events over Server-Sent Events.

versions.changelog:
- `library.item.downloaded` event on Jellyfin and Emby when a user downloads an item, from the server's activity log. Payload carries `userId`, `itemId` (absent on Emby, whose entry has none), `itemName` (the activity entry's name), and `app` and `device` parsed from the entry's overview.
- On Emby, the activity entry names the user by numeric internal id, so `library.item.downloaded` looks the user up and sends the same 32-character GUID that playback events carry. `userId` is omitted when no user matches.
- `download.transcoded` event on Jellyfin for clients that download at reduced quality through the stream endpoint, which logs no activity. A device session that transcodes without reporting playback for 20 seconds emits `phase: "started"`, and `phase: "ended"` when the transcode goes away. Payload carries `userId`, `deviceId`, `itemId`, `bitrate`, `width`, `height`, `videoCodec`, `audioCodec`, `container`, `bytesTranscoded`, and `completionPercentage`. `itemId` and `bytesTranscoded` are read from Jellyfin's internal transcoding job list and are omitted if that read fails.
- The events endpoint now requires an administrator or an API key on both Jellyfin and Emby.

- Jellyfin builds now target .NET 10 against the Jellyfin 12.0 plugin ABI. Jellyfin 12 moved the server to .NET 10 and changed several plugin interfaces, so a 10.11 build does not load on it. Catalog entries carry `targetAbi` 12.0.0.0, which hides them from 10.11 servers; 0.4.1 stays the last release for 10.11.
- Emby is unaffected. `Emby.Plugin.Sse` is still netstandard2.0 and still targets Emby 4.9+.

- Emby dashboard thumbnail is the 16:9 catalog tile instead of the square Tracearr logo.
- Catalog art replaced: a 1920x1080 tile shared by the Jellyfin catalog and the Emby thumb, and an Emby terminal preview showing the wire format. The old images were Tracearr app placeholders.
- Both catalog manifests describe the full event set and carry per-version release notes; new releases pull them from this changelog.
Adds server.stats CPU/RAM samples every 6 seconds while a client is connected, and task.started, task.progress, and task.completed events from the scheduled task manager.
Adds library.item.added and library.item.removed events carrying itemId, itemType, and parentId.
Adds the hello event on connect, disconnects subscribers whose buffer fills so they reconnect and resync, raises the per-subscriber buffer to 512, and makes release builds report their real version.
First release: playing, progress, paused, stopped, session.start, and session.end events plus a ping keepalive every 30 seconds.

Transcode Downloader.description: Adds a quality-selection download button to Jellyfin item detail pages.
Transcode Downloader.overview: Adds a 'Download (Transcode…)' entry to the More menu on every movie and episode detail page. Selecting it opens a quality picker — choose a bitrate tier and Jellyfin re-encodes the video server-side to H.264/AAC, streaming it to your browser with a live progress bar, or pick Original to save the unmodified source file directly. Requires the File Transformation companion plugin (>= v2.2.1.0) for permission-safe script injection.

fix: transcoding actually respects selected quality tier.

versions.changelog:
## Fixed
- Session cleanup logs now name the user whose device was logged out, instead of showing their user ID.

## Fixed
- Users created by an administrator now get all of the default group's restrictions, not just its membership and password rules.

## Developer
- Built for Jellyfin 12.2 (target ABI 12.2.0.0). Servers on Jellyfin 12.0 or 12.1 keep the previous release.
- Updated test dependencies (Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.11, NSubstitute 6.2, xunit 2.9.3, xunit.runner.visualstudio 4.0.1).

## Security
- Accounts created through an invite get only the invite's group, rather than also keeping settings and password rule enrollment from the default group
- Invite signups and lookups are limited per network address (per /64 block for IPv6), counting failed attempts as well as successful ones; the server warns once when invites arrive through a reverse proxy that is not in Known proxies
- If an invite signup fails partway, the half-created account is removed instead of being left on the server's default permissions, so the invitee can try again
- A new invited account cannot be signed in to until its password has been set
- Each invite now defaults to 10 signups per hour; servers whose saved plugin settings already include an invite rate limit keep it

## Fixed
- Invites into a group that has expired are refused with a clear message, and the Invites tab warns about them
- Invite usage and PIN counters no longer overwrite a lockout reset or invite deletion made at the same time from the dashboard
- Invite status is kept in memory instead of being read from disk on every invite page load
- Administrators and deleted users are cleaned out of group membership on every save, including saves made right after the server starts
- The plugin's category and description are now the same in the catalog and on the server

## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.19.

## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Features
- Groups can now manage whether members may change their own display and playback preferences
- Groups can now manage the sync transcoding and public sharing permissions
- Groups can now manage whether a Collections view is shown on the home screen

## Fixes
- A deleted user is dropped from group membership and enrollment records the moment the server deletes them, rather than on the next save or sync

## Developer
- Remove the unused HasPassword override. Jellyfin 12 dropped it from IAuthenticationProvider and performs that check itself, so the method was dead code the server never called

## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

## Features
- Invites can target the default group instead of a fixed one
- The invite group list marks which group is the default
- Group expiry and inactivity disabling now write activity log warnings

## Fixes
- A member promoted to administrator is reverted to their original authentication provider
- Administrators are dropped from group member lists on save
- Users deleted from Jellyfin no longer linger in groups or enrollment records
- A new user could land in no group when a save ran at the same moment
- The Inactive card counts each member against their own group's window
- Invite usage counters no longer race with deleting or re-enabling an invite
- A configuration save no longer discards a concurrent membership write
- Select fields no longer render overlapping dropdown arrows

## Developer
- Bump Base to 2026.7.31

## Features
- Groups can log out member devices that have not checked in within a set number of days
- Cleanup rules target all clients, only selected clients, or all except selected clients
- Overlapping rules resolve to the shortest window
- New Clean Expired Sessions scheduled task

## Developer
- Bump Base to 2026.7.12
- Use ActivityLogger from Base 2026.7.12
- Standardize activity log messages

versions.changelog:
This update brings together 2.0.12.0 and 2.0.13.0 from the beta channel.

If you use Dispatcharr Mode: the first sync after updating re-reads every series once, so it takes longer than usual. This corrects series episodes that failed to play with a 404 from Dispatcharr, and in some setups a series that showed another series' episodes. Files keep their names, so watched status is kept.

If you posted a Jellyfin log from an earlier version somewhere public: it may contain your provider username and password, which were in the stream address logged each time a channel was opened and in provider errors and retries. Consider asking your provider for a new password. The log no longer contains them.

Fixed: with Enable Native Tuner on, Live TV did not show up until you added an "Xtream Library" tuner by hand under Dashboard > Live TV > Tuner Devices. The plugin now adds that entry itself, as "Xtream Library (added by the plugin)", when Enable Live TV and Enable Native Tuner are both on, and removes it when you turn either off. A tuner you added by hand is kept and no second one is added.

Fixed: with Live TV through an M3U tuner and Epg.xml as the guide, channels whose name starts with a number, such as "24 Kitchen" or "3sat", got no guide. This shows after the next guide refresh.

Fixed: when the provider could not deliver a series during a sync, orphan cleanup deleted that series' files. They are now kept until the provider answers again.

Fixed: errors from LiveTv.m3u, Catchup.m3u and Epg.xml (for example "Live TV is not enabled") arrived as an empty "406 Not Acceptable". They now come with their real status and message.

This update brings together 2.0.10.0 and 2.0.11.0 from the beta channel.

If you use the Live TV allow-list behind a reverse proxy: add the proxy to Known Proxies in Jellyfin's networking settings. Without that, every request through the proxy counts as coming from the proxy, and if its address is on your list, everyone gets in. The help text now says so.

Fixed: with Live TV set up on two or more providers, the guide never used your providers' XMLTV files. They were combined into one file that could not be read past the first provider, so the guide always fell back to the simpler per-channel listings and lost categories, ratings and the other details XMLTV carries. Each provider's file is now read on its own. If one provider's file is missing or broken, only that provider's channels fall back, and the others keep their full guide (found and fixed by dillardblom).

Fixed: when two providers used the same guide id for different channels, one of them got no guide, or showed the other provider's programmes. Guide ids are now matched per provider (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: when your provider's XMLTV guide came through cut off part way, building the guide never finished. Each request for the EPG URL kept one CPU core busy until Jellyfin gave up, and the guide stayed empty. A broken file now falls back to fetching the guide per channel, as it already did when the file was missing, and no programme is listed twice (by dillardblom).

Fixed: with Dispatcharr mode on, every sync worker logged in to Dispatcharr at the same time when a sync started. Dispatcharr's login limit refused most of them, and those workers fell back to the Xtream API for the first minutes. There is now one login shared by all of them, and it waits its turn like every other request (reported by dillardblom).

This update brings together 2.0.2.0 to 2.0.9.0 from the beta channel.

If you use Live TV with the Native Tuner only, open the Live TV tab after updating and turn off the new "Publish Playlists" switch. It stays on for anyone who already had Live TV enabled, so an M3U tuner or TiviMate setup keeps working, but the native tuner does not need it.

Fixed: Request Delay now limits how fast the plugin talks to your provider in total. Each parallel worker used to apply it separately, so with Sync Parallelism at 10 and the default of 50 ms up to 200 requests a second could go out, enough for some providers to block your IP. It is now one shared gap per provider: 50 ms means at most 20 a second. When the provider says it is getting too many requests, every request to it waits. A first sync of a large library takes longer as a result; if your provider allows more, lower Request Delay. Setting it to 0 is no longer saved as 50 (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: a single unreadable value from your provider, such as an empty value where a number belongs, no longer makes content disappear. It could blank a series' title, plot and TMDB id, drop every episode of a series, or make a whole category fail to sync. Such values are now ignored or read as 0, and an item whose ID cannot be read is skipped with a warning while the rest syncs normally (reported by foXaCe).

Fixed: changing Folder Mode, or moving a category to another folder, no longer leaves every moved item in your library twice. The old copies are removed even beyond the orphan safety limit, as long as the item only moved to another category folder; anything that actually disappeared is still protected by the limit. Moved items lose their watched status, because Jellyfin sees a new folder as a new item (reported in andreadegiovine's fork).

Fixed: when orphan cleanup removes a movie or series, the NFO and poster the plugin wrote are removed with it, so the folder no longer stays behind. Files you added yourself, such as subtitles or your own NFO, are kept, and so is the folder (idea from andreadegiovine).

Fixed: with "Group movies with the same TMDB id" on, a film whose request the provider missed no longer ends up in a folder of its own. It is held back and picked up on the next sync. Films already split this way stay split; to fix them, use Delete Movies Library in the Danger Zone and sync again (reported by andreadegiovine).

New: with "Fallback to Year-Free Lookup" on, an unmatched movie is also searched with the year of the provider's release date and with its original title, which helps when the title carries the wrong year or is in another language. A search without a year is checked against the release date, so it cannot pick a remake. A match found by the year-free retry is now remembered for later syncs, for movies and series. Movies already in your library keep their folders (idea from philx17).

New: "Publish Playlists" on the Live TV tab. The M3U and Catch-up M3U URLs contain your Xtream username and password and can be reached without a Jellyfin login. They are now only served while this switch is on, and it is off when you enable Live TV from now on. The EPG URL and channel logos are not affected (proposed by dillardblom).

New: "Restrict These URLs To" limits the Live TV URLs to the addresses you list, one per line. Leave it empty for no restriction. If you use it, include 127.0.0.1 and ::1, since Jellyfin fetches channel logos itself, and behind a reverse proxy add the proxy to Known Proxies in Jellyfin's networking settings first (written by dillardblom).

Fixed: a Live TV category, channel or logo address with & in it no longer shows as & or breaks (reported by TheBazeman).

Categories load their items again on Jellyfin 12 (#117).

Jellyfin 12 stops accepting the legacy `X-Emby-Token` request header. Two of the configuration page fetch sites still sent it: the Live TV category loader and the Series / VOD content loader. Both now send `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=` instead, which Jellyfin 12's `CustomAuthentication` middleware expects. The Test connection button was never affected and still works as before. Two-line header swap in `config.js`, no server-side change.

This update brings together 1.55.1.0 to 1.55.3.0 from the beta channel.

Fixed: Request Delay now limits how fast the plugin talks to your provider in total. Each parallel worker used to apply it separately, so with Sync Parallelism at 10 and the default of 50 ms up to 200 requests a second could go out, enough for some providers to block your IP. It is now one shared gap per provider: 50 ms means at most 20 a second. When the provider says it is getting too many requests, every request to it waits. A first sync of a large library takes longer as a result; if your provider allows more, lower Request Delay. Setting it to 0 is no longer saved as 50 (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: with "Group movies with the same TMDB id" on, a film whose request the provider missed no longer ends up in a folder of its own. It is held back and picked up on the next sync. Films already split this way stay split; to fix them, use Delete Movies Library in the Danger Zone and sync again (reported by andreadegiovine).

Fixed: a Live TV category, channel or logo address with & in it no longer shows as & or breaks (reported by TheBazeman).

Test Dispatcharr now tests the password you just typed.

Typing a Dispatcharr API password and pressing Test before saving tested the password that was already saved, not the one on screen. It came back red with "authentication failed" for credentials that were perfectly correct, and nothing suggested that saving first would change the answer. Type, test, save once it goes green is the obvious way to use a test button, and that order never worked.

It now sends what is on the form, the way the Test Connection button above it always has. Clearing the Dispatcharr URL and pressing Test now tests the Xtream address, which is what leaving that field empty means, instead of quietly putting the old URL back.

A provider you are setting up for the first time can be tested as well. Before, with nothing saved yet, it answered "Please configure Base URL first" about a Base URL sitting on screen in front of you.

Nothing else changed, and catch-up, syncing and Live TV are untouched.

The last of your provider password is out of the Live TV playlist.

1.53 replaced every stream URL in LiveTv.m3u and Catchup.m3u with a Dispatcharr address that needs no credentials. One thing still carried the password: the catch-up attribute on channels that have an archive. That attribute is a template your IPTV app fills in and plays by itself, so it has to work on its own, and the only address that does is the one with your username and password in it. Dispatcharr has a catch-up address of its own, but it refuses callers who have not logged in, and these playlists are deliberately served without a Jellyfin login so that Jellyfin's own tuner can read them. There was nothing safe to put there, so the attribute is now left out.

What this changes for you: nothing, if you watch catch-up in Jellyfin. Those channels still have their archive and still play the same way. If you point an external IPTV app at these playlists, that app will no longer offer catch-up on those channels. If you would rather have it back, there is a new setting under Catch-up / Timeshift that puts the attribute in again, with the warning that it carries your password.

Measured on a live setup before and after: 720 channels, 63 lines with the password in them, now none.

Also fixed: the line in the log that tells you how much of the playlist still carries credentials only appeared on the rare occasions the plugin fetched the channel list fresh. It now appears whenever a playlist is built, which is when you would actually go looking for it.

Your provider password is no longer in the Live TV playlist.

If you run Dispatcharr in front of your provider, the M3U the plugin serves now points at Dispatcharr's own channel addresses instead of building URLs with your Xtream username and password in them. Those URLs have always been reachable without a Jellyfin login, on purpose, because Jellyfin's own tuner cannot send one, which meant anyone who had one of those links also had your provider account. Measured on a real setup: 720 of 720 channels, every stream address credential free, where before every single line carried the password.

A channel Dispatcharr does not recognise keeps its old address rather than disappearing from your guide, and the log says how many did and that those lines still carry credentials. Without Dispatcharr nothing changes at all.

One part is not done yet. Channels with a catch-up archive carry a separate address for replaying past programmes, and that one is a template other apps fill in themselves, so it still has your credentials in it. On the setup this was measured against that is 63 lines out of 720. Finishing it needs checking how Dispatcharr expects a time to be expressed, which has not been verified, so it was left rather than guessed at.

Also fixed: with Dispatcharr on a different address than your provider, movie links were pointed at the wrong one of the two.

Channels that would not direct play, and quicker metadata behind Dispatcharr.

Fixed: if your provider does not send stream statistics, every channel arrived at your player with nothing to say what it actually was. Players refused them as an unsupported format, and the server re-encoded pictures they could have shown as they were, without graphics acceleration because it did not know what it was decoding either. Jellyfin can work this out by looking at the stream, and the plugin was accidentally stopping it from looking. Channels from providers that do send statistics are unchanged. One trade-off worth knowing: if the inspection fails, Jellyfin now assumes the picture is interlaced and smooths it, which is slower than before, where the plugin simply asserted it was not (diagnosed by pemontto).

Changed: with Dispatcharr Mode on, film and series descriptions, cast, ratings and artwork now come from Dispatcharr directly instead of going the long way round through its Xtream compatibility layer. Series episodes had no Dispatcharr route at all until now. Anything that does not answer falls back to the old route, so a Dispatcharr too old to have these endpoints keeps working exactly as before, and with Dispatcharr Mode off nothing changes at all (contributed by dillardblom).

Radio channels, and a plainer warning about the Live TV setup URLs.

Fixed: radio stations were published as ordinary television channels. Providers mark them with a stream type that the plugin read and then ignored, so they ended up in the TV list with everything else. The playlist now flags them as radio, which is what players like Kodi use to put them under Radio, and the built-in tuner reports them as radio to Jellyfin, which keeps radio in its own section. Only the one value that is known to mean radio counts: providers use that same field for their own bookkeeping, and guessing would move real television channels out of the TV list, which is harder to recover from than a radio station in the wrong place. If you run Dispatcharr in front of the plugin you will not see a difference, because it reports every channel as ordinary live TV (reported by dillardblom).

The three setup URLs on the Live TV tab now say what they are. They work without a Jellyfin login, on purpose, because Jellyfin's own tuner and guide fetcher do not send one when they fetch them. What was never spelled out is what that means: Xtream has no token or session, so your provider username and password sit in every stream line of the playlist, and anyone who can reach one of those URLs has your account. The settings page, the README and the developer notes now all say so, along with the two things that limit it: keeping those URLs off the open internet, and using the built-in tuner, which never publishes a playlist at all (raised by dillardblom).

## Developer
- Still built for Jellyfin 12.2 (target ABI 12.2.0.0, unchanged).
- Updated test dependencies (Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.11, NSubstitute 6.2, xunit 2.9.3, xunit.runner.visualstudio 4.0.1).
- Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.Core is now compiled against 10.0.11, the version Jellyfin 12.2 ships. It is not bundled, so nothing changes at runtime.
- No user-facing changes in this release; the plugin works the same as 12.2.3.4.

## Security
- yt-dlp and Deno downloads are checked against the SHA-256 checksums their releases publish, and a file that does not match is deleted instead of run.
- YouTube links containing spaces, quotes or other characters that could add extra arguments to yt-dlp are refused, and only the cleaned-up link is passed to yt-dlp.
- Approved users can queue at most 200 videos from one playlist link by default; change the limit under Settings > Approved Users.

## Fixed
- Importing a different song with the same title as one already on the album, such as a second "Interlude" with its own track number, no longer overwrites it; it is saved as "Title (2)".
- Downloads can be cancelled from the Download tab, which also lets Update yt-dlp run without waiting for a large playlist to finish.
- Failed and cancelled downloads no longer leave partial files in the cache, and leftovers are cleaned up when the server starts.
- Reset Queue now deletes the cached files of the items it removes, and both resets stop running downloads first.
- Deno is now kept up to date along with yt-dlp, on the same schedule and with the Update yt-dlp button.
- Repairing a downloaded file with ffmpeg can no longer hang.
- On Alpine and other musl-based systems the plugin downloads the musl build of yt-dlp, which runs there.
- A yt-dlp or Deno copy that cannot start no longer makes every download fail; the update check logs it and carries on.
- A damaged song in an album folder no longer stops other songs from being imported into it.

## Developer
- The publish workflow passes the release notes to the shell through environment variables.
- The test project uses SQLitePCLRaw 2.1.13, which fixes a known SQLite vulnerability.
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.19.

## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Features
- Replace a library song's audio with a different YouTube upload from the Download tab; it keeps the song's file, tags, cover and playlist places.
- Choosing an album already in the library on the Import tab takes that album's cover.
- Imports join existing artist and album folders whose names differ only in case, punctuation or year, and take that album's name and year.

## Features
- Republishes 12.2.3.0, whose download did not match its checksum and could not install.

## Features
- Import Spotify playlists exported with Exportify, one playlist as CSV or all of them as a ZIP.
- Spotify imports embed Spotify's album cover and fill in the genre from Apple Music.
- Playlist tracks with an ISRC are matched to their official YouTube upload by it first.
- Generate a cover with the wand button on the Import tab; choose its text, order and colors in Settings → Album Art.
- Composer credits are stored as separate composers.
- Live, remix, cover, acoustic and instrumental versions are never matched unless the song's title names that version.

## Features
- When Apple Music has no cover, the album cover from the official YouTube Music track is used.
- Re-pitched, sped-up, 8D and nightcore uploads are never matched.
- Artists YouTube Music credits in another alphabet (such as Cyrillic) are matched by album or exact length.
- Re-importing a playlist removes queued or failed songs your library now has.

## Features
- YouTube matches must contain the song title, so another song by the same artist with a similar length is never downloaded instead.
- Importing rescans only the imported songs' folders instead of the whole library.

## Features
- Look up each download on Apple Music to fill in its title, album, album artist, year, track number and genre (Settings, on by default).
- Embed the album cover from Apple Music in downloaded files (Settings, on by default).
- Upload your own cover art on the Import tab, for one file or all selected files.
- Songs already in your library are marked Already in your library on the Import tab.
- Joint artist credits are stored as separate artists, and new imports reuse the library's spelling of an artist.
- Playlist imports use the album's release date for its year.
- Playlist tracks the regular YouTube search cannot match are looked up in YouTube Music's song results.

## Features
- Change the YouTube link of any queued track from its queue row, keeping its details and playlist.
- Better matching for classical tracks, and uploads by other performers are no longer picked.
- Classical tracks already in your library are recognized even when tagged with only the movement name (or only the full work title), so they are not downloaded again.

- Reduced unnecessary CPU and disk activity during library refreshes.
- Fixed selected voice tracks changing after a library scan.
- Fixed episodes ending a few seconds early when playback switches to a backup source.
- Fixed cleanup of releases removed from your YummyAnime list when automatic removal is enabled.
- Improved borrowed intro and outro timings by comparing available voice tracks. Existing fallback behavior is preserved when timings disagree.

Requires Jellyfin 12.

- Your selected voice track stays selected when moving to the next episode, including choices made through Jellyfin's standard version selector.
- On slow connections, the player buffers video ahead of playback and shows buffering progress.
- Improved playback recovery after temporary loading failures.
- Reduced unnecessary load during library refreshes.
- Fixed issues with episode information and available voice tracks.

Requires Jellyfin 12.
